status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The formation pathways of massive early-type galaxies remain an active and unresolved research area. While substantial progress has been made (e.g., identification of compact massive quiescent galaxies at z~2, evidence for size growth via minor mergers, and recognition of cold accretion and secular processes alongside mergers), a single, fully consistent quantitative scenario reconciling all observational constraints is not established. The question is therefore considered open.

Let q be an odd prime power with q ≡ 2 (mod 3), and let K = F_{q^2} denote the finite field with q^2 elements. Consider the function field F = K(x, y) defined by the affine relation
    y^{(q+1)/3} + x^{(q+1)/3} + 1 = 0.
Choose an element w ∈ F_{q^2} satisfying w^{(q+1)/3} = 3, set u = w·x·y, and let z be a root of T^3 − u in an algebraic closure of F. Define the cubic Kummer extension
    F̄ = F(z),    where z^3 = w·x·y.
It is known that F̄ is an F_{q^2}-maximal function field (i.e. attains the Hasse–Weil upper bound for the number of rational places), of genus g(F̄) = (q^2 − q + 4)/6, and that the Frobenius dimension of F̄ (the dimension over F_{q^2} of the F_{q^2}-vector space of regular differentials annihilated by the Cartier operator) equals 3.

Independently, there is a family of F_{q^2}-maximal function fields of the same genus (q^2 − q + 4)/6 and the same Frobenius dimension 3 that arises as a Galois subfield of the Hermitian function field over F_{q^2} via a degree-3 quotient construction (the Cossidente–Korchmáros–Torres-type subfield).

Question: Is F̄ isomorphic, as a function field over F_{q^2}, to a member of this earlier family of F_{q^2}-maximal function fields of genus (q^2 − q + 4)/6 and Frobenius dimension 3?

Question: Is F̄ isomorphic, as a function field over F_{q^2}, to a member of this earlier family of F_{q^2}-maximal function fields of genus (q^2 − q + 4)/6 and Frobenius dimension 3?

Define the following classes of finitely presented groups:

- K_0: the class of fundamental groups of complements of 0-spheres in S^2 (equivalently, the class consisting of the infinite cyclic group ℤ).
- K_1: the class of fundamental groups of complements of (tame) 1-spheres in S^3 (classical knot groups).
- K_2: the class of fundamental groups of complements of (locally flat) 2-spheres in S^4 (2-knot groups).
- K_3: the class of fundamental groups of complements of (locally flat) 3-spheres in S^5; equivalently, by Kervaire's characterization, the class of finitely presented groups G with H_1(G) ≅ ℤ, H_2(G) = 0, and such that some element t ∈ G normally generates G.
- S: the class of fundamental groups of complements of orientable closed surfaces (locally flatly embedded) in S^4.
- M: the class of fundamental groups of complements of locally flat 2-spheres in simply connected closed 4-manifolds; equivalently, the class of finitely presented groups G such that some single element t ∈ G normally generates G.
- G: the class of all finitely presented groups.

These satisfy K_0 ⊊ K_1 ⊊ K_2 ⊊ K_3 ⊊ S ⊊ M ⊊ G.

It is known that whenever A and B are members of {K_0, K_1, K_2, K_3, S, M, G} with B ⊊ A and K_3 ⊆ A, there is no algorithm that, given a finite presentation of a group known to lie in A, decides whether that group lies in B.

Question: Does the same statement hold when A = K_2? That is, for every B ∈ {K_0, K_1} (so that B ⊊ K_2), is it the case that there is no algorithm which, given a finite presentation of a 2-knot group G ∈ K_2, decides whether or not G ∈ B?

(It is known that this conclusion would follow if there exists a group in K_2 with unsolvable word problem.)

Observations indicate that early-type galaxies (ETGs) at redshift z > 1 are structurally compact, with effective radii R_e ≲ 1 kpc — a factor of about 2–3 smaller than ETGs of comparable stellar mass at z ≈ 0 — implying stellar mass surface densities up to about 10 times and stellar volume densities up to about 30 times those of present-day ETGs. Local ETGs satisfy the Kormendy relation, an empirical correlation between effective radius R_e and mean surface brightness ⟨μ_e⟩ within R_e of the form ⟨μ_e⟩ = α + β log R_e. Simple passive luminosity-evolution models cannot reconcile the high-z compact ETGs with the local Kormendy relation, so these "superdense" ETGs must somehow grow in size between z > 1 and z ≈ 0.

Provide a quantitative physical explanation that accounts for: (i) the origin of the small effective radii of ETGs at z > 1 with the densities stated above; (ii) the mechanism(s) (e.g., dissipationless minor merging, AGN/stellar-feedback-driven adiabatic expansion, progenitor bias, or other processes) by which an individual superdense ETG, or the population as a whole, can increase R_e by the required factor of 2–3 (and reduce surface/volume densities by the corresponding factors) so as to lie on the local Kormendy relation by z ≈ 0; and (iii) an assessment of whether the inferred high-z compactness is genuine or could instead be partly an artifact of observational biases such as cosmological surface-brightness dimming (∝ (1+z)^4) and finite signal-to-noise effects on the recovery of extended low-surface-brightness wings in Sérsic-profile fits.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Subsequent work has substantially advanced understanding of this question. The compactness of high-z ETGs has been confirmed to be largely real (not solely an observational artifact) by deeper imaging and JWST observations, and dry minor mergers plus progenitor bias (newly quenched, larger ETGs entering the population at later times) are now widely accepted as the dominant drivers of mean size growth, supported by simulations and observations. However, the relative contributions of these mechanisms, the survival of compact relics in clusters, and quantitative reconciliation of size–mass evolution remain actively debated, so the problem is partially solved rather than fully resolved.

An n-knot is a smooth (or piecewise-linear locally flat) embedding of the n-sphere $S^n$ into the (n+2)-sphere $S^{n+2}$. The group of an n-knot $K \subset S^{n+2}$ is the fundamental group $\pi_1(S^{n+2} \setminus K)$. Let $K_n$ denote the class of all groups (up to isomorphism) that arise as the group of some n-knot. Each group in $K_n$ is finitely presentable.

The isomorphism problem for a class $\mathcal{C}$ of finitely presentable groups asks whether there exists an algorithm that, given two finite presentations $\langle X_1 \mid R_1 \rangle$ and $\langle X_2 \mid R_2 \rangle$, each known to present a group in $\mathcal{C}$, decides whether the two presented groups are isomorphic.

Question: Is the isomorphism problem for the class $K_2$ of 2-knot groups algorithmically unsolvable? Equivalently, prove or disprove that no Turing machine takes as input two finite presentations of groups known to lie in $K_2$ and always correctly decides whether they present isomorphic groups.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The isomorphism problem for 3-knot groups (and larger classes containing K_3) is known to be algorithmically unsolvable, since every finitely presentable group embeds in a 3-knot group, yielding 3-knot groups with unsolvable word problem. For 2-knot groups, however, unsolvability is only conjectural; it would follow if a 2-knot group with unsolvable word problem were exhibited, but no such example is currently known. The status appears to remain open as of the latest available sources.

Consider candidate early-type galaxies (ETGs) — galaxies whose observed broad-band spectral energy distributions (SEDs) are consistent with old, passively evolving stellar populations — identified at photometric redshift z > 3. Because spectroscopy at such redshifts has historically been infeasible for these faint objects, identifications rely on photometric redshifts and SED-fitting, which suffers a known degeneracy: a heavily dust-enshrouded starburst can mimic the SED of an old, passive system. A small subset of candidates at z ≈ 4–5 nevertheless appears formally consistent with massive galaxies (stellar mass M⋆ ≈ 10^11 M⊙) having low dust extinction and ages near the maximum allowed by the age of the Universe at that redshift.

Determine, via spectroscopic confirmation, the true nature of the population of ETG candidates at z > 3: specifically, what fraction of these candidates are genuinely old, passive, massive galaxies, and what fraction are dust-obscured star-forming galaxies whose SEDs imitate passive systems? In particular, confirm or refute the existence of bona fide massive (M⋆ ≈ 10^11 M⊙), low-extinction, maximally old quiescent galaxies at z ≈ 4–5.

A 2-knot is a smooth (or locally flat topological) embedding of the 2-sphere $S^2$ into the 4-sphere $S^4$. The group of a 2-knot $K \subset S^4$ is the fundamental group $\pi_1(S^4 \setminus K)$ of its complement. A finitely presented group $G = \langle x_1,\ldots,x_n \mid r_1,\ldots,r_m \rangle$ is said to have solvable word problem if there exists an algorithm that, given any word $w$ in the generators $x_1^{\pm 1},\ldots,x_n^{\pm 1}$, decides whether $w$ represents the identity element of $G$; otherwise the word problem is unsolvable.

Question: Does there exist a 2-knot $K \subset S^4$ whose group $\pi_1(S^4 \setminus K)$ has unsolvable word problem?

Consider the population of compact, superdense early-type galaxies (quiescent, spheroid-dominated galaxies with stellar masses M* ≳ 10^11 M☉ and effective radii substantially smaller than those of local early-type galaxies of comparable mass) observed at redshifts 1 < z < 2. Their characteristic effective radii are observed to grow by roughly a factor of several between z ≈ 2 and z ≈ 0 while their stellar masses change comparatively little. A candidate mechanism for this size growth is major dissipationless ("dry") merging, i.e. mergers of mass ratio close to 1:1 between gas-poor stellar systems, in which the remnant's effective radius scales approximately linearly with the total stellar mass.

Determine whether major dry merging alone can quantitatively account for the observed size evolution of these compact early-type galaxies between z ≈ 2 and z ≈ 0, subject to two empirical constraints:
(i) the small-scale (sub-Mpc) two-point clustering amplitude of low-redshift (z ≲ 0.2) early-type galaxies, which limits the close-pair frequency and hence the allowed major-merger rate;
(ii) the weak evolution of the high-mass end (M* ≳ 10^11 M☉) of the early-type galaxy stellar mass function over 0 < z < 0.7, which limits the net mass build-up by major mergers.

If major dry merging is insufficient under these constraints, determine the relative contribution required from alternative size-growth channels, in particular smooth accretion of stellar envelopes onto the central galaxy and frequent minor (mass ratio ≪ 1) dry mergers, for which the effective radius grows approximately as the square of the mass increase, in order to reproduce simultaneously the size evolution, the clustering, and the mass-function constraints.

Consider the population of compact, superdense early-type galaxies (quiescent, spheroid-dominated galaxies with stellar masses M* ≳ 10^11 M☉ and effective radii substantially smaller than those of local early-type galaxies of comparable mass) observed at redshifts 1 < z < 2. Their characteristic effective radii are observed to grow by roughly a factor of several between z ≈ 2 and z ≈ 0 while their stellar masses change comparatively little. A candidate mechanism for this size growth is major dissipationless ("dry") merging, i.e. mergers of mass ratio close to 1:1 between gas-poor stellar systems, in which the remnant's effective radius scales approximately linearly with the total stellar mass.

Determine whether major dry merging alone can quantitatively account for the observed size evolution of these compact early-type galaxies between z ≈ 2 and z ≈ 0, subject to two empirical constraints:
(i) the small-scale (sub-Mpc) two-point clustering amplitude of low-redshift (z ≲ 0.2) early-type galaxies, which limits the close-pair frequency and hence the allowed major-merger rate;
(ii) the weak evolution of the high-mass end (M* ≳ 10^11 M☉) of the early-type galaxy stellar mass function over 0 < z < 0.7, which limits the net mass build-up by major mergers.

If major dry merging is insufficient under these constraints, determine the relative contribution required from alternative size-growth channels, in particular smooth accretion of stellar envelopes onto the central galaxy and frequent minor (mass ratio ≪ 1) dry mergers, for which the effective radius grows approximately as the square of the mass increase, in order to reproduce simultaneously the size evolution, the clustering, and the mass-function constraints.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Subsequent work has converged toward the view that major dry merging alone cannot account for the observed factor-of-several size growth of compact massive early-type galaxies from z~2 to z~0 while remaining consistent with low-z clustering and the near-constancy of the high-mass end of the stellar mass function. N-body and semi-analytic studies (e.g., Nipoti et al. 2009, 2012; Oser et al.; Newman et al.) find that frequent minor dry mergers and smooth stellar envelope accretion ("two-phase" assembly) provide more efficient size growth (Δr/r scales roughly as the square of the mass increase) and can plausibly reproduce the observations, though quantitative tensions remain about whether the predicted minor-merger rates are sufficient. The problem is therefore not fully closed but a partial consensus favors a dominant role for minor mergers/accretion over major dry merging.

A 2-knot is a smooth (or locally flat topological) embedding $K \colon S^2 \hookrightarrow S^4$ of the 2-sphere into the 4-sphere. The group of a 2-knot $K$ is $\pi_1(S^4 \setminus K(S^2))$. Let $\mathcal{K}_2$ denote the class of all groups that arise as the group of some 2-knot.

Question: Does every finitely presented group embed (as a subgroup) into some group in $\mathcal{K}_2$? Equivalently, given an arbitrary finitely presented group $G$, must there exist a 2-knot $K \subset S^4$ such that $G$ is isomorphic to a subgroup of $\pi_1(S^4 \setminus K(S^2))$?

The question is posed as a conjecture (with expected answer "yes") in Hillman's monograph on 2-knots. Web searches did not surface a published proof or disproof; the problem appears to remain open. Known results show that 2-knot groups satisfy various restrictive conditions (e.g., deficiency, weight, ends), but a universal embedding theorem encompassing all finitely presented groups has not been established.

representations.normalized:
Let an early-type galaxy (ETG) be a galaxy whose stellar population is dominated by old stars and whose morphology and spectral energy distribution are consistent with elliptical or lenticular (E/S0) classification. For a galaxy population at redshift z, define:

- the rest-frame luminosity function Φ_L(L, z) dL as the comoving number density of galaxies with luminosity in (L, L+dL) in a chosen rest-frame band, and
- the stellar mass function Φ_M(M_*, z) dM_* as the comoving number density of galaxies with stellar mass in (M_*, M_* + dM_*).

Determine Φ_L(L, z) and Φ_M(M_*, z) for the population of ETGs in the redshift interval 1 < z < 3, with particular attention to the high-mass / high-luminosity end (massive ETGs) where the bulk of the assembly of this population is expected to occur. The problem is to derive these functions in a manner that is statistically robust against the cosmic variance induced by the strong spatial clustering of massive ETGs at these redshifts, specifying:

(a) the survey area, depth, and photometric/spectroscopic selection requirements (e.g. near-infrared selection criteria such as pBzK or analogous color cuts) sufficient to control sampling fluctuations at the high-mass end;
(b) the resulting comoving number density of massive ETGs as a function of redshift in 1 < z < 3, and its ratio to the corresponding z = 0 number density;
(c) the inferred evolution of the characteristic luminosity L_*(z), characteristic mass M_*(z), faint-end slope α(z), and normalization φ_*(z) of Schechter-like fits to Φ_L and Φ_M over 1 < z < 3.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Subsequent wide-field and deep surveys (e.g. COSMOS2020, COSMOS-Web with JWST, miniJPAS) have substantially advanced measurements of galaxy stellar mass and luminosity functions, including the quiescent/early-type subpopulation, out to z ~ 7. These studies place constraints on the shape, normalization, and evolution of Φ_M and Φ_L at 1 < z < 3 with reduced cosmic variance, but residual uncertainties from clustering, sample selection (color vs. morphology), and stellar-mass systematics persist, so the problem is best characterized as partially solved rather than fully closed.

For each fixed non-negative integer $g$, decide whether there exists an algorithm which, given a finite combinatorial description of a locally flat PL-embedded closed orientable surface $\Sigma \subset S^4$ of genus $g$, terminates and correctly outputs whether $\Sigma$ is unknotted.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

No general decision algorithm for recognizing unknotted locally flat PL-embedded surfaces of arbitrary genus $g$ in $S^4$ appears in the literature. Recent work establishes topological unknottedness in specific low-genus (especially nonorientable) cases via case-by-case computational obstructions, but these do not constitute a uniform algorithm, and the recognition problem for surface-knots in $S^4$ remains open.

representations.normalized:
Consider the multi-server first-come-first-served (FCFS) queue G/G/m with m ≥ 1 servers. Let {(σ_n, t_n) : n ∈ ℤ} be a two-dimensional stationary ergodic sequence on some probability space, where σ_n ≥ 0 is the service time of the n-th customer and t_n > 0 is the interarrival time between the n-th and (n+1)-st customers. Assume the stability condition E σ_1 < m · E t_1, and that customers are assigned to servers under the FCFS discipline.

Let W_n = (W_n^{(1)}, …, W_n^{(m)}) ∈ ℝ_+^m denote the Kiefer–Wolfowitz workload vector, whose coordinates are the (sorted in increasing order) residual workloads at the m servers seen by the n-th arriving customer. The vector W_n satisfies the recursion
   W_{n+1} = R(W_n + σ_n e_1 − t_n 1)^+,
where e_1 = (1,0,…,0), 1 = (1,…,1), (·)^+ denotes coordinatewise positive part, and R(·) reorders the entries in increasing order. Assume the initial condition W_0 = 0.

Under the stability condition there exists a unique stationary distribution π for the workload vector. The question is the following:

Prove or disprove that, under the assumptions above (stationarity and ergodicity of {(σ_n, t_n)}, the stability condition Eσ_1 < m E t_1, and W_0 = 0), and without imposing any additional mixing, regenerative, or independence condition, one has convergence in total variation:
   sup_{A ∈ 𝓑(ℝ_+^m)} | P(W_n ∈ A) − π(A) | → 0  as n → ∞.

Let $G$ be a group with identity $e$. A subset $A\subseteq G$ is called *central* if $e\in A$ and for every finite subset $F\subseteq G$ there exists $g\in G$ such that $gFg^{-1}\subseteq A$ (equivalently, in the abelian setting, $A$ is central if $e\in A$ and $A$ contains a translate of every finite symmetric subset of $G$, where a set $S\subseteq G$ is symmetric if $S=-S$). For an abelian group $G$, define
$$\chi(G)=\min\{|A|:A\text{ is a central subset of }G\},$$
the minimal cardinality of a central subset of $G$.

Consider the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^n$ for $n>3$.

(a) Compute the value of $\chi(\mathbb{Z}^n)$.

(b) Describe the structure of central subsets of $\mathbb{Z}^n$ (in particular, characterize those central subsets attaining or close to attaining the minimum cardinality $\chi(\mathbb{Z}^n)$).

Consider a first-come-first-served queue with m identical servers (m ≥ 2) operating in continuous time. Customers arrive at epochs determined by an i.i.d. sequence of strictly positive interarrival times {t_n}_{n≥1} with finite mean E t_1, and require service times forming an i.i.d. sequence {σ_n}_{n≥1} with finite mean E σ_1; the two sequences are mutually independent. Define the traffic load
   ρ := E σ_1 / E t_1,
and assume the stability condition ρ < m, so that the stationary waiting (delay) distribution is unique. Let D denote a random variable with this stationary waiting-time distribution.

For γ > 0, give necessary and sufficient conditions on the distributions of σ_1 and t_1 under which
   E D^γ < ∞,
in the case where ρ is a positive integer (1 ≤ ρ ≤ m−1).

status_assertions.value: open_status:unknown

Necessary and sufficient conditions for finiteness of power moments of stationary delay in stable GI/GI/m FCFS queues are well established when the load ρ is non-integer (notably by Scheller-Wolf and Vesilo, 2006/2011, and via tail-bound methods by Foss and Korshunov). The boundary case where ρ is exactly a positive integer is recognized as a gap: the standard sufficient/necessary conditions involve ⌈ρ⌉ and a strict separation that degenerates when ρ is integral. No published source located in this search definitively resolves the integer-load case in full generality, so the status is treated as unknown.

Let G be a group. A subset S ⊆ G is called symmetric if there exists g ∈ G such that S = gS^{-1}g, i.e., S is invariant under the involution x ↦ gx^{-1}g for some g ∈ G. For an infinite cardinal κ, define ν(G, κ) to be the smallest cardinal number λ such that G admits a coloring χ : G → λ with the property that no color class contains a symmetric subset of cardinality ≥ κ.

Question: Is it provable in ZFC (without any additional set-theoretic assumptions such as GCH) that
   ν(G, κ) ≥ ℵ₀
for every infinite cardinal κ and every infinite Abelian group G with |G| > κ? Equivalently, must it be the case that for every Abelian group G with |G| > κ and every coloring of G with finitely many colors, some color class contains a symmetric subset of cardinality at least κ?

Consider a first-come first-served GI/GI/2 queue: i.i.d. interarrival times with mean $1/\lambda \in (0,\infty)$ feed two identical servers in parallel, with i.i.d. service times having distribution $B$ on $[0,\infty)$, mean $\mu^{-1}\in(0,\infty)$, independent of the arrival process. Define the traffic intensity $\rho := \lambda/(2\mu)$ and consider the critical case $\rho = 1$. Assume that the service-time distribution $B$ is subexponential, i.e. $\overline{B}(x):=1-B(x)>0$ for all $x$ and $\overline{B^{*2}}(x)/\overline{B}(x) \to 2$ as $x\to\infty$; in particular consider the case where $\overline{B}$ is regularly varying at infinity with some index $-\alpha$, $\alpha>1$.

Although under $\rho = 1$ the system is not stable in the usual sense, suppose a stationary version of the waiting time $D$ exists (in an appropriate generalized or limiting sense). Determine the exact tail asymptotics of $P(D > x)$ as $x \to \infty$, expressed as an explicit function of $x$ (with a sharp constant) in terms of $\overline{B}$, $\lambda$, and $\mu$. As a particular instance, give the asymptotics when $\overline{B}(x) = L(x)x^{-\alpha}$ for a slowly varying function $L$.

Additionally, characterize the typical sample paths of the input process leading to $\{D > x\}$ for large $x$ (the "fluid" / large-deviations description of the most likely scenario).

Blanchet and Murthy (arXiv:1502.04431, published in Queueing Systems, 2015) established asymptotic upper and lower bounds for the tail of the steady-state waiting time in the half-loaded (ρ=1) GI/GI/2 queue with regularly varying job sizes, identifying two competing phenomena (one big job vs. two big jobs) when service times have finite variance, and a phase transition to a single-big-job regime in the infinite-variance case. However, exact tail asymptotics with sharp constants for general subexponential service-time distributions in the critical regime ρ=1 do not appear to be fully resolved; only bounds and special cases are available, so the problem is partially solved.

representations.normalized:
Consider a GI/GI/2 first-come-first-served queue: customers arrive at the epochs of a renewal process with i.i.d. interarrival times having mean 1/λ, and require i.i.d. service times {σ_n} (independent of the arrival process) with common distribution F on [0,∞) and finite mean E σ. There are two identical servers in parallel, and an arriving customer is assigned to the first available server (ties broken arbitrarily). Let ρ = λ E σ / 2 denote the traffic intensity, and assume the system is stable in the sense that the stationary waiting time D (the delay in queue of a typical customer in steady state) exists and is finite a.s.

Describe the typical sample paths (i.e. the most likely scenarios in terms of the joint behavior of interarrival times and service times of finitely or infinitely many customers preceding the tagged one) that lead to large values of D, in each of the following two regimes:

(a) ρ = 1 (critical loading at the level of a single server, i.e. λ E σ = 2) with service-time distribution F belonging to the class of subexponential distributions on [0,∞) (a distribution F with unbounded support on [0,∞) is subexponential if its tail F̄(x) = 1 − F(x) satisfies F̄(x+y)/F̄(x) → 1 for every y as x → ∞, and F*F̄(x)/F̄(x) → 2 as x → ∞).

(b) ρ ∈ (1, 2) (so the system is stable as a two-server queue but unstable as a single-server queue) with F heavy-tailed but having all power moments finite, i.e. ∫_0^∞ e^{εx} dF(x) = ∞ for every ε > 0 while ∫_0^∞ x^p dF(x) < ∞ for every p > 0 (for example, F a Weibull-type distribution with shape parameter strictly less than 1).

Identify, for each regime, the qualitative form of the trajectory of preceding interarrival and service times conditional on {D > x} as x → ∞, and the asymptotics of P(D > x) consistent with such typical paths.

For multi-server GI/GI/s queues with heavy-tailed (intermediate regularly varying) service times, Foss and Korshunov established a "principle of s−k big jumps" giving the most probable way for the stationary delay to be large, where k = ⌊ρ⌋. This addresses heavy-tailed cases when the tail is regularly varying, and was extended (e.g., by Foss, Korshunov, and others) to Weibull service times in the multi-server setting. However, the specific cases asked here — ρ = 1 with a general subexponential service distribution, and ρ ∈ (1,2) with a heavy-tailed distribution having all power moments finite — are not fully resolved in the same explicit "typical-path" form, so the problem appears to be only partially solved.

representations.normalized:
Consider a two-server queueing system operating under the join-the-shortest-queue (JSQ) discipline. There are two servers, each with its own individual FIFO queue. Customers arrive according to a stationary ergodic marked point process {(t_n, σ_n)}_{n∈ℤ}, where t_n ∈ ℝ is the arrival time of the n-th customer (with t_n ≤ t_{n+1}) and σ_n ≥ 0 is its service requirement. Upon arrival, customer n instantaneously joins the queue with the smaller current number of waiting-and-in-service customers (ties broken uniformly at random); once placed, the customer does not switch queues. Each server works at unit speed serving its own queue in FIFO order.

Let λ = 1/E[t_{n+1}-t_n] denote the arrival rate and E[σ] the mean service requirement. Assume the natural (necessary) stability condition λ E[σ] < 2, and make no further structural assumptions on the input (in particular, no independence, no renewal property, and no specific distribution for the service times).

A "stationary regime" means a stationary ergodic distribution of the workload/queue-length process on the Palm probability space, compatible with the given input.

Question: Under only the above stability condition, how many distinct stationary regimes can this two-server JSQ system admit? In particular, must the stationary regime be unique, or can multiple (finitely or infinitely many) stationary regimes coexist?

Consider a multi-server queue with $s \ge 2$ identical servers and an infinite waiting room, governed by the join-the-shortest-queue (JSQ) discipline: each arriving customer is routed upon arrival to a server whose current queue length (including the customer in service, if any) is minimal, with ties broken by some fixed rule. The input is described by a sequence $\{(t_n,\sigma_n)\}_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}$, where $t_n$ is the arrival epoch of customer $n$ (with interarrival times $\tau_n=t_{n+1}-t_n$) and $\sigma_n$ is the service requirement of customer $n$. Assume that $\{(\tau_n,\sigma_n)\}_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}$ is a stationary and ergodic sequence on some probability space, with finite mean interarrival time $\mathbb{E}\tau_0$ and finite mean service time $\mathbb{E}\sigma_0$, satisfying the natural traffic condition $\mathbb{E}\sigma_0 < s\,\mathbb{E}\tau_0$.

Determine the minimal additional assumptions on the joint law of $\{(\tau_n,\sigma_n)\}$ (beyond stationarity, ergodicity, and the traffic condition) under which the system admits a unique stationary regime, i.e., a unique stationary distribution of the workload (or queue-length) vector compatible with the driving input.

Consider the join-the-shortest-queue (JSQ) model with $N \ge 2$ parallel single-server FIFO queues. Customers arrive according to a stationary ergodic point process on $\mathbb{R}$ with finite intensity $\lambda$, and the $n$-th customer brings a service requirement $\sigma_n$, where $\{\sigma_n\}$ is a stationary ergodic sequence with finite mean $\mathbb{E}[\sigma_0] = 1/\mu$ jointly stationary with the arrivals. Each server works at unit speed. Upon arrival, a customer is routed to a queue with the smallest current queue length (ties broken by an arbitrary measurable rule, e.g., lowest index). Assume only the natural stability condition $\rho := \lambda/(N\mu) < 1$.

Let $Q(t) = (Q_1(t), \dots, Q_N(t))$ denote the vector of queue lengths at time $t$ and $W(t) = (W_1(t), \dots, W_N(t))$ the vector of workloads at time $t$, started from a fixed initial condition (e.g., all queues empty at time $0$).

Determine conditions on the joint law of the arrival process and service times under which the distribution of $Q(t)$ (respectively $W(t)$) converges, as $t \to \infty$, weakly, or in total variation, to a stationary distribution of the JSQ system. In particular, decide whether such convergence holds under the sole assumption $\rho < 1$, and if not, identify additional ergodicity, mixing, or regeneration assumptions on the input that ensure weak or total variation convergence to stationarity.

representations.normalized:
Consider a single server moving on a circle of unit circumference. Particles (customers) arrive according to a homogeneous Poisson process of rate $\lambda > 0$, and each arriving particle is placed independently and uniformly at random on the circle. Serving a particle takes exactly one unit of time, during which the server is stationary at the particle's location. After completing a service the particle disappears and the server chooses, among the particles currently waiting, the one nearest to its current position (along the circle) and moves toward it at a fixed positive finite constant speed $v$; new arrivals during this travel are ignored for routing purposes (the destination is not updated mid-trip), although they join the queue. Upon reaching the chosen particle, the server serves it (taking one unit of time) and the procedure repeats.

Let $N_t$ denote the number of waiting particles at time $t$. The system is called stable if the underlying Markov process describing the configuration (server position together with the locations of waiting particles) is positive recurrent.

Prove or disprove: for every $\lambda < 1$ and every fixed speed $v \in (0,\infty)$, this greedy-server system is stable.

status_assertions.value: open_status:solved

The conjecture (commonly attributed to Coffman and Gilbert, 1987) that the greedy server on the circle is positive recurrent whenever the arrival rate is less than the service rate has been proven. Rojas-Nandayapa, Foss, and Kroese (arXiv:1112.2389, "Stability of the Greedy Algorithm on the Circle") establish that lambda < 1 is sufficient for stability, regardless of the server's speed.

Fix a circle $\mathbb{T}_L$ of length $L > 0$ and a parameter $\varepsilon > 0$. Consider the following continuous-time stochastic particle system on $\mathbb{T}_L$, driven by two independent homogeneous Poisson point processes on $\mathbb{T}_L 	imes [0,\infty)$:

- Black arrivals occur at rate $\lambda$ per unit length per unit time. When a black arrival occurs at location $x \in \mathbb{T}_L$ and time $t$, a black particle is placed at $x$ and remains there indefinitely (until possibly removed by the rule below).
- White arrivals occur at rate $1$ per unit length per unit time. When a white arrival occurs at location $y \in \mathbb{T}_L$ and time $t$, the white particle inspects all black particles currently lying in the arc $\{z \in \mathbb{T}_L : d(z,y) \leq \varepsilon\}$, where $d$ is the geodesic distance on $\mathbb{T}_L$. If this set is non-empty, the white particle deletes the black particle in this set that is closest to $y$ (ties broken arbitrarily); the white particle then disappears. If the set is empty, the white particle simply disappears, leaving the configuration unchanged.

Let $N_t$ denote the number of black particles on $\mathbb{T}_L$ at time $t$, started from $N_0 = 0$. Call the system stable if $\{N_t : t \geq 0\}$ is tight (equivalently, the Markov process admits a stationary distribution).

Prove or disprove: for every $L > 0$ and every $\varepsilon > 0$, the system is stable whenever $\lambda < 1$.

representations.normalized:
Consider a continuous-time queueing system with three servers, labeled 1, 2, 3, fed by a single Poisson arrival process of rate λ > 0. Each arriving customer is independently assigned to one of three classes with equal probability 1/3. The class structure determines server accessibility as follows: class-1 customers may be served only by servers 1 or 2; class-2 customers only by servers 2 or 3; class-3 customers only by servers 3 or 1. For each class, designate one of its two accessible servers as the "left" server and the other as the "right" server (e.g., for class i, server i is left and server i+1 mod 3 is right). Upon arrival, a customer observes the current workloads (i.e., remaining work) of its two accessible servers and joins the one with the smaller workload (ties broken by some fixed rule). Service times are independent across customers; if a customer ends up being served by its left server, its service time is drawn from a probability distribution F_l on [0,∞), and if served by its right server it is drawn from a distribution F_r on [0,∞). Service is non-preemptive and work-conserving at each server.

Question: Is it true that whether or not this system is stable (in the sense of positive Harris recurrence of the workload process) can depend not only on the mean service times and λ, but jointly on the initial workload state and on the entire shapes of the distributions F_l and F_r? Equivalently, exhibit choices of λ, F_l, F_r such that the system started from one initial state is stable while the same system started from a different initial state is unstable, or such that two pairs (F_l, F_r) sharing the same coarse summary parameters (e.g., means) yield different stability behaviors.

The conjecture appears in a list of open problems related to queueing stability and asserts that even for simple symmetric three-server systems with workload-based routing, stability conditions can depend on the initial state and on the full service-time distributions rather than just on summary parameters. Status is therefore taken as unknown.

representations.normalized:
Consider an open polling system consisting of two stations, labelled $i = 1, 2$, and two heterogeneous servers, labelled $j = 1, 2$. Customers arrive at station $i$ according to a Poisson process of rate $\lambda_i = 1$, and the two arrival processes are independent. The service time of a customer at station $i$ when served by server $j$ is exponentially distributed with rate $\mu_i^{(j)} > 0$, with all service times mutually independent and independent of the arrival processes. Both servers follow the exhaustive service policy: a server present at a station continues to serve customers there until the queue at that station empties, after which it switches instantaneously (zero switch-over time) to the other station. If, upon arriving at a station (or after emptying one), a server finds no customers waiting at either station, it becomes passive and remains idle until a new customer arrives. The system is parametrized by the positive vector $(\mu_1^{(1)}, \mu_1^{(2)}, \mu_2^{(1)}, \mu_2^{(2)}) \in (0, \infty)^4$.

The underlying Markov process describing the joint queue lengths and server locations may be positive recurrent, null recurrent, or transient depending on the parameters. Question: does the set of parameter vectors $(\mu_i^{(j)})_{i,j \in \{1,2\}} \in (0,\infty)^4$ for which the system is null recurrent have strictly positive four-dimensional Lebesgue measure?

The problem appears to be a stated conjecture about a specific two-station, two-heterogeneous-server exhaustive polling model. Related work on polling systems with parameter regeneration has shown that null recurrence can occur on thick (positive-measure) regions of parameter space for related models, but no source found establishes (or refutes) the conjecture for the specific exhaustive two-server polling system as stated. Status appears still open.

Let $S^{m-1}=\{x=(x_1,\dots,x_m)\in\mathbb{R}^m:\ x_i\ge 0,\ \sum_{i=1}^m x_i=1\}$ be the standard $(m-1)$-simplex, and let $\mathrm{int}\,S^{m-1}$ denote its interior. A Volterra quadratic stochastic operator $V:S^{m-1}\to S^{m-1}$ is a map of the form
$$x'_k = x_k\Bigl(1+\sum_{i=1}^m a_{ki}\,x_i\Bigr),\qquad k=1,\dots,m,$$
where the matrix $A=(a_{ij})$ is skew-symmetric ($a_{ij}=-a_{ji}$) and satisfies $|a_{ij}|\le 1$ for all $i,j$.

A continuous function $\varphi:\mathrm{int}\,S^{m-1}\to\mathbb{R}$ is called a Lyapunov function for the discrete dynamical system $x^{(n+1)}=V(x^{(n)})$ if the sequence $\{\varphi(x^{(n)})\}_{n\ge 0}$ is monotone (non-increasing or non-decreasing) along every trajectory in $\mathrm{int}\,S^{m-1}$.

Three families of Lyapunov functions are already known for every such operator:
(i) multiplicative monomials $\varphi_p(x)=x_1^{p_1}\cdots x_m^{p_m}$ with $p_i\ge 0$ and $\sum_{i=1}^m p_i=1$;
(ii) under a suitable sign condition on the coefficients (existence of $r\in\{1,\dots,m\}$ such that $a_{ij}<0$ for appropriate $i,j$), the coordinate sums $\varphi(x)=\sum_{i=r+1}^m x_i$;
(iii) coordinate ratios $\varphi(x)=x_i/x_j$ with $i\ne j$.

Problem. Determine whether there exists a Lyapunov function for the Volterra quadratic stochastic operator above that does not belong to any of the three families (i), (ii), (iii); if so, exhibit such a new family.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Subsequent work has produced additional Lyapunov functions in restricted settings (e.g., for ℓ-Volterra operators and for infinite-dimensional Volterra/Lotka–Volterra operators on the simplex), enriching the catalogue of Lyapunov functions beyond the three classical families. However, no general classification or complete answer characterizing all Lyapunov functions of an arbitrary finite-dimensional Volterra QSO appears to be available, so the problem is best regarded as partially solved.

Consider a slotted multi-access communication channel with unit-length time slots. The number of packets arriving in slot n is Poisson with parameter λ > 0, and arrivals in distinct slots are independent. Let W_n denote the number of packets present in the system at the beginning of slot n. At slot n, each packet currently in the system independently attempts transmission with probability p_n ∈ (0,1]. A slot is called:
 • successful if exactly one packet transmits (in which case that packet leaves the system),
 • a collision if two or more transmit (all such packets remain in the system),
 • empty if no packet transmits.

Define the success indicator S_n ∈ {0,1} by S_n = 1 if slot n is successful and S_n = 0 otherwise. Suppose the transmission probabilities are produced by a deterministic update rule of the form
   p_{n+1} = f(p_n, S_n),
for some measurable function f, so that p_{n+1} depends on past history only through p_n and the single bit S_n (success vs. non-success). Under this rule, (W_n, p_n) is a time-homogeneous Markov chain.

Question: Does there exist a choice of update rule f and an initial p_0 ∈ (0,1] such that, for some λ > 0, the Markov chain (W_n, p_n) is positive recurrent (ergodic)?

A targeted search did not yield a definitive resolution of this specific question (existence of a positive recurrent protocol for slotted ALOHA when feedback is restricted to the single bit "success vs. non-success"). Related stability results for ALOHA with richer (ternary) feedback and instability results for binary exponential backoff under infinite-population models are known, but the success-only-feedback variant for the finite-state Markov chain (W_n, p_n) does not appear to have a published resolution found in this search. Status is therefore reported as unknown.

A quadratic stochastic operator (QSO) on the (m−1)-dimensional simplex
S^{m−1} = { x = (x_1,…,x_m) ∈ R^m : x_i ≥ 0, ∑_i x_i = 1 }
is a map V : S^{m−1} → S^{m−1} of the form
(V(x))_k = ∑_{i,j=1}^{m} P_{ij,k} x_i x_j,    k = 1,…,m,
where the heredity coefficients P_{ij,k} satisfy
P_{ij,k} = P_{ji,k} ≥ 0    and    ∑_{k=1}^{m} P_{ij,k} = 1   for all i,j.

A QSO is called Volterra if P_{ij,k} = 0 whenever k ∉ {i,j}; in this case V is determined by a skew-symmetric matrix A = (a_{ij}) with a_{ij} ∈ [−1,1] via (V(x))_k = x_k(1 + ∑_{i=1}^m a_{ki} x_i).

A skew-symmetric matrix A is called transversal if every even-order leading principal minor of A is nonzero. A Volterra QSO is called transversal when its associated skew-symmetric matrix A is transversal.

Problem. Extend the notion of transversality from Volterra QSO to the class of all quadratic stochastic operators. Specifically:
(a) Give a definition of "transversal QSO" that, when restricted to Volterra operators, coincides with the classical definition above.
(b) Determine necessary and sufficient conditions, expressed directly in terms of the cubic array of heredity coefficients P = (P_{ij,k})_{i,j,k=1}^{m}, under which a quadratic stochastic operator V with heredity coefficients P is transversal in the sense of (a).

Let $S^{m-1} = \{x = (x_1,\dots,x_m) \in \mathbb{R}^m : x_i \geq 0,\ \sum_{i=1}^m x_i = 1\}$ denote the standard $(m-1)$-simplex. A quadratic stochastic operator $V : S^{m-1} \to S^{m-1}$ is given by
$$ (Vx)_k = \sum_{i,j=1}^m p_{ij,k}\, x_i x_j, \qquad k=1,\dots,m, $$
where the coefficients satisfy $p_{ij,k} = p_{ji,k} \geq 0$ and $\sum_{k=1}^m p_{ij,k} = 1$ for all $i,j$. The operator $V$ is called Volterra if $p_{ij,k} = 0$ whenever $k \notin \{i,j\}$; equivalently $(Vx)_k = x_k\bigl(1 + \sum_{j=1}^m a_{kj} x_j\bigr)$ with $a_{kj} = -a_{jk}$ and $|a_{kj}| \leq 1$. Call $V$ transversal if its set of fixed points in $S^{m-1}$ is finite; let these fixed points be $x_1,\dots,x_t$.

Choose pairwise disjoint open neighborhoods $U_1,\dots,U_t \subset S^{m-1}$ with $x_s \in U_s$, and assume $U := U_1 \cup \cdots \cup U_t$ has the property that for every initial point $x^{(0)} \in S^{m-1}$, the trajectory $x^{(s)} = V^s(x^{(0)})$ eventually enters $U$ and from some step on lies entirely in $U$. For such a trajectory, define its itinerary to be the sequence $n_1, n_2, \dots \in \{1,\dots,t\}$ where $x^{(s)} \in U_{n_s}$ for all sufficiently large $s$ (after reindexing).

Question: Does there exist a transversal Volterra quadratic stochastic operator $V$ and an initial point $x^{(0)} \in S^{m-1}$ whose trajectory has an eventually periodic itinerary $n_1, n_2, \dots$ that is non-constant (i.e., the trajectory genuinely cycles through neighborhoods of distinct fixed points)?

Let $k$ be a field of characteristic zero, and let $\mathrm{GA}_n(k)$ denote the group of polynomial automorphisms of the affine $n$-space $\mathbb{A}^n_k$, i.e. the group of $k$-algebra automorphisms of the polynomial ring $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$. The tame subgroup $\mathrm{TA}_n(k) \subseteq \mathrm{GA}_n(k)$ is the subgroup generated by all affine automorphisms together with all elementary automorphisms of the form
$$(x_1,\dots,x_n)\mapsto (x_1,\dots,x_{i-1},\,x_i + f(x_1,\dots,\hat x_i,\dots,x_n),\,x_{i+1},\dots,x_n),$$
where $f \in k[x_1,\dots,\hat x_i,\dots,x_n]$. A one-parameter subgroup of $\mathrm{GA}_n(k)$ is a homomorphism $(k,+)\to \mathrm{GA}_n(k)$ of algebraic groups; equivalently, it is the exponential flow $\{\exp(tD)\}_{t\in k}$ of a locally nilpotent $k$-derivation $D$ of $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$.

Question: Is there a finite collection of one-parameter subgroups $U_1,\dots,U_m$ of $\mathrm{GA}_n(k)$ such that $\mathrm{GA}_n(k)$ is generated, as a group, by $\mathrm{TA}_n(k) \cup U_1\cup \cdots \cup U_m$?

Let $S^2 = \{(x,y,z) \in \mathbb{R}^3 : x,y,z \geq 0,\ x+y+z = 1\}$ denote the 2-dimensional standard simplex. For parameters $a,b,c \in [-1,1]$, define the Volterra quadratic stochastic operator $V : S^2 \to S^2$ by
$$x' = x(1 + ay - bz),\qquad y' = y(1 - ax + cz),\qquad z' = z(1 + bx - cy).$$
For a point $u \in S^2$, say that the ergodic theorem holds at $u$ if the Cesàro averages
$$\frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1} V^k(u)$$
converge as $n \to \infty$, and say the ergodic theorem holds for $V$ if it holds at every $u \in S^2$.

It is known that if $a,b,c$ are all nonzero and all have the same sign, then the ergodic theorem fails for $V$.

Problem: Determine a sharp sufficient condition on $(a,b,c) \in [-1,1]^3$ that guarantees the ergodic theorem holds for $V$. In particular, decide whether the negation of the same-sign-and-nonzero condition (i.e., $abc = 0$ or $a,b,c$ do not all share the same sign) is sufficient for the ergodic theorem to hold for $V$.

Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. For each integer $n\ge 2$ and each polynomial $f(x)\in k[x]$ with $f(0)\ne 0$, consider the normal affine surface
$$S_{n,f} = \mathrm{Spec}\, A_{n,f},\qquad A_{n,f}=k[x,y,z]/(x^n z - y^2 - f(x)y).$$
These algebras (a family of Danielewski-type surfaces) are pairwise non-isomorphic for suitable parameter choices, yet they share many classical invariants (e.g. they can be homeomorphic at infinity in the topological sense while being algebraically rigid).

Problem. Construct an intrinsic algebraic invariant $\mathcal{I}(A)$, defined for every normal finitely generated $k$-algebra $A$, with the following properties:
(i) $\mathcal{I}(A)$ depends only on the $k$-algebra structure of $A$ (intrinsic);
(ii) $\mathcal{I}(A)$ captures algebraic rigidity of the "tubular neighborhood of infinity" of $\mathrm{Spec}\, A$, in the sense that it refines the homotopy type at infinity by adding a "continuous" dimension;
(iii) the value of $\mathcal{I}$ on $A_{n,f}$ distinguishes, in a direct way, all isomorphism classes among the algebras $\{A_{n,f}\}_{n\ge 2,\ f\in k[x],\ f(0)\ne 0}$.

Provide such an invariant and prove that it has these three properties.

Let $S^{m-1}=\{x=(x_1,\dots,x_m)\in\mathbb{R}^m : x_i\ge 0,\ \sum_{i=1}^m x_i=1\}$ denote the standard $(m-1)$-simplex, with $m\ge 2$. A Volterra quadratic stochastic operator (Volterra QSO) on $S^{m-1}$ is a map $V:S^{m-1}\to S^{m-1}$ of the form
$$x'_k = (V(x))_k = x_k\Bigl(1+\sum_{i=1}^m a_{ki}x_i\Bigr),\qquad k=1,\dots,m,$$
where the coefficient matrix $A=(a_{ij})_{i,j=1}^m$ is skew-symmetric ($a_{ij}=-a_{ji}$) and satisfies $|a_{ij}|\le 1$ so that $V$ maps the simplex into itself.

For $n\ge 1$ and $x\in S^{m-1}$, define the Cesàro averages of the trajectory of $x$ under $V$ by
$$C_n(x)=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}V^k(x).$$
We say that the ergodic theorem holds for $V$ if $\lim_{n\to\infty}C_n(x)$ exists in $S^{m-1}$ for every $x\in S^{m-1}$.

Problem. Find necessary and sufficient conditions on the skew-symmetric matrix $A$ under which the ergodic theorem holds for the corresponding Volterra QSO on $S^{m-1}$.

Let $\mathbb{C}$ denote the field of complex numbers, and let $R = \mathbb{C}[a,b]$ be the polynomial ring in two variables $a,b$ over $\mathbb{C}$. Consider the polynomial ring $R[x,y,z]$ in three further variables $x,y,z$ over $R$. An $R$-derivation $D : R[x,y,z] \to R[x,y,z]$ is called triangular if
$$D(x) \in R, \qquad D(y) \in R[x], \qquad D(z) \in R[x,y].$$
Every triangular $R$-derivation is automatically locally nilpotent (for every $f \in R[x,y,z]$ there exists $n \geq 1$ with $D^n(f) = 0$). A slice for $D$ is an element $s \in R[x,y,z]$ with $D(s) = 1$. The kernel
$$\ker(D) = \{f \in R[x,y,z] : D(f) = 0\}$$
is an $R$-subalgebra of $R[x,y,z]$, and one writes $R^{[2]}$ for the polynomial ring in two variables over $R$.

Question: Suppose $D$ is a triangular locally nilpotent $R$-derivation of $R[x,y,z]$ that admits a slice. Must $\ker(D)$ be isomorphic, as an $R$-algebra, to $R^{[2]}$ (i.e., a polynomial ring in two variables over $R$)?

Let $S^{m-1} = \{x = (x_1, \dots, x_m) \in \mathbb{R}^m : x_i \ge 0, \sum_{i=1}^m x_i = 1\}$ be the standard $(m-1)$-simplex, and let $E = \{1, 2, \dots, m\}$. A quadratic stochastic operator (QSO) is a map $V : S^{m-1} \to S^{m-1}$ defined by
$$(Vx)_k = \sum_{i,j=1}^m P_{ij,k}\, x_i x_j, \qquad k \in E,$$
where the heredity coefficients satisfy $P_{ij,k} = P_{ji,k} \ge 0$ and $\sum_{k=1}^m P_{ij,k} = 1$ for all $i,j \in E$.

Fix $\ell \in E$. Call $V$ an $\ell$-Volterra QSO if its coefficients satisfy:
(i) $P_{ij,k} = 0$ whenever $k \notin \{i,j\}$ and $i,j \in \{1,\dots,\ell\}$ (Volterra-type restriction on the first $\ell$ coordinates);
(ii) for $i \in \{1,\dots,\ell\}$ and $j \in E$, $P_{ij,k}$ is allowed to be nonzero only for $k \in \{i,j\}$;
(iii) for $i, j \in \{\ell+1,\dots,m\}$, the coefficients $P_{ij,k}$ may be nonzero for arbitrary $k \in E$ (genuinely non-Volterra behavior on the last $m-\ell$ coordinates).

Let $e_1, \dots, e_m$ denote the vertices of $S^{m-1}$. It is known that for any subset $I_s = \{e_{i_1}, \dots, e_{i_s}\} \subset \{e_{\ell+1}, \dots, e_m\}$ with $s \le m$, there exists a family of $\ell$-Volterra QSOs for which $I_s$ is an $s$-cycle (i.e., the vertices in $I_s$ are permuted cyclically by $V$).

A trajectory $\{x, Vx, V^2x, \dots\}$ starting at $x \in S^{m-1}$ is called periodic with period $p \ge 1$ if $V^p x = x$ and $V^q x \ne x$ for $1 \le q < p$.

Problem. For a given $\ell$-Volterra QSO $V$ on $S^{m-1}$, classify the set of all periodic trajectories of $V$ (not only the vertex cycles described above).

be the subgroup of $\mathrm{GA}_n(k)$ that stabilizes the linear subspace $k\oplus kx_1\oplus\cdots\oplus kx_i$ of $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$. Note that $G_n=\mathrm{Aff}_n(k)$ is the affine group, and $G_1$ consists of the triangular (de Jonquières) automorphisms. Let $\mathrm{TA}_n(k)\subseteq\mathrm{GA}_n(k)$ denote the subgroup generated by $G_1,\dots,G_n$ (the tame subgroup).

(a) Is $\mathrm{GA}_n(k)$ generated by $G_1,\dots,G_n$, i.e., does $\mathrm{GA}_n(k)=\mathrm{TA}_n(k)$?

(b) If so, is $\mathrm{TA}_n(k)$ isomorphic to the amalgamated product of the groups $G_1,\dots,G_n$ along their pairwise intersections?

For $n=2$ the Jung–van der Kulk theorem gives the amalgamated product structure. For $n=3$ over a field of characteristic zero, Shestakov–Umirbaev (2004) showed $\mathrm{GA}_3(k)\neq\mathrm{TA}_3(k)$, so part (a) fails for $n\ge 3$. Wright (2015) established that $\mathrm{TA}_3(k)$ has a generalized amalgamated product structure as the amalgam of the three subgroups along pairwise intersections, answering (b) affirmatively for the tame group when $n=3$. The general case for $n\ge 4$ remains open.

The general problem of relating the dynamics of $V_\lambda=\lambda V_1+(1-\lambda)V_2$ to those of $V_1,V_2$ remains open in full generality. Partial results are known: the class of bistochastic QSOs is closed under convex combinations while the class of dissipative QSOs is not; specific families on the 2D simplex have been analyzed (e.g., a convex combination of two QSOs with the simplex center as unique attracting fixed point; non-Volterra one-parameter families where trajectories converge to a fixed point for $\alpha\in[0,1)$ and to a periodic orbit at $\alpha=1$). No general theory addressing arbitrary $V_1,V_2$ has been established.

Let $k$ be a field and let $\mathrm{GA}_n(k) = \mathrm{Aut}_k\,k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ denote the group of polynomial automorphisms of affine $n$-space over $k$. An automorphism $F\in\mathrm{GA}_n(k)$ is called elementary if it has the form
$$F:(x_1,\dots,x_n)\longmapsto(x_1,\dots,x_{i-1},\,a x_i+f(x_1,\dots,\hat{x_i},\dots,x_n),\,x_{i+1},\dots,x_n)$$
for some $i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$, $a\in k^\times$, and $f\in k[x_1,\dots,\hat{x_i},\dots,x_n]$. The tame automorphism group $\mathrm{TA}_n(k)\subseteq\mathrm{GA}_n(k)$ is the subgroup generated by all elementary automorphisms together with the general linear group $\mathrm{GL}_n(k)$ (acting linearly on the variables) and translations.

For each $i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$, let $G_i\subseteq\mathrm{GA}_n(k)$ be the stabilizer subgroup
$$G_i=\bigl\{F\in\mathrm{GA}_n(k):F\bigl(k[x_1,\dots,\hat{x_i},\dots,x_n]\bigr)=k[x_1,\dots,\hat{x_i},\dots,x_n]\bigr\},$$
i.e. the subgroup of automorphisms that preserve the subalgebra obtained by omitting $x_i$. Define
$$H_i:=G_i\cap\mathrm{TA}_n(k),\qquad i=1,\dots,n.$$

Question. (a) Is $\mathrm{TA}_n(k)$ generated by $H_1,\dots,H_n$, i.e. $\mathrm{TA}_n(k)=\langle H_1,\dots,H_n\rangle$? (b) If so, is $\mathrm{TA}_n(k)$ isomorphic to the amalgamated product of $H_1,\dots,H_n$ along their pairwise intersections $H_i\cap H_j$?

Let $E = \{1, 2, \ldots, m\}$ be a finite set (the "species set") and let $S^{m-1} = \{x = (x_1, \ldots, x_m) \in \mathbb{R}^m : x_i \geq 0,\ \sum_{i=1}^m x_i = 1\}$ denote the standard simplex. A quadratic stochastic operator (QSO) is a map $V: S^{m-1} \to S^{m-1}$ defined by
$$ (Vx)_k = \sum_{i,j=1}^m P_{ij,k}\, x_i x_j, \qquad k = 1, \ldots, m, $$
where the coefficients $P_{ij,k}$ satisfy $P_{ij,k} \geq 0$, $P_{ij,k} = P_{ji,k}$, and $\sum_{k=1}^m P_{ij,k} = 1$ for all $i,j$.

Fix a partition $\xi = \{E_1, \ldots, E_q\}$ of $E$ (so $E = E_1 \cup \cdots \cup E_q$ with the $E_p$ pairwise disjoint and nonempty). A QSO $V$ is called a $\xi$-QSO if
$$ P_{ij,k} = 0 \quad \text{whenever } i, j \in E_p \text{ for some } p \in \{1, \ldots, q\}. $$

For an F-QSO (the special case of a $\xi$-QSO arising from a particular framework) it is known that $V$ has a unique fixed point $(1, 0, \ldots, 0)$ on $S^{m-1}$ and that for every initial point $x^{(0)} \in S^{m-1}$, the trajectory $x^{(n+1)} = V(x^{(n)})$ converges exponentially fast to this fixed point.

Question: Does the analogous statement hold for every $\xi$-QSO? Namely, must every $\xi$-QSO have a unique fixed point in $S^{m-1}$ such that every trajectory converges to that fixed point?

Subsequent work has investigated $\xi$-QSOs (and the related $\xi^{(s)}$-QSOs and $\xi^{(a)}$-QSOs) on low-dimensional simplices. On the 2D simplex, $\xi^{(s)}$-QSOs were classified into 20 nonconjugate classes with diverse dynamical behavior, including instances admitting multiple fixed points or non-convergent trajectories, indicating that the F-QSO theorem does not extend uniformly to all $\xi$-QSOs. A complete answer in arbitrary dimension does not appear to be established, so the problem is partially resolved at best.

Setup. Let $S^{m-1}=\{x=(x_1,\dots,x_m)\in\mathbb{R}^m: x_i\ge 0,\ \sum_{i=1}^m x_i=1\}$ denote the (m-1)-dimensional standard simplex. A quadratic stochastic operator (QSO) is a map $V:S^{m-1}\to S^{m-1}$ of the form
$$(Vx)_k = \sum_{i,j=1}^m P_{ij,k}\, x_i x_j, \qquad k=1,\dots,m,$$
where the coefficients satisfy $P_{ij,k}=P_{ji,k}\ge 0$ and $\sum_{k=1}^m P_{ij,k}=1$ for all $i,j$. The QSO $V$ is called strictly non-Volterra if $P_{ij,k}=0$ whenever $k\in\{i,j\}$ (so heredity is excluded for every pair).

Known case ($m=3$). For $m=3$ the family of strictly non-Volterra QSOs admits a parametric description
$$(Vx)_1 = a x_2^2 + 2\alpha x_1 x_3 + b x_3^2,$$
$$(Vx)_2 = c x_1^2 + 2\beta x_2 x_3 + d x_3^2,$$
$$(Vx)_3 = (1-c)x_1^2 + 2(1-\alpha)x_1x_3 + (1-a)x_2^2 + 2(1-\beta)x_2 x_3 + (1-b-d)x_3^2,$$
with parameters $a,b,c,d,\alpha,\beta\in[0,1]$ satisfying $b+d\le 1$. In this $m=3$ case it is known that:
(i) $V$ has a unique fixed point in $S^2$;
(ii) this fixed point is not attractive (i.e. it is not a local attractor of the dynamics $x,Vx,V^2x,\dots$);
(iii) for suitable parameter values, $V$ admits 2-cycles and 3-cycles (nontrivial periodic orbits of periods 2 and 3).

Question. Determine whether the analogous statements hold for every strictly non-Volterra QSO $V$ on $S^{m-1}$ with $m\ge 4$. Specifically, prove or disprove:
(a) every strictly non-Volterra QSO on $S^{m-1}$ has a unique fixed point in $S^{m-1}$;
(b) such a fixed point is never attractive;
(c) such operators admit 2-cycles and 3-cycles for appropriate choices of parameters.

Let $S^{m-1}=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^m: x_i\ge 0,\ \sum_{i=1}^m x_i=1\}$ be the $(m-1)$-dimensional standard simplex. A quadratic stochastic operator (QSO) $V:S^{m-1}\to S^{m-1}$ is defined by a system of heredity coefficients $\{P_{ij,k}\}_{i,j,k=1}^{m}$ satisfying
$$P_{ij,k}=P_{ji,k}\ge 0,\qquad \sum_{k=1}^{m}P_{ij,k}=1\quad\text{for all }i,j\in\{1,\dots,m\},$$
acting by
$$(Vx)_k=\sum_{i,j=1}^{m}P_{ij,k}\,x_i x_j,\qquad k=1,\dots,m.$$
The operator $V$ is called regular if for every initial point $x\in S^{m-1}$ the iterates $V^n(x)$ converge, as $n\to\infty$, to a fixed point of $V$ (the limit may depend on $x$).

For each integer $m\ge 2$, define
$$\alpha_m=\inf\Big\{\alpha\in[0,1]:\ \text{every QSO $V$ on $S^{m-1}$ with $P_{ij,k}>\alpha$ for all $i,j,k$ is regular}\Big\}.$$
It is known that $\alpha_m\le \tfrac{1}{2m}$ and that $\alpha_2=\tfrac{1}{2}(3-\sqrt{7})$.

Determine the exact value of $\alpha_m$ for every $m\ge 3$.

Recall that a $k$-subspace $M \subseteq A$ is called a (two-sided) Mathieu subspace of $A$ if it satisfies the following property: whenever $a \in A$ is such that $a^m \in M$ for every integer $m \geq 1$, then for every $b, c \in A$ there exists an integer $N = N(a,b,c) \geq 1$ such that $b\,a^m\,c \in M$ for all $m \geq N$.

Question: Suppose $M_1$ and $M_2$ are two Mathieu subspaces of $A$. Must the $k$-subspace
$$M_1 + M_2 = \{x_1 + x_2 : x_1 \in M_1,\; x_2 \in M_2\}$$
also be a Mathieu subspace of $A$?

Let $S^{m-1} = \{x = (x_1, \dots, x_m) \in \mathbb{R}^m : x_i \ge 0, \sum_{i=1}^m x_i = 1\}$ denote the standard $(m-1)$-dimensional simplex. For $x, y \in S^{m-1}$, write $y \prec x$ (y is majorized by x) if, after rearranging the coordinates of $x$ and $y$ in non-increasing order $x_{[1]} \ge x_{[2]} \ge \cdots \ge x_{[m]}$ and $y_{[1]} \ge \cdots \ge y_{[m]}$, one has
$$\sum_{i=1}^k y_{[i]} \le \sum_{i=1}^k x_{[i]} \quad \text{for all } 1 \le k \le m-1, \quad \sum_{i=1}^m y_{[i]} = \sum_{i=1}^m x_{[i]}.$$

A quadratic stochastic operator $V: S^{m-1} \to S^{m-1}$ is a map of the form
$$(Vx)_k = \sum_{i,j=1}^m p_{ij,k} \, x_i x_j, \qquad k = 1, \dots, m,$$
where the coefficients satisfy $p_{ij,k} = p_{ji,k} \ge 0$ and $\sum_{k=1}^m p_{ij,k} = 1$ for all $i,j$.

The operator $V$ is called bistochastic if $V(x) \prec x$ for every $x \in S^{m-1}$.

Problem: Describe the long-term trajectory behavior of an arbitrary bistochastic quadratic stochastic operator $V$ on $S^{m-1}$. Specifically, characterize the limit sets of the iterates $\{V^n(x)\}_{n \ge 0}$, determine for which initial points convergence to a fixed point occurs (and identify the limiting fixed point), classify the fixed points by their stability type, and explain how the majorization constraint $V(x) \prec x$ governs the orbit structure.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Subsequent work (notably Bartoszek–Pułka and related papers around 2015–2016) established a structural characterization: a QSO on the simplex is surjective if and only if it can be written as the composition of a permutation matrix with a Lotka–Volterra QSO, and surjectivity is equivalent to bijectivity. This provides a general description valid in all dimensions, but a full enumeration/classification of extreme points in dimensions m ≥ 5 in the spirit of the m = 2, 3, 4 cases does not appear to have been completed. Hence the problem is best regarded as partially solved.

Setup. Let G = (L, E) be a finite graph with vertex set L (the "cells") and edge set E. Let Φ be a finite set, called the allele set. Define the configuration space
   Ω = Φ^L = { σ : L → Φ },
and, for each cell x ∈ L, the local configuration space Ω_x = Φ^{L_x} where L_x = {x} ∪ {y ∈ L : {x,y} ∈ E} is the closed neighborhood of x. For σ ∈ Ω write σ_x ∈ Ω_x for its restriction.

Let μ be a strictly positive probability measure on Ω, i.e. μ(σ) > 0 for all σ ∈ Ω and Σ_σ μ(σ) = 1. Define the marginal-type weights
   μ_x(σ_x) = Σ_{ω ∈ Ω: ω|_{L_x} = σ_x} μ(ω),    x ∈ L, σ_x ∈ Ω_x.

Heredity coefficients. For any two configurations σ_1, σ_2 ∈ Ω and any σ ∈ Ω, define
   P_{σ_1 σ_2, σ} = ∏_{x ∈ L}  ( μ_x(σ_x) ) /  ( ν_x(σ_1, σ_2) ),
where the normalizers ν_x(σ_1, σ_2) are chosen so that Σ_{σ ∈ Ω} P_{σ_1 σ_2, σ} = 1 for every pair (σ_1, σ_2), and so that the coefficients are symmetric in (σ_1, σ_2) and nonnegative. (This is the standard graph–measure construction in which the offspring distribution at each cell x is determined by μ_x restricted to the parents' alleles in L_x.)

Quadratic stochastic operator. Let S(L, Φ) = { h = (h_σ)_{σ ∈ Ω} : h_σ ≥ 0, Σ_σ h_σ = 1 } be the simplex of probability distributions on Ω. The associated quadratic stochastic operator (QSO) V = V_μ : S(L, Φ) → S(L, Φ) is defined by
   (V h)_σ = Σ_{σ_1, σ_2 ∈ Ω} P_{σ_1 σ_2, σ}  h_{σ_1}  h_{σ_2},   σ ∈ Ω.

   μ_x(σ_x) = Σ_{ω ∈ Ω: ω|_{L_x} = σ_x} μ(ω),    x ∈ L, σ_x ∈ Ω_x.

   P_{σ_1 σ_2, σ} = ∏_{x ∈ L}  ( μ_x(σ_x) ) /  ( ν_x(σ_1, σ_2) ),

Let $(\Gamma,+)$ be an abelian group and let $\langle\,\cdot\,,\,\cdot\,\rangle\colon \Gamma\times\Gamma\to\mathbb{Z}_2$ be a $\mathbb{Z}$-bilinear map. A $\Gamma$-graded associative algebra $A=\bigoplus_{\gamma\in\Gamma}A_\gamma$ over a field $\mathbb{K}$ (with $A_\gamma\cdot A_{\gamma'}\subseteq A_{\gamma+\gamma'}$) is called $\Gamma$-commutative if, for every pair of homogeneous elements $a\in A_{\bar a}$ and $b\in A_{\bar b}$, one has
$$ a\cdot b \;=\; (-1)^{\langle \bar a,\bar b\rangle}\, b\cdot a. $$
(Examples include ordinary commutative algebras, $\mathbb{Z}_2$-graded supercommutative algebras, and Clifford algebras viewed as $\mathbb{Z}_2^n$-commutative algebras.)

Develop a theory of the "spectrum" $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ of a $\Gamma$-commutative algebra $A$ that extends the classical spectrum of a commutative ring. Specifically:

1. Define an appropriate notion of $\Gamma$-graded prime ideal in a $\Gamma$-commutative algebra $A$, and an associated topological space $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ equipped with a Zariski-type topology and a structure sheaf, in such a way that when $\Gamma=0$ (or, more generally, when the bicharacter $\langle\,\cdot\,,\,\cdot\,\rangle$ is trivial) one recovers the classical affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}(A_0)$.
2. Establish the fundamental functorial properties of this construction (functoriality in $A$, behavior under localization at homogeneous elements, gluing to a notion of $\Gamma$-commutative scheme).
3. Identify and study the geometric points and a suitable analogue of the Nullstellensatz for $\Gamma$-commutative algebras.
4. Investigate to what extent classical commutative algebraic geometry (dimension theory, regularity, smoothness, sheaf cohomology) can be transported to this setting, and describe the spectra of natural examples such as Clifford algebras and quaternion-like $\Gamma$-commutative algebras for $\Gamma=\mathbb{Z}_2^n$.

Let $E$ be a continuous (uncountable) measurable state space, and let $H : E^{\Lambda} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a Hamiltonian defined on configurations over some index set $\Lambda$. For a temperature $T>0$, let $\mu_{H,T}$ denote a Gibbs measure on $E$ (or on configurations on $\Lambda$) associated with $H$ at temperature $T$, defined in the standard DLR sense. It is known that, depending on $H$ and $T$, the Gibbs measure $\mu_{H,T}$ may fail to be unique; the set of temperatures (or parameters) at which non-uniqueness occurs is called the set of phase transition points of the system.

Given such a Gibbs measure $\mu = \mu_{H,T}$, define the associated quadratic stochastic operator (QSO) $V_\mu$ on the simplex of probability measures on $E$ as follows. For a probability measure $\lambda$ on $E$, the QSO produces the new measure
$$ (V_\mu \lambda)(A) = \int_{E}\int_{E} P_\mu(x,y;A)\, d\lambda(x)\, d\lambda(y), \qquad A \subseteq E\ \text{measurable}, $$
where $\{P_\mu(x,y;\cdot)\}_{x,y\in E}$ is the family of transition probabilities canonically determined by $\mu$ (the conditional distribution governing offspring/state production from the pair $(x,y)$). The trajectory of $V_\mu$ starting from $\lambda_0$ is the sequence $\lambda_n = V_\mu^n \lambda_0$, $n\ge 0$.

Problem. Determine in a precise quantitative way how the thermodynamic behavior of the system $(H,T)$ — in particular the occurrence and structure of phase transitions of the Gibbs measure $\mu_{H,T}$ — affects the trajectories $\{\lambda_n\}_{n\ge 0}$ and the asymptotic dynamics of the corresponding QSO $V_{\mu_{H,T}}$. Specifically:

(a) Show whether non-uniqueness of $\mu_{H,T}$ at a phase transition point forces the QSO $V_{\mu_{H,T}}$ to exhibit qualitatively different asymptotic behavior (e.g. multiple limit points, non-ergodicity, periodic orbits, or coexisting attractors) compared to parameters where $\mu_{H,T}$ is unique.

(b) Identify the fixed points and $\omega$-limit sets of $V_{\mu_{H,T}}$ as functions of $(H,T)$, and relate bifurcations of these limit sets to phase transition points.

(c) Provide explicit results for at least one nontrivial family of Hamiltonians on a continuous state space.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

A general answer linking phase transitions of Gibbs measures on continuous state spaces to the asymptotic dynamics of the corresponding quadratic stochastic operators does not appear in the literature. Partial results exist for specific lattice models (e.g. Potts and Rock–Paper–Scissors models on Cayley trees, where translation-invariant and periodic Gibbs measures are linked to particular QSO dynamics) and for restricted subclasses such as F-QSOs (which have unique fixed points with exponential convergence), but no general theorem describes how phase transitions affect QSO trajectories in the continuous-state setting. The problem appears to remain open.

Let $S^{m-1}=\{x=(x_1,\dots,x_m)\in\mathbb{R}^m : x_i\ge 0,\ \sum_{i=1}^m x_i=1\}$ denote the $(m-1)$-dimensional simplex. A quadratic stochastic operator (QSO) is a map $V:S^{m-1}\to S^{m-1}$ given by
$$ (V x)_k \;=\; \sum_{i,j=1}^m P_{ij,k}\, x_i x_j, \qquad k=1,\dots,m, $$
where the coefficients $P_{ij,k}$ satisfy $P_{ij,k}=P_{ji,k}\ge 0$ for all $i,j,k$ and $\sum_{k=1}^m P_{ij,k}=1$ for all $i,j$. A QSO is called Volterra if $P_{ij,k}=0$ whenever $k\notin\{i,j\}$; otherwise it is called non-Volterra.

A QSO $V$ on $S^{m-1}$ is said to be reducible to $q\ge 2$ separate Volterra QSOs if there exists a partition $\{1,\dots,m\}=\bigsqcup_{s=1}^q I_s$ of the coordinate indices into $q$ nonempty disjoint blocks such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item each block $I_s$ is invariant under $V$ in the sense that for every $x\in S^{m-1}$ the sub-vector $(Vx)_{I_s}$ depends only on $(x_i)_{i\in I_s}$ (after a coordinate-wise normalization), and
\item the operator induced by $V$ on the simplex $\{y\in\mathbb{R}^{|I_s|} : y_i\ge 0,\ \sum_{i\in I_s} y_i=1\}$ is a Volterra QSO for each $s=1,\dots,q$.
\end{enumerate}

Problem. Give an explicit description (characterization) of the set of all non-Volterra quadratic stochastic operators $V:S^{m-1}\to S^{m-1}$ that are reducible to several separate Volterra QSOs in the above sense.

Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ ($n\ge 2$) be a bounded domain with smooth boundary, and consider a time interval $[0,T]$. Consider the motion of an incompressible Jeffreys-type viscoelastic fluid described by the unknowns: velocity field $v=(v_1,\dots,v_n)$, pressure $p$, and deviatoric (extra) stress tensor $\sigma$. Let $E=E(v)=\tfrac12(\nabla v+\nabla v^\top)$ denote the symmetric rate-of-strain tensor. For a tensor field $T$, let
$$\frac{DT}{Dt}=\frac{\partial T}{\partial t}+\sum_{i=1}^n v_i\,\frac{\partial T}{\partial x_i}+T\,W-W\,T,\qquad W=\tfrac12(\nabla v-\nabla v^\top),$$
denote a frame-indifferent (e.g. Jaumann) objective derivative. The governing system is
$$
\operatorname{div} v=0,\qquad v|_{\partial\Omega}=0,
$$
$$
\frac{\partial v}{\partial t}+\sum_{i=1}^n v_i\frac{\partial v}{\partial x_i}-\operatorname{Div}\sigma+\nabla p=f\quad\text{in }\Omega\times(0,T),
$$
$$
\sigma+\lambda_1\frac{D\sigma}{Dt}=2\eta\!\left(E+\lambda_2\frac{DE}{Dt}\right),
$$
together with initial data $v(0,\cdot)=v_0$, $\sigma(0,\cdot)=\sigma_0$, where $\eta>0$ and $0<\lambda_2<\lambda_1$ are constants and $f$ is a given external force. A weak solution is a triple $(v,p,\sigma)$ satisfying the system in the standard distributional sense with the natural energy class regularity.

Question: Is it true that, for every dimension $n\ge 2$, every weak solution of the system above is regular (i.e. smooth on $\Omega\times(0,T)$), without imposing any restrictions on the coefficients $\eta,\lambda_1,\lambda_2$, on the external force $f$, or on the initial data $(v_0,\sigma_0)$?

The regularity of weak solutions for the Jeffreys-type (Oldroyd-type) viscoelastic fluid model in dimensions $n\ge 2$ without any smallness or smoothness restrictions on data and coefficients is generally regarded as an open problem, closely related to (and at least as hard as) the unresolved global regularity question for the incompressible Navier–Stokes equations. No general regularity result without such restrictions appears in the literature; available results require small data, two-dimensional settings, or additional structural assumptions.

Let $\Omega_1, \Omega_2, \ldots, \Omega_q$ be finite sets, and let $\Omega = \Omega_1 \times \Omega_2 \times \cdots \times \Omega_q$ be the corresponding configuration space. Configurations $\sigma \in \Omega$ are written as $\sigma = (\sigma_1, \ldots, \sigma_q)$ with $\sigma_i \in \Omega_i$. Let $S(\Omega)$ denote the simplex of probability measures on $\Omega$.

A quadratic stochastic operator (QSO) $V: S(\Omega) \to S(\Omega)$ is a map of the form
$$(V x)(\sigma) = \sum_{\tau, \eta \in \Omega} P(\tau, \eta; \sigma)\, x(\tau)\, x(\eta), \qquad \sigma \in \Omega,$$

Let $S^{m-1} = \{x = (x_1, \ldots, x_m) \in \mathbb{R}^m : x_i \ge 0, \ \sum_{i=1}^m x_i = 1\}$ denote the $(m-1)$-dimensional standard simplex. A quadratic stochastic operator (QSO) is a map $V : S^{m-1} \to S^{m-1}$ defined by
$$ (V(x))_k = \sum_{i,j=1}^m p_{ij,k}\, x_i x_j, \qquad k = 1, \ldots, m, $$
where the coefficients $p_{ij,k}$ satisfy $p_{ij,k} = p_{ji,k} \ge 0$ and $\sum_{k=1}^m p_{ij,k} = 1$ for all $i,j$. For $x \in S^{m-1}$, the trajectory of $x$ under $V$ is the sequence $\{x, V(x), V^2(x), \ldots\}$, where $V^n$ is the $n$-fold iterate of $V$. The trajectory of $x$ is said to have historic behavior if there exists a continuous function $f : S^{m-1} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that the Cesàro time averages
$$ \frac{1}{n+1} \sum_{i=0}^{n} f(V^i(x)) $$
fail to converge as $n \to \infty$.

Exhibit a class of quadratic stochastic operators $V$ on some simplex $S^{m-1}$ for which the set
$$ H(V) = \{ x \in S^{m-1} : \text{the trajectory of } x \text{ under } V \text{ has historic behavior} \} $$
has positive Lebesgue measure (with respect to the natural Lebesgue measure on $S^{m-1}$).

Consider the initial-boundary value problem for an incompressible viscoelastic fluid of Jeffreys type in a bounded domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ with $n\ge 2$ and smooth boundary $\partial\Omega$. The unknowns are the velocity field $v(x,t)$, the pressure $p(x,t)$, and the deviatoric stress tensor $\sigma(x,t)$, satisfying

$$\frac{\partial v}{\partial t} + (v\cdot\nabla)v = \mathrm{Div}\,\sigma - \nabla p + f, \qquad \mathrm{div}\,v = 0 \quad\text{in }\Omega\times(0,\infty),$$

$$v\big|_{\partial\Omega} = 0, \qquad v\big|_{t=0} = v_0,$$

together with the Jeffreys constitutive law
$$\sigma + \lambda_1\,\frac{D\sigma}{Dt} = 2\eta\Big(E(v) + \lambda_2\,\frac{DE(v)}{Dt}\Big),$$
where $E(v) = \tfrac12(\nabla v + (\nabla v)^\top)$ is the rate-of-strain tensor, $\eta>0$ is the viscosity, $\lambda_1>\lambda_2>0$ are the relaxation and retardation times, $f\in L^2(\Omega)^n$ is a time-independent external force, and $D/Dt$ denotes a suitable objective (e.g., Jaumann or material) time derivative.

For the associated dynamical system on the natural trajectory space of weak solutions, denote by $\mathcal{A}_{tr}$ the trajectory attractor and by $\mathcal{A}_{gl}$ the global attractor (assumed to exist).

Problem: Establish, in every dimension $n\ge 2$ and without imposing any smallness or structural restrictions on the coefficients $\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\eta$, on the external force $f$, or on the initial data $v_0$, finite upper bounds for the Hausdorff dimensions $\dim_H \mathcal{A}_{tr}$ and $\dim_H \mathcal{A}_{gl}$.

$$ (V(x))_k = \sum_{i,j=1}^m P_{ij,k}\, x_i x_j, \qquad k\in E, $$
where the heredity coefficients $\{P_{ij,k}\}$ satisfy
$$ P_{ij,k}\ge 0,\qquad P_{ij,k}=P_{ji,k},\qquad \sum_{k=1}^m P_{ij,k}=1\quad\text{for all }i,j\in E. $$

Consider the subclass of QSOs whose heredity coefficients admit the factorization
$$ P_{ij,k} = a_{ik}\,b_{jk}\qquad \text{for all } i,j,k\in E, $$
for some real matrices $A=(a_{ik})$ and $B=(b_{jk})$ satisfying the symmetry and stochasticity constraints inherited from the conditions on $P_{ij,k}$ (in particular $a_{ik}b_{jk}=a_{jk}b_{ik}$ and $\sum_k a_{ik}b_{jk}=1$). Equivalently, defining the linear maps $A(x)$ and $B(x)$ by $(A(x))_k=\sum_i a_{ik}x_i$ and $(B(x))_k=\sum_j b_{jk}x_j$, one has
$$ (V(x))_k = (A(x))_k\cdot (B(x))_k. $$

Develop a structural and dynamical theory for this class of QSOs. In particular:
(a) Characterize the matrix pairs $(A,B)$ that yield well-defined QSOs of this form.
(b) Determine the fixed points, periodic points, and $\omega$-limit sets of the iterates $V^n$.
(c) Classify the ergodic behavior of trajectories on $S^{m-1}$.
(d) Establish how this class generalizes the class of Volterra QSOs (those with $P_{ij,k}=0$ whenever $k\notin\{i,j\}$).

Consider an incompressible Jeffreys-type viscoelastic fluid occupying a bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ ($n=2$ or $3$) with smooth boundary $\partial\Omega$. The motion is governed by the incompressible Navier–Stokes-type system

$$\rho\bigl(\partial_t v + (v\cdot\nabla)v\bigr) = \operatorname{div}\sigma + f, \qquad \operatorname{div} v = 0,$$

where $v(t,x)$ is the velocity field, $\rho>0$ is the constant density, and $f(t,x)$ is an external body force. The deviatoric stress tensor $\sigma$ is related to the rate-of-strain tensor $E(v) = \tfrac12(\nabla v + (\nabla v)^\top)$ by the Jeffreys constitutive law

$$\sigma + \lambda_1 \frac{D\sigma}{Dt} = 2\eta\Bigl(E(v) + \lambda_2 \frac{DE(v)}{Dt}\Bigr),$$

with positive constants $\eta>0$, $\lambda_1>\lambda_2>0$, where $D/Dt$ denotes a suitable objective (e.g., material or Jaumann) time derivative. The system is supplemented with the no-slip boundary condition $v|_{\partial\Omega}=0$ and initial data $v|_{t=0}=v_0$, $\sigma|_{t=0}=\sigma_0$.

Question: Does there exist, for arbitrary positive coefficients $\rho,\eta,\lambda_1,\lambda_2$ (with $\lambda_1>\lambda_2>0$), arbitrary external force $f$ in a natural function class (e.g., $L^2(0,T;V^*)$ for every $T>0$), and arbitrary initial data $v_0\in H$, $\sigma_0\in L^2(\Omega)$ (where $H$ is the standard space of solenoidal $L^2$ vector fields with vanishing normal trace), at least one generalized (weak) solution $(v,\sigma)$ defined globally in time on $[0,\infty)\times\Omega$, with no smallness or compatibility restrictions imposed on the coefficients, the force, or the initial data?

Global-in-time existence of weak/dissipative solutions has been established for several regularized or modified Jeffreys-type models (e.g., Jeffreys–Oldroyd-α model, integral/memory formulations, autonomous Jeffreys motion equations admitting trajectory and global attractors), without smallness assumptions on data. The problem in its full generality therefore appears partially solved.

representations.normalized:
Let $S^{m-1}=\{x=(x_1,\dots,x_m)\in\mathbb{R}^m:\ x_i\ge 0,\ \sum_{i=1}^m x_i=1\}$ be the $(m-1)$-dimensional simplex. A quadratic stochastic operator (QSO) is a map $V:S^{m-1}\to S^{m-1}$ defined by
$$ (Vx)_k = \sum_{i,j=1}^m P_{ij,k}\, x_i x_j, \qquad k=1,\dots,m, $$
where the heredity coefficients $\{P_{ij,k}\}$ satisfy
$$ P_{ij,k}=P_{ji,k}\ge 0,\qquad \sum_{k=1}^m P_{ij,k}=1\ \ \text{for all }i,j. $$
Two QSOs $V_1,V_2:S^{m-1}\to S^{m-1}$ are called topologically conjugate if there exists a homeomorphism $h:S^{m-1}\to S^{m-1}$ with $h\circ V_1 = V_2\circ h$.

A polynomial $f$ in the variables $\{P_{ij,k}\}$ is called an indicator if the value $f(P_{ij,k})$ is invariant (in a prescribed sense, e.g.\ equal up to specified bounds) under topological conjugacy: that is, whenever the QSOs $V_1$ and $V_2$ with coefficients $\{P^{(1)}_{ij,k}\}$ and $\{P^{(2)}_{ij,k}\}$ are topologically conjugate, $f(P^{(1)}_{ij,k})$ and $f(P^{(2)}_{ij,k})$ satisfy the same imposed constraints.

A finite system $f_1,\dots,f_t$ of indicators is called complete if the matching of values (or bounds) of $f_1,\dots,f_t$ on two QSOs $V_1,V_2$ implies that $V_1$ and $V_2$ are topologically conjugate. A minimal complete system is called a basis.

Problem: Does there exist a finite complete system of indicator polynomials in the heredity coefficients $P_{ij,k}$? If yes, exhibit a basis.

No published resolution of the existence of a finite complete system of indicator polynomials for the topological conjugacy classification of QSOs was found.
