Let $X$ and $Y$ be infinite-dimensional Banach spaces, and let $T:X\to Y$ be a bounded linear operator. For $n\ge 1$, denote by
$$a_n(T)=\inf\{\,\|T-F\|:F:X\to Y\text{ linear, }\operatorname{rank}F<n\,\}$$
the $n$-th approximation number of $T$. For parameters $0<p<\infty$ define the Lorentz-type approximation operator ideal
$$\mathrm{LAPP}_{p,\infty}(X,Y)=\bigl\{\,T\in\mathcal L(X,Y):\sup_{n\ge 1}n^{1/p}\,a_n(T)<\infty\,\bigr\}.$$
Fix two indices $0<r<s<\infty$ with both $r$ and $s$ "large" (in particular $r,s>1$). Exhibit a concrete (explicitly described) bounded linear operator
$$S\in \mathrm{LAPP}_{s,\infty}(X,Y)\setminus \mathrm{LAPP}_{r,\infty}(X,Y),$$
i.e., an operator $S:X\to Y$ for which $\sup_n n^{1/s}a_n(S)<\infty$ but $\sup_n n^{1/r}a_n(S)=\infty$.

Recall the following definitions.

(1) A field $K$ is called radically closed if its multiplicative group $K^{\times}$ is divisible; equivalently, for every $a \in K^{\times}$ and every positive integer $n$, the equation $x^{n}=a$ has a solution in $K$.

(2) A field $K$ is called ample (also large) if every smooth geometrically integral $K$-variety that has a $K$-rational point has a Zariski-dense set of $K$-rational points. Equivalently, every smooth $K$-curve with a $K$-rational point has infinitely many $K$-rational points.

Question: Is every radically closed field ample?

Let $\mathbb{N}_0 = \{0,1,2,\dots\}$. A sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is a linear subspace of the space of bounded scalar sequences indexed by $\mathbb{N}_0$ that is closed under coordinatewise multiplication by bounded sequences (so that the usual ideal property holds). Such a sequence ideal is called a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal if it is equipped with a complete quasi-norm $\|\cdot\|_z$ such that:

(a) the unit-vector basis $(e_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0}$ generates $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ in a suitable sense and the quasi-norm is monotone with respect to the natural pointwise order on nonnegative non-increasing sequences;

(b) shift-monotonicity holds: for every sequence $a=(a_n)\in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ and every $k\geq 0$, the shifted sequence $S_k a = (a_{n+k})$ also belongs to $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ with $\|S_k a\|_z \le \|a\|_z$.

For parameters $0<r<\infty$ and a non-increasing weight $w=(w_n)\in c_0\setminus\ell_1$ with $w_0=1$, the Lorentz-type sequence ideal $d_{r,w}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is defined by
$$d_{r,w}(\mathbb{N}_0) = \Big\{ a=(a_n) : \|a\|_{d_{r,w}} := \Big(\sum_{n=0}^\infty w_n\, a_n^{*\,r}\Big)^{1/r} <\infty \Big\},$$
where $(a_n^*)$ denotes the non-increasing rearrangement of $(|a_n|)$.

For a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ and infinite-dimensional Banach spaces $X$ and $Y$, the operator ideal of approximable operators of type $z$ is
$$\mathrm{LAPP}_z(X,Y) :=  ig\{ T\in \mathcal{L}(X,Y) : (a_n(T))_{n\ge 0} \in z(\mathbb{N}_0)  ig\},$$
endowed with its natural quasi-norm, where $a_n(T)$ denotes the $n$-th approximation number of $T$.

Fix infinite-dimensional Banach spaces $X$ and $Y$. Determine large families $\mathcal{Z}$ of quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideals satisfying:

(i) every Lorentz-type ideal $d_{r,w}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ belongs to $\mathcal{Z}$;

(ii) the assignment $z(\mathbb{N}_0) \mapsto \mathrm{LAPP}_z(X,Y)$ is injective on $\mathcal{Z}$, i.e. distinct members of $\mathcal{Z}$ give rise to distinct operator-ideal components $\mathrm{LAPP}_z(X,Y)$.

Let $X$ be an infinite-dimensional Banach space, and let $\mathcal{L}(X)$ denote the Banach algebra of bounded linear operators on $X$. Denote by $\mathrm{App}(X)$ the closed two-sided ideal of approximable operators on $X$, that is, the closure in the operator norm of the ideal of finite-rank operators on $X$. Let $c_0^*(\mathbb{N})$ denote the operator ideal consisting of all bounded linear operators $T \in \mathcal{L}(X)$ whose sequence of approximation numbers $(a_n(T))_{n=1}^\infty$ tends to $0$, where
$$a_n(T) = \inf\{\|T - F\| : F \in \mathcal{L}(X),\ \mathrm{rank}(F) < n\}.$$
One says that $X$ has few approximable operators if $\mathrm{App}(X)$ is strictly smaller than $c_0^*(\mathbb{N})(X)$ (i.e., there exists a bounded operator on $X$ whose approximation numbers tend to zero but which is not a norm limit of finite-rank operators).

Exhibit an example of an infinite-dimensional Banach space $X$ that simultaneously satisfies:
(i) $X$ contains an infinite unconditional basic sequence; and
(ii) $X$ has few approximable operators, i.e., $\mathrm{App}(X) \subsetneq c_0^*(\mathbb{N})(X)$.

A field $K$ is called ample (or large) if every smooth $K$-curve with a $K$-rational point has infinitely many $K$-rational points; equivalently, $K$ is existentially closed in the Laurent series field $K((t))$. A finite embedding problem over $K$ is a pair $(\alpha\colon \mathrm{Gal}(K)\twoheadrightarrow A,\ f\colon B\twoheadrightarrow A)$ consisting of a continuous surjection from the absolute Galois group of $K$ onto a finite group $A$ and a surjection of finite groups $f\colon B\to A$. The problem is split if $f$ admits a group-theoretic section. A regular solution of such an embedding problem is a Galois extension $F/K(z)$ (with $z$ transcendental over $K$) of group $B$, regular over $K$ (i.e.\ $F\cap \overline{K}=K$), together with an isomorphism $\mathrm{Gal}(F/K(z))\cong B$ compatible with $\alpha$ and $f$ via the canonical surjection $\mathrm{Gal}(K(z))\to \mathrm{Gal}(K)$. The Dèbes–Deschamps conjecture asserts that every finite split embedding problem over every field $K$ has a regular solution.

Question: Does there exist a non-ample field $K$ such that every finite split embedding problem over $K$ admits a regular solution? Equivalently, does there exist a non-ample field $K$ for which the Dèbes–Deschamps conjecture holds?

Background and definitions.

(a) For Banach spaces $E,F$ and $0<r\le 1$, an operator $S\in\mathcal{L}(E,F)$ is called $r$-nuclear if it admits a representation $S=\sum_{i=1}^{\infty} a_i\, x_i^*\otimes y_i$ with $x_i^*\in E^*$, $y_i\in F$, $\|x_i^*\|\le 1$, $\|y_i\|\le 1$, and $(a_i)\in\ell_r$. The class of all $r$-nuclear operators forms a quasi-Banach operator ideal $\mathcal{N}_r$.

(b) Given a Banach space $Z$, the factor ideal $\mathcal{N}_r^{Z}$ consists of all operators $S\in\mathcal{L}(E,F)$ that admit a factorization $S=BTA$ with $A\in\mathcal{L}(E,Z)$, $T\in\mathcal{N}_r(Z,Z)$, $B\in\mathcal{L}(Z,F)$. We write $\mathcal{N}(r,Z)$ for this ideal and $\mathcal{N}(r,Z)(\ell_2)$ for its component on $\ell_2$, i.e. the operators $S\in\mathcal{L}(\ell_2)$ admitting such a factorization through $Z$.

(c) A Banach space $Z$ is called $\mathcal{C}_0$-trivial (in the sense relevant here) if every operator on $Z$ has the form $\lambda I_Z + K$ with $\lambda\in\mathbb{C}$ and $K$ compact, equivalently if the Calkin algebra $\mathcal{L}(Z)/\mathcal{K}(Z)$ is one-dimensional. The Argyros–Haydon construction provides such a Banach space $X_K$ which is moreover a predual of $\ell_1$ and possesses a Schauder basis.

(d) Fix $r=2/3$ and an $\mathcal{C}_0$-trivial Banach space $Z$. For $S\in\mathcal{N}(2/3,Z)(Z,Z)$, choose any factorization $S=\sum_{i} U_i T_i V_i$ with $T_i\in\mathcal{N}_{2/3}(Z,Z)$ such that the canonical scalar $\varphi(U_iV_i)$ (the unique scalar $\lambda_i$ with $U_iV_i-\lambda_i I_Z$ compact, extracted via the trivial Calkin algebra of $Z$) is well defined. Then the formula
$$ \tau_Z(S)\;:=\;\sum_{i} \varphi(U_iV_i)\,\operatorname{tr}(T_i) $$
defines a continuous singular trace on the quasi-Banach operator ideal $\mathcal{N}(2/3,Z)$ (here $\operatorname{tr}$ is the standard nuclear trace on $\mathcal{N}_{2/3}(Z,Z)$, which is well defined because $2/3\le 2/3$).

Problem. Take $Z=X_K$, the $\mathcal{C}_0$-trivial Argyros–Haydon predual of $\ell_1$. Give an explicit description of the restriction of the trace $\tau_{X_K}$ to the ideal $\mathcal{N}(2/3,X_K)(\ell_2)$ of operators on $\ell_2$ that factor (in the sense above) through $X_K$ via a $2/3$-nuclear middle operator. In particular, identify this restriction in terms of standard traces (the operator trace, Dixmier-type singular traces, etc.) on the corresponding ideal in $\mathcal{L}(\ell_2)$.

A holomorphic germ at the origin in one complex variable is a power series f(z) = λz + a_2 z^2 + a_3 z^3 + ⋯ converging in a neighborhood of 0, fixing 0 with multiplier f'(0) = λ. The germ is called elliptic if |λ| = 1 and λ is not a root of unity. The germ f is said to be holomorphically linearizable at 0 if there exists a local biholomorphism φ with φ(0) = 0 such that φ ∘ f ∘ φ^{-1}(z) = λz. Writing λ = e^{2π i θ} with θ ∈ ℝ ∖ ℚ, and letting p_n / q_n denote the convergents of the continued fraction expansion of θ, the number λ (equivalently θ) is said to satisfy the Brjuno condition if
   ∑_{n ≥ 0} (log q_{n+1}) / q_n < ∞.

Consider parameterized families of elliptic germs of the form
   f_{λ, a}(z) = λ z + z^2 g_a(z),
where a ranges over a parameter space M and g_a is holomorphic near 0 with g_a(0) ≠ 0 (in particular, M may be a space of polynomials of fixed degree).

Problem.
(a) Exhibit explicit nontrivial families {f_{λ, a}}_{a ∈ M} of elliptic one-variable holomorphic germs such that, for every a ∈ M, f_{λ, a} is holomorphically linearizable at 0 if and only if λ satisfies the Brjuno condition.

(b) In particular, decide whether the following statement is true: every elliptic polynomial f(z) = λz + a_2 z^2 + ⋯ + a_d z^d (with |λ| = 1, λ not a root of unity, a_d ≠ 0) is holomorphically linearizable at 0 if and only if its multiplier λ is a Brjuno number.

(c) Decide the same question restricted to the cubic case: is every elliptic cubic polynomial f(z) = λz + a_2 z^2 + a_3 z^3 (with a_3 ≠ 0) holomorphically linearizable at 0 if and only if λ is a Brjuno number?

Background and notation. Work in the category of bounded linear operators between (complex) Banach spaces. An operator ideal $\mathfrak{A}$ assigns to every pair of Banach spaces $X,Y$ a linear subspace $\mathfrak{A}(X,Y)\subseteq\mathcal{L}(X,Y)$ that is stable under composition with bounded operators on either side and contains the finite-rank operators. A quasi-Banach operator ideal is an operator ideal equipped with a complete quasi-norm respecting the ideal structure.

For a bounded sequence $(s_n)$ of non-negative reals, the Lorentz quasi-norm of type $(r,\infty)$ is
$$\|(s_n)\|_{r,\infty} := \sup_{n\ge 1} n^{1/r} s_n^*,$$
where $(s_n^*)$ is the non-increasing rearrangement. For an operator $T\in\mathcal{L}(X,Y)$, denote by $a_n(T)$ the $n$-th approximation number
$$a_n(T)=\inf\{\|T-F\|:\ F\in\mathcal{L}(X,Y),\ \mathrm{rank}(F)<n\},$$
and by $x_n(T)$ the $n$-th Weyl number
$$x_n(T)=\sup\{a_n(T A):\ A\in\mathcal{L}(\ell_2,X),\ \|A\|\le 1\}.$$

Define the following quasi-Banach operator ideals:
\begin{itemize}
\item $\mathrm{APP}_{r,\infty}$: operators with $(a_n(T))\in\ell_{r,\infty}$, quasi-normed by $\|T\|_{\mathrm{APP}_{r,\infty}}=\|(a_n(T))\|_{r,\infty}$.
\item $\mathrm{WEYL}_{r,\infty}$: operators with $(x_n(T))\in\ell_{r,\infty}$.
\item $\mathrm{LAPP}_{r,\infty}$ and $\mathrm{LWEYL}_{r,\infty}$: the "left-sided" versions, defined as the components $\mathrm{APP}_{r,\infty}\circ\mathfrak{F}$ and $\mathrm{WEYL}_{r,\infty}\circ\mathfrak{F}$ obtained by composing on the right with arbitrary bounded operators (equivalently, the largest ideals whose Hilbert-space components coincide with those of $\mathrm{APP}_{r,\infty}$ resp. $\mathrm{WEYL}_{r,\infty}$ via factorization through arbitrary Banach spaces on the left and $\ell_2$ on the right).
\item $\mathfrak{H}$: the ideal of operators that factor through some Hilbert space.
\item $\mathrm{LLEX}_{r,\infty} := \mathfrak{H}\circ\mathrm{LWEYL}_{r,\infty}$, the "left-hand extension" ideal.
\end{itemize}

Product ideals are defined componentwise via factorization: $T\in\mathfrak{A}\circ\mathfrak{B}(X,Y)$ iff $T=AB$ with $B\in\mathfrak{B}(X,Z)$, $A\in\mathfrak{A}(Z,Y)$ for some Banach space $Z$.

Problem. Show that the operator ideal $\mathrm{LWEYL}_{2,\infty}\circ\mathrm{APP}_{2,\infty}$ is not contained in $\mathrm{LLEX}_{1,\infty}$. More strongly, show that even
$$\mathrm{LAPP}_{1,\infty}\ \not\subseteq\ \mathrm{LLEX}_{1,\infty}.$$
Equivalently, exhibit Banach spaces $X,Y$ and an operator $T\in\mathrm{LAPP}_{1,\infty}(X,Y)$ that does not admit a factorization $T=A_2 A_1$ with $A_1\in\mathrm{LWEYL}_{1,\infty}$ and $A_2$ factoring through a Hilbert space.

Let $\mathbb{D}$ denote the open unit disk in $\mathbb{C}$. For $\theta\in[0,1)$, let
$$r(\theta)=\inf\{\,r(f)\mid f\in\operatorname{End}(\mathbb{C},0)\text{ is defined and injective on }\mathbb{D}\text{ with }f'(0)=e^{2\pi i\theta}\,\},$$
where $r(f)$ is the radius of convergence of the (formal) linearization of $f$ at $0$ (with the convention that $r(f)=0$ when $f$ is not linearizable).

Let $B:[0,1)\to[0,+\infty]$ be the Brjuno function, defined for irrational $\theta$ by
$$B(\theta)=\sum_{n\ge 0}\beta_{n-1}(\theta)\log\frac{1}{\theta_n},$$
where $\theta_0=\theta$, $\theta_{n+1}=\{1/\theta_n\}$, $\beta_{-1}=1$, and $\beta_n=\theta_0\theta_1\cdots\theta_n$. The Brjuno numbers are precisely those $\theta$ for which $B(\theta)<\infty$, equivalently those for which $r(\theta)>0$.

The function $\theta\mapsto \log r(\theta)+B(\theta)$ is therefore well defined and finite on the set of Brjuno numbers in $[0,1)$.

Question: Does $\log r(\theta)+B(\theta)$ extend from the set of Brjuno numbers in $[0,1)$ to a $\tfrac{1}{2}$-Hölder continuous function on all of $[0,1)$?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

Buff and Chéritat (2006) proved that for quadratic polynomials the analogous function $\log r(\alpha)+Y(\alpha)$ extends continuously to $\mathbb{R}$, but no $1/2$-Hölder continuous extension is known. For the general univalent-germ setting with $r(\theta)$ defined by an infimum over all injective germs on the unit disk, the $1/2$-Hölder regularity question appears to remain open; it is consistent with conjectural "universality up to a 1/2-Hölder function" suggested by Marmi–Moussa–Yoccoz, but no proof is recorded in the literature found.

Setting. Let $\mathfrak{L}$ denote the class of all bounded linear operators acting between arbitrary Banach spaces. An operator ideal $\mathfrak{A}$ is an assignment, to every pair of Banach spaces $(X,Y)$, of a linear subspace $\mathfrak{A}(X,Y) \subseteq \mathfrak{L}(X,Y)$ such that:
(i) every finite-rank operator belongs to $\mathfrak{A}$;
(ii) for all Banach spaces $W,X,Y,Z$ and all $B\in\mathfrak{L}(W,X)$, $A\in\mathfrak{A}(X,Y)$, $C\in\mathfrak{L}(Y,Z)$, the composition $CAB$ lies in $\mathfrak{A}(W,Z)$.

A trace on $\mathfrak{A}$ is a family of linear functionals $\tau_X : \mathfrak{A}(X,X) \to \mathbb{C}$, defined for every Banach space $X$, satisfying:
(a) $\tau_X(\mathrm{id}_X \otimes x^*\otimes x) = \langle x, x^*\rangle$ for all rank-one operators on $X$ (equivalently, $\tau$ extends the standard trace on finite-rank operators);
(b) the trace property: $\tau_Y(AB) = \tau_X(BA)$ whenever $A\in\mathfrak{A}(X,Y)$ and $B\in\mathfrak{L}(Y,X)$ (or, more generally, whenever both compositions lie in the relevant ideal components).

A trace $\tau$ on $\mathfrak{A}$ is said to be non-vanishing if $\tau$ is not identically zero on $\mathfrak{A}$.

It is known that non-vanishing traces exist on certain operator ideals, e.g. on the ideal of nuclear operators (where the spectral / Grothendieck–Lidskii trace need not vanish), and on certain ideals constructed via specific shift-invariant sequence space methods.

Problem. Exhibit operator ideals defined on the class of all Banach spaces, distinct from the previously known examples (the nuclear-type ideals and ideals built from the standard sequence-ideal/shift-invariant-functional construction), that support a non-vanishing trace in the sense above.

Let f: (ℂ,0) → (ℂ,0) be a holomorphic germ fixing the origin, written near 0 as f(z) = λz + O(z²), with multiplier λ = f'(0). Assume that 0 is a Cremer point of f, meaning that |λ| = 1, λ is not a root of unity, and f is not holomorphically (equivalently, formally) linearizable at 0; in particular, f is not holomorphically conjugate to the rotation z ↦ λz on any neighborhood of 0.

For such a germ, define the stable set at 0 by
   K(f) = { z ∈ U : f^n(z) is defined and remains in U for all n ≥ 0 },
where U is a sufficiently small neighborhood of 0; the germ at 0 of K(f) is independent of the choice of U.

Two germs f, g ∈ End(ℂ,0) are said to be topologically locally conjugate if there exists a germ of a homeomorphism h: (ℂ,0) → (ℂ,0) such that h ∘ f = g ∘ h as germs at 0.

Question: Is it true that for any two holomorphic germs f, g ∈ End(ℂ,0) with Cremer points at 0, f and g are topologically locally conjugate if and only if
  (i) their multipliers f'(0) and g'(0) coincide, and
  (ii) the germs at 0 of their stable sets K(f) and K(g) are homeomorphic?

In other words, do the multiplier together with the homeomorphism class of the germ of the stable set form a complete set of topological invariants for local topological conjugacy in the Cremer case?

Setup. Let $\mathbb{N}_0=\{0,1,2,\dots\}$. A sequence ideal $x(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is a linear subspace of the space of scalar sequences indexed by $\mathbb{N}_0$, equipped with a quasi-norm $\|\cdot\|_x$ making it a quasi-Banach space, and satisfying the usual ideal property (it contains all finitely supported sequences and is closed under coordinate-wise multiplication by bounded sequences with $\|(\lambda_n a_n)\|_x\le \sup_n|\lambda_n|\,\|(a_n)\|_x$). It is called shift-monotone if the forward and backward shift operators act boundedly on it and the quasi-norm is monotone with respect to the natural shift partial order (equivalently, $\|(a_{n+1})\|_x\le\|(a_n)\|_x$).

A quasi-Banach operator ideal $\mathfrak{A}=(\mathfrak A(E,F),\|\cdot\|_{\mathfrak A})$ assigns to each pair of Banach spaces $(E,F)$ a linear subspace $\mathfrak A(E,F)$ of bounded operators, complete under a quasi-norm $\|\cdot\|_{\mathfrak A}$ dominating the operator norm, with the usual ideal axioms (containing finite-rank operators and being closed under composition with bounded operators on either side).

For a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal $x(\mathbb{N}_0)$ and a quasi-Banach operator ideal $\mathfrak{A}$, define the approximation procedure $\mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{APP}}_{x}$ as the class of all bounded operators $T:E\to F$ between Banach spaces such that there exists a sequence $(T_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0}$ of operators with $T_n\in\mathfrak A(E,F)$ for all $n$, $\sup_n\|T_n\|_{\mathfrak A}<\infty$, and the sequence of approximation-type numbers $(\|T-T_n\|)_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0}$ belongs to $x(\mathbb{N}_0)$, equipped with the natural quasi-norm
$$\|T\|_{\mathfrak A^{\mathrm{APP}}_x}:=\inf\big\{\max(\sup_n\|T_n\|_{\mathfrak A},\,\|(\|T-T_n\|)_n\|_x)\big\},$$
the infimum running over all such sequences $(T_n)$. Then $\mathfrak A^{\mathrm{APP}}_x$ is again a quasi-Banach operator ideal.

Problem. Prove or disprove: for every quasi-Banach operator ideal $\mathfrak A$ and every pair $x(\mathbb{N}_0)$, $y(\mathbb{N}_0)$ of quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideals, there exists a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ such that the reiteration identity
$$\big(\mathfrak A^{\mathrm{APP}}_x\big)^{\mathrm{APP}}_y \;=\; \mathfrak A^{\mathrm{APP}}_z$$
holds (with equivalent quasi-norms).

A germ of one-variable holomorphic diffeomorphism tangent to the identity is an equivalence class, under agreement near the origin, of holomorphic maps $f:(\mathbb{C},0)\to(\mathbb{C},0)$ whose Taylor expansion at $0$ has the form $f(z)=z+a_{k+1}z^{k+1}+a_{k+2}z^{k+2}+\cdots$ with $k\ge 1$ (so $f'(0)=1$). Two such germs $f$ and $g$ are said to be holomorphically locally conjugate if there exists a germ of biholomorphism $h:(\mathbb{C},0)\to(\mathbb{C},0)$ with $h\circ f = g\circ h$ as germs at $0$.

The Écalle–Voronin theorem provides a complete set of analytic invariants (the multiplicity $k+1$, the residual constant, and the horn-map data) classifying such germs up to holomorphic local conjugacy. However, these invariants are functional moduli, defined via Fatou coordinates, and are not given by a finite computation in the Taylor coefficients.

Problem: Provide an effective and implementable decision procedure that, given two convergent power series $f(z)=z+\sum_{n\ge k+1}a_n z^n$ and $g(z)=z+\sum_{n\ge k+1}b_n z^n$ representing germs tangent to the identity (specified by an algorithm producing their Taylor coefficients to arbitrary order, together with explicit bounds expressing convergence), decides in finite time whether $f$ and $g$ are holomorphically locally conjugate.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The classification of one-variable parabolic germs up to holomorphic local conjugacy is given by the Écalle–Voronin functional moduli (multiplicity, residual constant, and horn maps). While numerical schemes (e.g., resurgent/Borel-summation methods, parabolic renormalization) can compute these invariants as convergent series, we found no published work providing a finite, effective decision procedure that takes two tangent-to-identity germs as input and decides holomorphic local conjugacy. The problem appears to remain open.

Setup. Let $\mathbb{N}_0 = \{0,1,2,\dots\}$ and let $c_{00}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ denote the space of eventually zero scalar sequences indexed by $\mathbb{N}_0$. A quasi-normed sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is a linear subspace of the space of bounded sequences containing $c_{00}(\mathbb{N}_0)$, equipped with a quasi-norm $\|\cdot\,|z\|$ that makes it complete (or at least quasi-normed) and that satisfies the ideal property: for every $\xi=(\xi_n)\in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ and every bounded sequence $(\lambda_n)$, the pointwise product $(\lambda_n\xi_n)$ belongs to $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ with $\|(\lambda_n\xi_n)\,|z\|\le \sup_n|\lambda_n|\cdot\|\xi\,|z\|$.

For $k\in\mathbb{N}_0$ let $\sigma_k:\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}_0}\to\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}_0}$ denote the right-shift defined by $(\sigma_k\xi)_n=\xi_{n-k}$ for $n\ge k$ and $(\sigma_k\xi)_n=0$ for $n<k$. The ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is called shift-monotone if $\sigma_k$ maps $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ into itself for every $k\ge 0$ and the operator quasi-norms $c_k:=\|\sigma_k:z\to z\|$ satisfy $c_k\to 0$ as well as $c_0=1$ (more precisely, the standard shift-monotonicity assumption $\|\sigma_k\xi\,|z\|\le c_k\|\xi\,|z\|$ with $c_k\downarrow 0$ as $k\to\infty$ -- equivalently, the canonical embedding $z(\mathbb{N}_0)\hookrightarrow c_0$ is bounded and shifts contract suitably).

Approximation numbers. For Banach spaces $X,Y$ and a bounded linear operator $S:X\to Y$, the $n$-th approximation number is
$$a_n(S):=\inf\{\|S-L\|: L:X\to Y \text{ linear, } \mathrm{rank}\,L<n\}, \qquad n\in\mathbb{N}.$$
Set $\alpha_n(S):=a_{n+1}(S)$ for $n\in\mathbb{N}_0$, so that $\alpha_0(S)=\|S\|\ge \alpha_1(S)\ge \alpha_2(S)\ge\cdots$.

The approximation operator ideal associated with $z$. Define
$$\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z(X,Y):=\{S\in\mathcal{L}(X,Y): (\alpha_n(S))_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0}\in z(\mathbb{N}_0)\}$$
and equip it with the quasi-norm
$$\|S\,|\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z\|:=\bigl\|(\alpha_n(S))_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0}\,\bigm|\,z\bigr\|.$$
A second quasi-norm is defined by means of finite-rank approximations: with $\mathcal{F}_{<n}(X,Y)$ the set of bounded linear operators of rank strictly less than $n$,
$$|||S\,|\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z|||:=\bigl\|(\beta_n(S))_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0}\,\bigm|\,z\bigr\|, \quad \text{where } \beta_n(S):=\inf\{\|S-L\|: L\in\mathcal{F}_{<n+1}(X,Y)\text{ attains a rank-}n\text{ optimal-type form}\},$$
the second quantity being the natural "ideal-internal" quasi-norm obtained by replacing the scalar infimum defining $\alpha_n$ with the $z$-quasi-norm of the residual sequences; equivalently,
$$|||S\,|\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z|||:=\inf\bigl\{\bigl\|(\|S-L_n\|)_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0}\,\bigm|\,z\bigr\|: L_n\in\mathcal{F}_{<n+1}(X,Y)\bigr\}.$$

It is known that $\|\cdot\,|\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z\|$ and $|||\cdot\,|\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z|||$ are equivalent quasi-norms on $\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z(X,Y)$ for every quasi-normed shift-monotone sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$.

Problem. Exhibit a quasi-normed shift-monotone sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$, Banach spaces $X,Y$, and an operator $S\in\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z(X,Y)$ for which the two quasi-norms are not equal, that is,
$$\|S\,|\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z\|\;\neq\;|||S\,|\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z|||.$$
Equivalently, determine whether the two equivalent quasi-norms can fail to coincide, and produce an explicit example if so.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

The complexity of computing the RNNI distance has been resolved: Collienne and Gavryushkin (published 2021) gave an O(n^2)-time algorithm (FINDPATH) for computing shortest paths in the RNNI graph, and the same approach extends to RNNIu. However, related variants remain hard: with rank moves only (RNNI(0)) the problem is NP-hard, and the complexity for the full DtTm and DtTum graphs (which include integer length moves on event intervals) does not appear to have been settled. Thus the original problem is partially solved.

Let $f:(\mathbb{C}^n,O)\to(\mathbb{C}^n,O)$ be a holomorphic germ fixing the origin, and assume $f$ is non-invertible (i.e.\ its differential at $O$ is not invertible) and dominant (i.e.\ its Jacobian determinant does not vanish identically). Denote by $\mathfrak{m}\subset\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{C}^n,O}$ the maximal ideal of the local ring of holomorphic germs at $O$, and for any holomorphic germ $g:(\mathbb{C}^n,O)\to(\mathbb{C}^n,O)$ define the order
$$c(g)=\min\{\,k\geq 0 : g^*\mathfrak{m}\not\subset\mathfrak{m}^{k+1}\,\}=\sup\{\,k\geq 0 : g^*\mathfrak{m}\subset\mathfrak{m}^{k}\,\}.$$
For the iterates $f^k=f\circ\cdots\circ f$ ($k$ times) one has the submultiplicativity $c(f^{k+l})\geq c(f^k)\,c(f^l)$, which guarantees that the asymptotic attraction rate
$$c_\infty(f)=\lim_{k\to+\infty} c(f^k)^{1/k}\in[1,+\infty)$$
exists.

Prove or disprove the following two statements:

(a) The number $c_\infty(f)$ is an algebraic integer of degree at most $n$; that is, there exist integers $a_0,a_1,\dots,a_{n-1}\in\mathbb{Z}$ such that
$$c_\infty(f)^n + a_{n-1}\,c_\infty(f)^{n-1}+\cdots+a_1\,c_\infty(f)+a_0 = 0.$$

(b) There exists a constant $\delta\in(0,1]$ (depending on $f$) such that
$$\delta\,c_\infty(f)^k \leq c(f^k) \leq c_\infty(f)^k\qquad\text{for every integer } k\geq 1.$$

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

For $n=2$, work of Favre–Jonsson on eigenvaluations established that $c_\infty(f)$ is a quadratic integer and the two-sided estimate holds. In higher dimensions $n\geq 3$, only partial generalizations are known (e.g., for monomial or rigid germs, by Favre, Jonsson, Ruggiero and collaborators), and the general algebraicity and lower-bound questions appear to remain open.

Let L be a fixed finite leaf set with |L| = n. A discrete time-tree on L is a rooted phylogenetic tree with leaves bijectively labelled by L, in which each internal node is assigned an integer "time" (rank) such that times strictly increase along every path from a leaf to the root. Consider the following four graphs whose vertices are such trees:

• DtT: discrete time-trees on L, where each internal node carries a positive integer time and ties between non-adjacent nodes are allowed.
• DtTu: the analogue of DtT in which all leaves are required to have time 0 ("ultrametric"/coalescent-style).
• RNNI: ranked nearest-neighbour-interchange graph, whose vertices are discrete time-trees in which the n−1 internal nodes have distinct ranks 1,…,n−1.
• RNNIu: the ultrametric variant of RNNI.

In each of these graphs, edges are given by the natural local moves: an NNI-style move that exchanges two subtrees adjacent to an interval between consecutive-rank internal nodes, and a "rank move" that swaps the ranks of two internal nodes whose ranks differ by one (plus, in DtT/DtTu, moves that change an integer time by one, when permitted). Distance d(T,R) is the length of a shortest path in the graph.

Given a tree T on L and an internal edge e of T, removing e disconnects T into two components and induces a bipartition (split) of L. Two trees T and R are said to share a split σ if each of them has an internal edge inducing the bipartition σ.

Question. Let G be any one of DtT, DtTu, RNNI, RNNIu. Suppose T and R are two vertices of G that share a split σ. Must every shortest path from T to R in G consist entirely of trees that also display σ?

A counterexample to the conjectured Split Theorem in the RNNI graph was found by Collienne (reported on the bioAI lab page describing Collienne's RNNI geometry paper). Thus the strong split-preservation statement is false in RNNI; a weaker version remains plausible but is not established.

Let $f=(f_1,\dots,f_n)\colon (\mathbb{C}^n,O)\to(\mathbb{C}^n,O)$ be a holomorphic germ fixing the origin, and define its order at the origin by
$$c(f)=\min\bigl\{\,\mathrm{ord}_O(f_j) \,:\, j=1,\dots,n\,\bigr\},$$
where $\mathrm{ord}_O(f_j)$ is the lowest degree of a non-zero homogeneous term in the Taylor expansion of $f_j$ at $O$. Assume that $f$ is dominant (i.e.\ its Jacobian determinant does not vanish identically) and non-invertible (i.e.\ $c(f)\ge 2$). For each positive integer $k$ let $f^k=f\circ\cdots\circ f$ denote the $k$-fold iterate, and consider the integer sequence $\{c(f^k)\}_{k\in\mathbb{N}}$.

Question: Does there exist an integer $K\ge 1$, an integer $r\ge 1$, and integers $a_1,\dots,a_r$ such that
$$c(f^{k+r}) = a_1\,c(f^{k+r-1}) + a_2\,c(f^{k+r-2}) + \cdots + a_r\,c(f^{k})$$
holds for all $k\ge K$? In other words, must the sequence $\{c(f^k)\}_{k\in\mathbb{N}}$ eventually satisfy a linear recurrence relation with integer coefficients?

Consider a single-server queue with finite capacity K (the GI/G/1/K queue): customers arrive according to a renewal process with i.i.d. inter-arrival times having mean 1/λ, variance σ_a², and squared coefficient of variation c_a² = λ²σ_a²; service times are i.i.d. with mean 1/μ, variance σ_s², and squared coefficient of variation c_s² = μ²σ_s²; arrivals finding K customers in the system are lost. Assume the system is critically loaded, i.e. ρ = λ/μ = 1. Let D(t) denote the number of departures (served customers) in [0, t], and define the asymptotic variance rate

   V_K = lim_{t → ∞} Var(D(t)) / t,

and the normalized variability parameter γ_K* = V_K / μ. It has been conjectured that, under suitable distributional assumptions on the inter-arrival and service time distributions,

   γ_K* = (1/3)(c_a² + c_s²) + O(1/K)   as K → ∞.

The original conjecture is stated under the assumption that both the inter-arrival and service distributions possess a finite exponential moment (i.e., are light-tailed). The problem is the following:

(a) Determine the weakest distributional assumptions on the inter-arrival and service time distributions under which the asymptotic formula above holds.

(b) In particular, decide whether the existence of 2+ε moments (for some ε > 0) on both inter-arrival and service time distributions is sufficient for the formula to hold, or whether some strictly stronger condition (weaker than an exponential moment but stronger than 2+ε moments) is necessary.

Consider a GI/G/1/K queue: a single-server queue with renewal inter-arrival times, i.i.d. service times independent of the arrivals, FCFS discipline, and a finite buffer of size K (so that arrivals finding K customers in the system are lost). Assume the queue is critically loaded, i.e., the traffic intensity ρ = E[S]/E[T] equals 1, where T and S denote a generic inter-arrival and service time. Let D(t) denote the number of departures from the system in [0,t], and define

  γ*(t) := Var(D(t))/t,   γ* := lim_{t→∞} γ*(t),

assumed to exist for the distributions under consideration. A widely studied phenomenon (the BRAVO effect — "Balancing Reduces Asymptotic Variance of Outputs") is captured by the conjecture that, for critically loaded GI/G/1/K queues with light-tailed inter-arrival and service distributions,

  γ* = (1/3)(Var(T)/E[T]^3 + Var(S)/E[S]^3) · E[S] + o_K(1),  with o_K(1) = O(1/K) as K → ∞.

Empirically, simulations with heavy-tailed Weibull service times, as well as light-tailed services, are consistent with this 1/3 BRAVO factor, while simulations with Lognormal or Pareto service distributions appear to deviate, displaying a BRAVO effect but with an apparently different multiplicative constant.

Problem. For critically loaded GI/G/1/K queues with Lognormal or Pareto service-time distributions, determine which of the following explains the observed deviation from the 1/3 BRAVO conjecture:
(a) the convergence γ*(t) → γ* as t → ∞ is genuinely much slower than for light-tailed and Weibull cases (so that finite-time simulations have not yet entered the asymptotic regime);
(b) the finite-buffer correction term o_K(1) above vanishes substantially more slowly than 1/K as K → ∞ for these distributions;
(c) the limiting asymptotic constant γ* itself differs from the conjectured (1/3)(Var(T)/E[T]^3 + Var(S)/E[S]^3)·E[S] for these distributions.

Identify which of (a), (b), (c) (possibly more than one) is responsible, and quantify the corresponding rates of convergence in t and in K.

representations.normalized:
Let $\mathrm{End}(\mathbb{C}^n, O)$ denote the set of germs at the origin of holomorphic self-maps $f:(\mathbb{C}^n,O)\to(\mathbb{C}^n,O)$ fixing the origin. A germ $f \in \mathrm{End}(\mathbb{C}^n,O)$ is called superattracting at $O$ if its differential $df_O$ vanishes. The critical set $\mathrm{Crit}(f)$ is the analytic germ at $O$ where the Jacobian determinant of $f$ vanishes, and the postcritical set is
$$\mathrm{PCrit}(f) \;=\; \bigcup_{k\ge 1} f^k(\mathrm{Crit}(f)),$$
viewed as a germ at $O$. Define the critical multiplicity $c(f)$ as the order of vanishing at $O$ of the Jacobian determinant of $f$.

Two germs $f, g \in \mathrm{End}(\mathbb{C}^n,O)$ are said to be locally topologically (respectively, holomorphically) conjugate if there exists a germ of homeomorphism (respectively, biholomorphism) $\varphi:(\mathbb{C}^n,O)\to(\mathbb{C}^n,O)$ such that $\varphi \circ f = g \circ \varphi$. Two postcritical sets are said to be topologically (respectively, holomorphically) conjugate if there exists a germ of homeomorphism (respectively, biholomorphism) of $(\mathbb{C}^n,O)$ sending one onto the other.

Question: Let $f, g \in \mathrm{End}(\mathbb{C}^n, O)$ be superattracting germs with $c(f) = c(g)$. Is it true that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ and $g$ are locally topologically conjugate if and only if $\mathrm{PCrit}(f)$ and $\mathrm{PCrit}(g)$ are topologically conjugate; and
\item $f$ and $g$ are locally holomorphically conjugate if and only if $\mathrm{PCrit}(f)$ and $\mathrm{PCrit}(g)$ are holomorphically conjugate?
\end{enumerate}

Consider a single-server queue (for example, the M/M/1 queue, or more generally a GI/G/1 queue) with arrival rate λ and service rate μ, and let ρ = λ/μ denote the traffic intensity. Let D(t) denote the number of departures (served customers) up to time t. Define the asymptotic variance rate of the departure process as

  V = lim_{t→∞} Var(D(t)) / t,

assuming the limit exists. It is known that for a wide class of single-server queues, V exhibits a striking drop precisely at the critical load ρ = 1: as ρ → 1, V is strictly smaller than what would be predicted by either the stable regime (ρ < 1, where departures inherit the variability of arrivals) or the overloaded regime (ρ > 1, where departures inherit the variability of service). This sharp reduction of long-run output variability at criticality is known as the BRAVO (Balancing Reduces Asymptotic Variance of Outputs) phenomenon.

Problem. Provide a complete and conceptually satisfying intuitive explanation of the BRAVO phenomenon for basic single-server queues. The explanation should clarify, in qualitative and mechanistic terms, why critically balancing the arrival and service rates causes the asymptotic variance rate of the departure process to be strictly smaller than in the off-critical regimes, and should account for the universality of the effect across different single-server models (M/M/1, GI/G/1, etc.).

Let $\mathrm{End}(\mathbb{C}^n,O)$ denote the set of germs at the origin of holomorphic self-maps $f\colon(\mathbb{C}^n,O)\to(\mathbb{C}^n,O)$ fixing the origin. Write $f$ as a formal power series $f(z)=\sum_{|\alpha|\ge 1}a_\alpha z^\alpha$ with $a_\alpha\in\mathbb{C}^n$, and define the order of $f$ at $O$ as $\nu(f):=\min\{|\alpha|:a_\alpha\neq 0\}$. The germ $f$ is called superattracting at $O$ if $df_O=0$, equivalently $\nu(f)\ge 2$.

Two germs $f,g\in\mathrm{End}(\mathbb{C}^n,O)$ are formally conjugate if there exists a formal invertible change of coordinates $\varphi\in\widehat{\mathrm{Diff}}(\mathbb{C}^n,O)$ (a formal power-series map with $\varphi(O)=O$ and invertible linear part) such that $\varphi\circ f=g\circ\varphi$ as formal power series.

Problem. Provide a complete classification, up to formal conjugacy, of the superattracting germs $f\in\mathrm{End}(\mathbb{C}^n,O)$ in each of the following two cases:
(a) $n\ge 3$ and $\nu(f)=2$;
(b) $n=2$ and $\nu(f)=3$.

That is, exhibit a list of formal normal forms such that every superattracting germ in the indicated class is formally conjugate to exactly one (or to one in a specified equivalence family) of these normal forms, and determine the moduli.

Consider the Sturm–Liouville boundary value problem L(q,α,β) on the interval (0,1) defined by

   -y''(x) + q(x) y(x) = λ y(x),   x ∈ (0,1),

with real-valued potential q ∈ L^1(0,1) and separated boundary conditions

   y(0) cos α + y'(0) sin α = 0,    y(1) cos β + y'(1) sin β = 0,

where α ∈ [0,π) and β ∈ (0,π]. For each n ≥ 1, let y_n denote a real-valued eigenfunction associated with the n-th eigenvalue λ_n, and let X_n = { x_{n,k} : k = 1,…,n−1 } ⊂ (0,1) denote its set of interior nodal points (zeros). Set X = ⋃_{n≥1} X_n.

Fix b ∈ (1/2, 1]. Suppose one is given a subset W ⊂ X ∩ (0,b) that is dense in (0,b) (but not necessarily satisfying the stronger s-dense condition, namely that for every x ∈ (0,b) there is a sequence x_{n_j,k_j} ∈ W with x_{n_j,k_j} → x and k_j/n_j → x).

Given two such problems L(q,α,β) and L(q̃,α̃,β̃) sharing the same dense nodal subset W in (0,b) (in the sense that the corresponding nodal points coincide on W), determine whether the left boundary parameter is forced to coincide, i.e. whether α = α̃.

A holomorphic germ $f:(\mathbb{C}^n,0)\to(\mathbb{C}^n,0)$ is called dominant if its Jacobian determinant does not vanish identically, and non-invertible if $df_0$ is not invertible. Define the generalized critical set of $f$ as $C^\infty(f)=\bigcup_{k\ge 1} C(f^k)$, where $C(f^k)$ is the critical set of the $k$-th iterate. The germ $f$ is called rigid if:
(i) $C^\infty(f)$ has at most simple normal crossings at $0$, and
(ii) $C^\infty(f)$ is totally invariant under $f$, i.e. $f^{-1}(C^\infty(f))\subseteq C^\infty(f)$ as germs.

Problem: Provide a complete classification, up to holomorphic conjugacy, of rigid non-invertible dominant holomorphic germs $f:(\mathbb{C}^3,0)\to(\mathbb{C}^3,0)$ (i.e. produce a list of normal forms exhausting all conjugacy classes of such germs in complex dimension three).

Consider the Sturm–Liouville eigenvalue problem on [0,1]:

  -y''(x) + q(x) y(x) = λ y(x),  x ∈ (0,1),
  y'(0) - h y(0) = 0,   y'(1) + H y(1) = 0,

where q ∈ L^1(0,1) is real-valued and h, H ∈ ℝ. The problem has a discrete spectrum of real eigenvalues λ_1 < λ_2 < ⋯, with corresponding eigenfunctions y_n having exactly n-1 zeros (nodes) 0 < x_1^{(n)} < x_2^{(n)} < ⋯ < x_{n-1}^{(n)} < 1 in (0,1). Let X(q,h,H) = { x_k^{(n)} : n ≥ 2, 1 ≤ k ≤ n-1 } denote the full set of nodal points.

For a fixed b ∈ (0,1), a subset S ⊂ (0,b) of nodal points of (q,h,H) is called twin and dense in (0,b) if S is dense in (0,b) and there exist infinitely many indices n for which two consecutive nodes x_k^{(n)}, x_{k+1}^{(n)} both lie in S.

Question. Suppose b ∈ (0, 1/2], and suppose (q,h,H) and (q̃, h̃, H̃) are two such Sturm–Liouville triples whose nodal sets in (0,b) share a common twin dense subset (with matching index conditions of the standard inverse nodal setup). Does it follow that q − ⟨q⟩ = q̃ − ⟨q̃⟩ on (0,1) (where ⟨q⟩ := ∫_0^1 q) and that h = h̃, H = H̃? Equivalently, can nodal observations restricted to a left subinterval (0,b) with b ≤ 1/2 determine the potential (up to its mean) and the boundary parameters?

Let $\mathrm{End}(\mathbb{C}^3,O)$ denote the set of holomorphic germs $f:(\mathbb{C}^3,O)\to(\mathbb{C}^3,O)$ fixing the origin. A modification based at $O$ is a proper holomorphic map $\pi:\widetilde{M}\to(\mathbb{C}^3,O)$ from a smooth complex 3-fold $\widetilde{M}$ which is a biholomorphism away from the exceptional divisor $E=\pi^{-1}(O)$. Given $f\in\mathrm{End}(\mathbb{C}^3,O)$, a lift of $f$ over $\pi$ at a point $p\in E$ is a holomorphic germ $\widetilde{f}\in\mathrm{End}(\widetilde{M},p)$ satisfying $\pi\circ\widetilde{f}=f\circ\pi$.

For a holomorphic germ $g\in\mathrm{End}(X,p)$ on a smooth complex manifold, let $C(g)$ denote the critical set of $g$ and let the generalized critical set be $C^\infty(g)=\bigcup_{n\ge 1} C(g^n)$. The germ $g$ is called rigid if $C^\infty(g)$ (as a germ at $p$) is either empty or a divisor with simple normal crossings at $p$ that is totally invariant under $g$, i.e.\ $g^{-1}(C^\infty(g))\subseteq C^\infty(g)$ as germs. The germ $g$ is called weakly rigid if these conditions hold up to allowing a non-totally-invariant but well-controlled component (the standard weakening used in the rigidification program).

Determine explicit conditions on $f\in\mathrm{End}(\mathbb{C}^3,O)$ which guarantee the existence of a modification $\pi:\widetilde{M}\to(\mathbb{C}^3,O)$ based at $O$, a point $p\in E=\pi^{-1}(O)$, and a (possibly weakly) rigid holomorphic germ $\widetilde{f}\in\mathrm{End}(\widetilde{M},p)$ such that $\pi\circ\widetilde{f}=f\circ\pi$.

representations.normalized:
Let $f:(\mathbb{C}^n,0)\to(\mathbb{C}^n,0)$ be a holomorphic germ tangent to the identity at the origin, that is, $f(z)=z+P_\nu(z)+P_{\nu+1}(z)+\cdots$, where $P_k$ is a homogeneous polynomial map of degree $k$ and $\nu\geq 2$ is the order of $f-\mathrm{id}$. The stable set of $f$ is defined as
\[ \mathcal{S}(f)=\{z\in U : f^{\circ k}(z)\in U\text{ for all }k\geq 0,\text{ and }f^{\circ k}(z)\to 0\text{ as }k\to\infty\}, \]
for some neighborhood $U$ of the origin.

A characteristic direction of $f$ is a point $[v]\in\mathbb{P}^{n-1}(\mathbb{C})$ such that $P_\nu(v)=\lambda\,v$ for some $\lambda\in\mathbb{C}$; it is called non-degenerate if $\lambda\neq 0$ and degenerate if $\lambda=0$. Attached to each non-degenerate characteristic direction $[v]$ are its directors (the eigenvalues of a naturally defined linear endomorphism on $T_{[v]}\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$ that arises from the linearization of the induced map on the exceptional divisor of the blow-up of the origin) and its index (a residual index in the sense of Camacho–Sad / Abate).

Problem. Give a complete description of the stable set $\mathcal{S}(f)$ of an arbitrary holomorphic germ $f:(\mathbb{C}^n,0)\to(\mathbb{C}^n,0)$ tangent to the identity, expressed in terms of its characteristic directions, the directors and indices attached to them, and, where these prove insufficient, identify the further holomorphic/dynamical invariants of $f$ that are required in order to capture the full structure of $\mathcal{S}(f)$.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The problem of describing the stable set of a germ tangent to the identity in C^n via characteristic directions, directors, indices and additional invariants remains an active area of research. Partial results exist (Hakim's theorem on parabolic manifolds for non-degenerate directions with suitable directors, Abate's theorem in dimension 2, work of Arizzi–Raissy, Vivas, Rong, Lapan on degenerate directions, and recent work of Mongodi and collaborators on germs without non-degenerate directions in C^3), but no complete description is known in general.

representations.normalized:
Let $X$ be a homogeneous holomorphic vector field of degree $\nu\ge 2$ on $\mathbb{C}^2$, and consider the associated "geodesic-type" vector field on a chart with coordinates $(z,v)$ given by
$$G \;=\; g_1(z)\,v\,\frac{\partial}{\partial z} \;+\; (\nu-1)\,g_2(z)\,v^2\,\frac{\partial}{\partial v},$$
where $g_1,g_2$ are holomorphic functions of $z$ obtained from $X$ via the standard projectivization/blow-up construction (so that integral curves of $G$ project to geodesics of $X$ on the projective line at infinity). For $\zeta_0\in\mathbb{C}$, let
$$\mu_1(\zeta_0) := \operatorname{ord}_{z=\zeta_0} g_1(z), \qquad \mu_2(\zeta_0) := \operatorname{ord}_{z=\zeta_0} g_2(z),$$
and call $(\zeta_0,0)$ an irregular singularity of $G$ when
$$\mu_1(\zeta_0) \;>\; \mu_2(\zeta_0) + 1.$$
Describe the local dynamics of $G$ in a neighborhood of an irregular singularity $(\zeta_0,0)$: in particular, classify the topological/analytic behavior of orbits, separatrices, and any normal forms or invariants that govern the flow near such a point.

Let $n\ge 2$ and let $\lambda=(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n)\in\mathbb{C}^n$. For an integer $m\ge 2$ define
$$\Omega_\lambda(m)=\min\bigl\{\,|\lambda_1^{k_1}\cdots\lambda_n^{k_n}-\lambda_j|\;:\; k_1,\dots,k_n\in\mathbb{N},\;2\le k_1+\cdots+k_n\le m,\;1\le j\le n,\;\lambda_1^{k_1}\cdots\lambda_n^{k_n}\ne\lambda_j\,\bigr\}.$$
Assume that
$$\sum_{k=0}^{+\infty}\frac{1}{2^k}\,\log\frac{1}{\Omega_\lambda(2^{k+1})}=+\infty,$$
i.e.\ the multivariable Brjuno-type series associated with $\lambda$ diverges.

Let $\mathrm{End}(\mathbb{C}^n,O)$ denote the set of germs at the origin of holomorphic self-maps of $\mathbb{C}^n$ fixing $O$. A germ $f\in\mathrm{End}(\mathbb{C}^n,O)$ is said to be formally linearizable if there exists a formal power series tangent to the identity that conjugates $f$ to its linear part $df_O$, and holomorphically linearizable if such a conjugation can be chosen to be a convergent (holomorphic) germ at $O$.

Question: Does there exist a germ $f\in\mathrm{End}(\mathbb{C}^n,O)$ whose differential $df_O$ is diagonalizable with eigenvalues $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n$, such that $f$ is formally linearizable but not holomorphically linearizable?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The question is the multivariable analogue of Yoccoz's theorem on the necessity of the Brjuno condition. In one variable, Yoccoz proved necessity; in several variables, sufficiency results (under the reduced Brjuno / Rüssmann condition) are known due to Brjuno, Rüssmann, and Raissy, but the necessity of the multivariable Brjuno-type condition remains, to the best of available evidence, an open problem. Recent surveys on small divisors in discrete local holomorphic dynamics still list this as an outstanding open problem.

Setup. Let $n\ge 2$ and let $\vec\lambda=(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n)\in(\mathbb{C}^*)^n$ be non-resonant, meaning that $\lambda^Q:=\lambda_1^{q_1}\cdots\lambda_n^{q_n}\ne \lambda_j$ for every multi-index $Q=(q_1,\dots,q_n)\in\mathbb{N}^n$ with $|Q|=q_1+\cdots+q_n\ge 2$ and every $j\in\{1,\dots,n\}$. For $m\ge 2$ define
$$\Omega_{\vec\lambda}(m)=\min\{\,|\lambda^Q-\lambda_j|\;:\; 2\le |Q|\le m,\;1\le j\le n\,\}.$$
Say that $\vec\lambda$ satisfies the multivariable Brjuno condition if
$$\sum_{k\ge 0} 2^{-k}\log\frac{1}{\Omega_{\vec\lambda}(2^{k+1})}<+\infty. \quad (\ast)$$

Let $\mathrm{End}(\mathbb{C}^n,O)$ denote germs of holomorphic self-maps of $\mathbb{C}^n$ fixing the origin. A germ $f\in\mathrm{End}(\mathbb{C}^n,O)$ with $df_O=\mathrm{diag}(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n)$ is holomorphically linearizable if there exists a germ of biholomorphism $\varphi$ at $O$, tangent to the identity, such that $\varphi^{-1}\circ f\circ\varphi(z)=(\lambda_1 z_1,\dots,\lambda_n z_n)$. Non-resonance ensures that such an $f$ is always formally linearizable.

Problems.
(a) For each non-resonant $\vec\lambda\in(\mathbb{C}^*)^n$, construct a family $\{f_{\vec\lambda,a}\}_{a\in M}\subset\mathrm{End}(\mathbb{C}^n,O)$ of formally linearizable germs with $df_{\vec\lambda,a}|_O=\mathrm{diag}(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n)$, with the property that $f_{\vec\lambda,a}$ is holomorphically linearizable for every (equivalently, for some non-trivial) $a\in M$ if and only if $\vec\lambda$ satisfies $(\ast)$.

(b) Prove or disprove the following sharp version in dimension two: for every non-resonant pair $(\lambda_1,\lambda_2)\in(\mathbb{C}^*)^2$ and every pair $Q=(Q_1,Q_2)$ of homogeneous quadratic polynomials in $(z_1,z_2)$ with $Q\not\equiv 0$, the germ
$$f(z_1,z_2)=(\lambda_1 z_1,\lambda_2 z_2)+Q(z_1,z_2)$$
is holomorphically linearizable if and only if $(\lambda_1,\lambda_2)$ satisfies the multivariable Brjuno condition $(\ast)$.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

A search for results on multivariable Brjuno conditions and holomorphic linearization of non-resonant quadratic germs in dimension two did not produce a definitive proof or disproof of the sharp equivalence stated. The sufficiency of multivariable Brjuno-type (Brjuno–Rüssmann) conditions for linearization is classical, but no source confirms that the multivariable Brjuno condition is necessary for holomorphic linearization of all non-resonant quadratic perturbations, nor an explicit sharp family realizing the equivalence. The problem appears to remain open.

Let $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$ be such that $1,\alpha,\beta$ are linearly independent over $\mathbb{Q}$. Consider the 2-plane
$$E(\alpha,\beta)=\{(x,y,\alpha x+\beta y):x,y\in\mathbb{R}\}\subset\mathbb{R}^3,$$
and let $E^{\perp}(\alpha,\beta)$ denote its orthogonal complement. The canonical cut-and-project set $Y(\alpha,\beta)\subset E(\alpha,\beta)$ is defined by
$$Y(\alpha,\beta)=\{\pi_1(z):z\in\mathbb{Z}^3,\ \pi_2(z)\in W\},$$
where $\pi_1,\pi_2$ are the orthogonal projections of $\mathbb{R}^3$ onto $E(\alpha,\beta)$ and $E^{\perp}(\alpha,\beta)$ respectively, and $W=\pi_2([0,1]^3)$ is the canonical window.

For a finite set $\Omega\subset E(\alpha,\beta)$ (a "shape"), and for $y\in Y(\alpha,\beta)$, the patch of $Y(\alpha,\beta)$ of shape $\Omega$ at $y$ is $(y+\Omega)\cap Y(\alpha,\beta)$; two such patches are said to be of the same type (type-2 equivalence) if one is a translate of the other by an element of $E(\alpha,\beta)$ inducing the same combinatorial pattern. Each patch type has a well-defined asymptotic frequency in $Y(\alpha,\beta)$. Let $\xi_{(\alpha,\beta)}(\Omega)$ denote the set of distinct frequencies that occur for patches of shape $\Omega$ in $Y(\alpha,\beta)$.

Let $\mathcal{S}$ denote the collection of all "aligned squares" in $E(\alpha,\beta)$, i.e. shapes consisting of the four corners of a square whose sides are parallel to the projections of two of the standard basis vectors of $\mathbb{R}^3$ onto $E(\alpha,\beta)$.

Question: Does there exist a choice of $\alpha,\beta$ as above such that
$$\sup_{\Omega\in\mathcal{S}}\#\xi_{(\alpha,\beta)}(\Omega)=+\infty?$$

Call a rectangle $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ aligned if its sides are parallel to the coordinate axes. For such an aligned rectangle $\Omega$, partition $\Omega$ into the equivalence classes of the relation $x\sim y\iff (x+\pi_\perp(\Lambda^*))\cap\Omega=(y+\pi_\perp(\Lambda^*))\cap\Omega$, where $\Lambda^*=\Lambda\setminus\{0\}$; equivalently, consider the patches of $Y(\Omega)$ seen through translates of the window. $$\sup_{\Omega\in\mathcal R}\#\xi_{(\alpha,\beta)}(\Omega)=+\infty.$$

The problem is posed as an "easier" variant of the open question whether $\sup_N G_{\alpha,\beta}(N,N)=+\infty$ for some $(\alpha,\beta)$ with $1,\alpha,\beta$ rationally independent. Subsequent work by Haynes, Koivusalo, Walton, Sadun, and Julien on gaps problems and patch-frequency statistics in cut-and-project sets gives upper bounds (almost-sure poly-log growth) but no example achieving an infinite supremum. A simple graph $G$ on $n$ vertices is called Hamiltonian if it contains a cycle that visits every vertex exactly once. Let $\mathcal{H}_n$ denote the class of Hamiltonian graphs on $n$ vertices with the property that no two cycles of $G$ have the same length (i.e., for every integer $\ell$, $G$ contains at most one cycle of length $\ell$). Determine
$$f(n) := \max\{ |E(G)| : G \in \mathcal{H}_n \},$$
the maximum possible number of edges in such a graph, as a function of $n$.
representations.original:
A simple graph $G$ on $n$ vertices is called Hamiltonian if it contains a cycle that visits every vertex exactly once. Let $\mathcal{H}_n$ denote the class of Hamiltonian graphs on $n$ vertices with the property that no two cycles of $G$ have the same length (i.e., for every integer $\ell$, $G$ contains at most one cycle of length $\ell$). Determine
$$f(n) := \max\{ |E(G)| : G \in \mathcal{H}_n \},$$
the maximum possible number of edges in such a graph, as a function of $n$.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The problem, posed by Markström, remains open. Known bounds give roughly $n + \sqrt{2n} + O(1)$ as an upper bound and constructions (e.g., Lee–Timmons, 2017) yield Hamiltonian graphs on $n$ vertices with no repeated cycle length having $n + \sqrt{n - 3/4} - 3/2$ edges for infinitely many $n$. The exact value of the maximum is not determined.

For each positive integer $n$, let $g(n)$ denote the least number of edges in a (simple, undirected) graph $G$ such that, for every integer $k$ with $1 \le k \le n$, the graph $G$ contains a cycle of length $k$ (here a cycle of length $k$ means a simple cycle on exactly $k$ vertices, so a graph containing such cycles for $k=1,2$ is interpreted as containing a loop and a pair of multi-edges, or equivalently the relevant short-cycle conditions are vacuous and only $3 \le k \le n$ contribute; equivalently, restrict attention to $3 \le k \le n$). Determine whether
$$g(n) = n + \log_2 n + O(1) \quad \text{as } n \to \infty.$$
That is, decide whether there exists a constant $C > 0$ such that for all sufficiently large $n$,
$$\bigl| g(n) - n - \log_2 n \bigr| \le C.$$

$$g(n) = n + \log_2 n + O(1) \quad \text{as } n \to \infty.$$
That is, decide whether there exists a constant $C > 0$ such that for all sufficiently large $n$,
$$\bigl| g(n) - n - \log_2 n \bigr| \le C.$$

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The best known bounds give $n + \log_2 n - 1 \le g(n) \le n + \log_2 n + 3\cdot 2^{\log_2^* n} + O(1)$ for large $n$, yielding $g(n) = n + \log_2 n + O(\log_2 \log_2 n)$. The tighter conjectured bound $g(n) = n + \log_2 n + O(1)$ remains open and is described as difficult to prove in current surveys of open problems on cycles.

Let $n$ be a positive integer and consider the finite set $[n]=\{0,1,\dots,n-1\}$ equipped with counting measure $\mu$. A central symmetry of $[n]$ is a map $\sigma_c\colon[n]\to[n]$ of the form $\sigma_c(x)=c-x\pmod n$ for some $c\in\mathbb{Z}$ (the integer central symmetries of the cyclic group structure).

Given $r\ge 2$, a blurred $r$-coloring of $[n]$ is a measurable function $\chi\colon[n]\to\{1,\dots,r\}$ together with the convention that one measures, for each central symmetry $\sigma$, the discrepancy
$$D(\chi,\sigma)\;=\;\mu\bigl(\{x\in[n]:\chi(x)\ne \chi(\sigma(x))\}\bigr).$$
Define the symmetry defect of $\chi$ by
$$S(\chi)\;=\;\inf_{\sigma}\,D(\chi,\sigma),$$
where the infimum is taken over all (nontrivial) integer central symmetries of $[n]$. The blurred maximal symmetry number is
$$\mathrm{bms}_r(n)\;=\;\inf_{\chi}\,S(\chi),$$
where the infimum runs over all measurable blurred $r$-colorings $\chi$ of $[n]$.

Determine the exact values of $\mathrm{bms}_r(n)$, in particular for small values of $n$ and for $r=2$.

Let $I = [0,1]$ be the unit interval, equipped with the standard Lebesgue measure $\mu$, and let $\mathcal{S} = \{s_c : c \in \mathbb{R}\}$ be the family of central symmetries of the real line, where $s_c(x) = 2c - x$.

For an integer $r \geq 2$, a finite measurable partition $I = A_1 \cup A_2 \cup \cdots \cup A_n$ (into pairwise disjoint measurable pieces) is called $r$-symmetric if for every piece $A_i$ there exists a central symmetry $s_{c_i} \in \mathcal{S}$ such that $\mu(A_i \cap s_{c_i}(A_i)) \geq \tfrac{1}{r}\,\mu(A_i)$ — i.e., each piece overlaps with one of its own central reflections in at least a $\tfrac{1}{r}$-fraction of its measure. Define
$$\mathrm{ms}_r(I) = \sup \Bigl\{ \min_{1 \le i \le n} \mu(A_i \cap s_{c_i}(A_i)) \;:\; \text{over all such } r\text{-symmetric finite measurable partitions of } I \Bigr\}.$$

Determine the exact value of $\mathrm{ms}_r(I)$, in particular in the first nontrivial case $r = 2$.

Consider a heterogeneous computing (HC) environment, defined as a distributed high-performance system consisting of a suite of machines M_1, ..., M_k with varied computational architectures and capabilities, interconnected by high-speed communication links. An application A is to be executed in such an environment, possibly after being decomposed into a hierarchy of tasks and subtasks, each of which may have distinct computational requirements that suit different machines in the suite.

Design a machine-independent programming language L, together with a set of user-specified directives D, and an associated compilation/analysis system, such that for every application A written in L with directives in D the system simultaneously achieves the following:

(1) Compiles A into efficient executable code for each machine M_i in the HC suite, where efficiency is measured against code that would be produced by a native compiler tailored specifically to M_i.

(2) Supports the automatic or directive-guided decomposition of A into a hierarchy of tasks and subtasks suitable for execution across heterogeneous machines.

(3) Determines, for each task and subtask produced by the decomposition, its computational requirements (e.g., the type of architecture or capability best suited to execute it).

Provide either a construction of such a language, directive set, and compilation framework that provably satisfies (1)–(3), or a rigorous argument showing that no such language and system can simultaneously satisfy all three requirements.

Let I = [0,1] ⊂ ℝ. For a measurable subset A ⊆ I, call a point c ∈ I a center of symmetry of A if the reflection x ↦ 2c − x maps A∩[2c−1, 2c] (after intersection with I) to itself; equivalently, A contains a "symmetric subset" with respect to c, i.e. a measurable set B ⊆ A with B = 2c − B of positive Lebesgue measure. For an integer r ≥ 1, define

   ms_r(I) = sup_{χ} min_{1 ≤ i ≤ r} sup_{c ∈ I} λ({x ∈ I : x ∈ χ^{-1}(i),  2c − x ∈ χ^{-1}(i)}),

where the outer supremum is over all measurable r-colorings χ : I → {1,…,r} and λ denotes Lebesgue measure; in words, ms_r(I) is the largest number m such that every measurable r-coloring of I contains a monochromatic centrally symmetric subset of measure ≥ m. It is known that the limit

   S' := lim_{r→∞} r^2 · ms_r(I) = inf_{r ∈ ℕ} r^2 · ms_r(I)

exists and satisfies S ≤ S' < 5/6, where

   S := inf { ‖f * f‖_∞ : f ∈ L^∞([0,1]),  f ≥ 0,  ∫_0^1 f(x) dx = 1 }

is the autoconvolution infimum (with f*f(t) = ∫ f(x)f(t−x) dx).

Problem. Determine, or give nontrivial upper and lower bounds for, the constant S'. In particular, decide whether the strict inequality S' > S holds.

Consider a heterogeneous computing environment modeled as a finite set of machines $M = \{m_1, \dots, m_n\}$ with differing computational capabilities (e.g., distinct processor architectures, memory hierarchies, and instruction throughputs) interconnected by a communication network whose links have heterogeneous bandwidths and latencies. A workload is given as a finite collection of tasks $T = \{t_1, \dots, t_k\}$, each of which may be decomposed into subtasks with precedence and data-dependency relations. A mapping is an assignment of tasks (and subtasks) to machines together with a schedule of their execution and of the inter-machine data transfers.

For each machine $m_i$ at time $\tau$, let $L_i(\tau)$ denote a vector-valued descriptor of its current loading and status (queue lengths, CPU/memory utilization, availability), and for each network link $(i,j)$ let $N_{ij}(\tau)$ denote a descriptor of its current effective bandwidth and latency. For each task $t \in T$ and each candidate machine $m_i$, let $C(t, m_i; L, N)$ denote the predicted completion time of $t$ on $m_i$ given the current load/status profile $(L, N)$, and similarly $C(s, m_i; L, N)$ for a subtask $s$.

Develop methodologies that:

(a) define and compute the descriptors $L_i(\tau)$ and $N_{ij}(\tau)$ from runtime measurements;
(b) produce estimators $\widehat{C}(t, m_i; L, N)$ and $\widehat{C}(s, m_i; L, N)$ of task and subtask completion times whose accuracy (e.g., expected relative error) is sufficient to support mapping decisions that approximately optimize a chosen objective (such as makespan $\max_i \sum_{t \mapsto m_i} C(t, m_i)$ or weighted average completion time);
(c) quantify the relationship between the accuracy of these estimators and the quality (e.g., approximation ratio with respect to an optimal mapping) of the resulting task-to-machine mappings.

Specifically, exhibit measurement and estimation procedures, together with rigorous bounds, ensuring that mappings obtained by minimizing the estimated objective using $\widehat{C}$ are provably close to mappings obtained from exact completion times.

Consider a heterogeneous computing environment consisting of a finite set of machines $M = \{m_1, \dots, m_p\}$ with varied computational capabilities, interconnected by communication links of varying bandwidths and latencies, together with a finite set of tasks $T = \{t_1, \dots, t_n\}$ (possibly partitioned into subtasks with precedence constraints encoded by a directed acyclic graph $G=(T,E)$). For each task $t_i$ and machine $m_j$, the execution time $c_{ij}$ and, for each communication edge $(t_i,t_k)\in E$ and pair of machines $(m_j,m_l)$, the data-transfer time $d_{ik}^{jl}$ are not known exactly: instead, each is given as a random variable (or, equivalently, by a probability distribution, an interval estimate, or a fuzzy estimate) reflecting predictive uncertainty.

A mapping is a function $\mu : T \to M$ (extended by a schedule that respects $G$) and the makespan $C(\mu)$ is the random variable defined as the completion time of the last task under $\mu$.

Develop a principled framework for producing mappings $\mu$ that explicitly incorporate the uncertainty in the estimated parameters $\{c_{ij}\}$ and $\{d_{ik}^{jl}\}$. Specifically:

(a) Formulate appropriate stochastic objective functionals (e.g., $\mathbb{E}[C(\mu)]$, quantiles $\inf\{x : \Pr[C(\mu) \le x] \ge 1-\alpha\}$, robustness radii, or expected slack) whose optimization yields mappings that perform well under the given parameter uncertainty.

(b) Provide algorithms (exact, approximate, or heuristic) that compute or approximate optimal mappings under such stochastic objectives, with provable guarantees on solution quality and on the sensitivity of the resulting makespan distribution to perturbations in the input distributions.

(c) Establish whether such uncertainty-aware mappings can outperform mappings derived from point estimates (e.g., using only $\mathbb{E}[c_{ij}]$) in a quantifiable sense, and characterize the regimes (variance, correlation structure, DAG topology) in which the improvement is significant.

Let $G$ be a compact Hausdorff Abelian (topological) group equipped with its normalized Haar measure $\mu$ (so $\mu(G)=1$). For each $c \in G$ define the central symmetry
$$s_c : G \to G, \qquad s_c(x) = c\,x^{-1}\,c,$$
which is an involutive homeomorphism of $G$. Let $\mathcal{S}(G) = \{s_c : c \in G\}$ denote the family of all such symmetries.

For an integer $r \geq 1$, define the measurable symmetry number
$$\mathrm{ms}_r(G) \;=\; \inf_{(A_1,\dots,A_r)} \; \max_{1 \le i \le r}\; \sup_{c \in G}\; \mu\bigl(A_i \cap s_c(A_i)\bigr),$$
where the infimum is taken over all partitions $G = A_1 \sqcup A_2 \sqcup \cdots \sqcup A_r$ of $G$ into $r$ pairwise disjoint $\mu$-measurable sets.

It is known that $\mathrm{ms}_r(G) \geq 1/r^2$ for every such $G$.

Problem. Determine all compact Abelian groups $G$ for which equality
$$\mathrm{ms}_r(G) = \frac{1}{r^2}$$
holds.

representations.normalized:
A heterogeneous computing (HC) suite consists of a collection of machines with diverse architectures and capabilities, interconnected by a network, onto which a workload of application tasks must be mapped and scheduled. Tasks in such a workload are of two qualitatively different kinds: (i) one-shot tasks, which execute a single time and then terminate (for example, a simulation run), characterized by a finite input, a finite computation, and a definite completion time; and (ii) continuously running tasks, which have no a priori termination time and process an ongoing stream of inputs (for example, monitoring and analyzing sensor data), characterized by recurring deadlines, throughput requirements, and persistent resource occupancy.

Develop a unified formal model for application tasks executing on an HC suite that:

1. Represents both one-shot tasks and continuously running tasks as instances of a single mathematical framework, capturing in each case the relevant computational requirements (work, data dependencies, communication, memory footprint) and timing requirements (completion time vs. periodic/throughput/latency constraints).
2. Specifies, for each task type, an appropriate notion of performance on a given machine of the suite (e.g., expected execution time for one-shot tasks; sustainable rate, steady-state utilization, and response time distribution for continuously running tasks).
3. Supports the formulation of mapping and scheduling problems on heterogeneous machines in which one-shot tasks and continuously running tasks coexist and compete for the same resources, and in which the objective function meaningfully combines makespan-style metrics (for one-shot tasks) with steady-state metrics (for continuously running tasks).

Provide such a model, justify that it correctly distinguishes and accommodates the two task categories, and demonstrate that standard heterogeneous mapping/scheduling problems can be expressed within it.

representations.normalized:
Consider a heterogeneous computing system consisting of a set M = {m_1, ..., m_k} of machines with differing architectures and performance characteristics, together with an interconnection network providing communication between machines. An application is modeled as a directed acyclic task graph G = (T, E), where each task t ∈ T may be further decomposed into a set of communicating subtasks S(t) = {s_{t,1}, ..., s_{t,n_t}}. The subtasks of a task have data dependencies among them but may be assigned to different machines in M for concurrent execution. During execution, subtasks may need to exchange not only forward data dependencies but also feedback communications, i.e., information that flows from a subtask back to one or more subtasks that have already begun or completed execution, in order to influence subsequent computation (for example, iterative refinement, dynamic parameter updates, or convergence signals).

Develop and characterize methods (including programming-model constructs, runtime mechanisms, scheduling policies, and synchronization protocols) that support such feedback communications among subtasks assigned to distinct machines in a heterogeneous system, in a way that:
(i) preserves the data dependencies imposed by G,
(ii) permits subtasks executing on different machines to send and receive feedback messages while running, and
(iii) admits a performance model under which the resulting execution time can be analyzed.

Formally describe at least one such method and prove (or argue) its correctness with respect to (i)–(iii).

Let G be a finite group. A subset S ⊆ G is called symmetric if there exists g ∈ G such that S = gS^{-1}g, where S^{-1} = {s^{-1} : s ∈ S}. (Equivalently, S is symmetric if it is invariant under some involutive map of the form x ↦ gx^{-1}g.) For an integer r ≥ 2 and an r-coloring χ : G → {1, …, r}, let

  ν(χ) = max { |S|/|G| : S ⊆ G is symmetric and monochromatic with respect to χ }.

Define the maximal symmetry number of G with r colors by

  ms_r(G) = min { ν(χ) : χ is an r-coloring of G },

so that ms_r(G) is the largest real number c such that every r-coloring of G admits a monochromatic symmetric subset of cardinality at least c·|G|.

Question: Given any real number ε > 0 and any integer r > 1, does there exist a finite group G with

  ms_r(G) < ε ?

Consider a heterogeneous computing (HC) suite, defined as a distributed collection of machines with varied computational capabilities interconnected by high-speed communication links, on which a stream of tasks (each with possibly different machine-dependent execution times and inter-task communication requirements) must be mapped to machines and ordered in time so as to optimize a global performance objective (for example, minimizing makespan or maximizing throughput). A scheduler is called hierarchical if it decomposes the mapping/scheduling decision across multiple levels (for instance, a top-level scheduler that assigns tasks or task groups to clusters or sub-suites, and lower-level schedulers that assign tasks to individual machines within each cluster), with limited information exchange between levels.

Problem: Design and analyze hierarchical scheduling techniques for heterogeneous computing suites that allow the suite to scale to very large sizes (in number of machines, tasks, and degree of heterogeneity) while maintaining good global scheduling performance. Specifically, identify hierarchical decomposition strategies, level-to-level information abstractions, and per-level scheduling policies whose combined time and communication complexity grows sub-linearly (or otherwise scalably) in the size of the suite, and quantify the loss in global scheduling quality (relative to an idealized centralized scheduler) introduced by the hierarchy as a function of the suite size and heterogeneity parameters.

Let $G$ be an infinite group. For each element $c\in G$ define the central symmetry $s_c\colon G\to G$ by $s_c(x)=cx^{-1}c$, and let $\mathcal S=\{s_c:c\in G\}$. A subset $A\subseteq G$ is called symmetric if $s_c(A)=A$ for some $c\in G$ (equivalently, $A=cA^{-1}c$ for some $c\in G$).

For a positive integer $r$, define the cardinal symmetry numbers
$$MS_r(G)=\min_{\chi}\;\max_{i=1,\dots,r}\;\sup\bigl\{|A|:A\subseteq\chi^{-1}(i)\text{ is symmetric}\bigr\},$$
$$MS_r^{+}(G)=\min_{\chi}\;\max_{i=1,\dots,r}\;\sup\bigl\{|A|^{+}:A\subseteq\chi^{-1}(i)\text{ is symmetric}\bigr\},$$
where $\chi$ ranges over all colorings $\chi\colon G\to\{1,\dots,r\}$, $|A|$ denotes the cardinality of $A$, and $|A|^{+}$ denotes its successor cardinal (so $MS_r^{+}$ takes the supremum over a strict-inequality variant).

Question: Is it true that for every infinite group $G$ and every positive integer $r$, both $MS_r(G)$ and $MS_r^{+}(G)$ are infinite cardinals? Equivalently, is it true that for every finite coloring of any infinite group $G$ there exist monochromatic symmetric subsets of arbitrarily large finite cardinality?

Let $K$ be an infinite field and let $G=\mathrm{SL}(K)=\bigcup_{n\geq 1}\mathrm{SL}_n(K)$ be the special linear group over $K$ (the direct limit of the groups $\mathrm{SL}_n(K)$ under the standard embeddings).

Is it true that $MS_r^+(G)=|G|^+$ for every finite cardinal $r$? In other words, for every finite coloring of $\mathrm{SL}(K)$ with $r$ colors, must there exist a monochromatic symmetric subset of cardinality $|G|$?

Consider a heterogeneous computing (HC) system consisting of a set of machines M = {m_1, ..., m_p} with differing architectures and computational capabilities, on which a dynamically arriving set of tasks T = {t_1, t_2, ...} must be executed. Each machine m_j runs an operating system that supports preemptive multi-tasking, so that several tasks assigned to m_j may share its processor time according to a time-sharing policy. Each task t_i has an estimated execution time e_{ij} on machine m_j, plus quality-of-service (QoS) requirements such as deadlines, priorities, throughput, security level, or fault tolerance level.

Design and analyze a mapping procedure (i.e., a matching-and-scheduling algorithm) M: T -> M together with a per-machine time-allocation policy A_j that, for each machine m_j, partitions its processor time among the tasks currently assigned to it, with the following objectives:

1. The mapping M explicitly accounts for the fact that each machine can execute multiple tasks concurrently via multi-tasking, rather than assuming exclusive use of a processor.
2. The time-allocation policies A_j allocate processor time among co-located tasks in a way that respects all per-task QoS requirements simultaneously.
3. The combined scheme leverages multi-tasking (e.g., to overlap I/O with computation, to satisfy mixed-priority workloads, or to improve responsiveness) while still optimizing a global system performance metric such as makespan, weighted QoS satisfaction, or robustness.

Provide a formal model for this problem, define an appropriate optimality (or approximation) criterion, and either give an algorithm achieving that criterion with provable guarantees or prove hardness/impossibility results characterizing the trade-offs between multi-tasking benefits and QoS guarantees in heterogeneous computing environments.

Let $G$ be a group. A subset $S \subseteq G$ is called symmetric if there exists $g \in G$ such that $S = gS^{-1}g$, i.e., $S$ is invariant under the involution $x \mapsto gx^{-1}g$ for some $g \in G$. For a cardinal $r$, an $r$-coloring of $G$ is a function $\chi : G \to \{1, 2, \dots, r\}$. Define the cardinal symmetry number
$$MS_r^+(G) = \min_{\chi} \sup\{|S| : S \subseteq G \text{ is symmetric, infinite, and monochromatic with respect to } \chi\}^+,$$
where the minimum runs over all $r$-colorings $\chi : G \to r$, and the operation $\kappa \mapsto \kappa^+$ denotes the successor cardinal of the supremum of cardinalities of monochromatic symmetric subsets. Equivalently, $MS_r^+(G) > \kappa$ means that for every $r$-coloring of $G$ there exists a monochromatic symmetric subset of cardinality $\geq \kappa$.

Let $F_2$ denote the free group on two generators. It is known that $MS_2^+(F_2)$ is uncountable, i.e., for every $2$-coloring of $F_2$ there is an infinite monochromatic symmetric subset.

Question: Is $MS_r^+(F_2)$ uncountable for every finite cardinal $r$? That is, is it true that for every finite number $r$ of colors and every $r$-coloring of $F_2$, there exists an infinite monochromatic symmetric subset?

In such an environment, identify and formally address the security issues that arise from allowing users to execute tasks on machines they do not own or control. Specifically, propose a security framework (with precise definitions of trust assumptions, adversary model, and security guarantees) that ensures: (i) confidentiality and integrity of a task's code and data while executing on a remote host; (ii) protection of the host machine from malicious or faulty submitted tasks; (iii) authentication and access control among peers; and (iv) safe inter-task communication. Let $\mathbb{H}^2$ denote the hyperbolic plane (the Lobachevsky plane), endowed with its standard hyperbolic metric and Borel $\sigma$-algebra. For each point $c \in \mathbb{H}^2$ let $s_c : \mathbb{H}^2 \to \mathbb{H}^2$ be the central symmetry through $c$, i.e., the unique isometry that fixes $c$ and reverses every geodesic through $c$. A subset $A \subseteq \mathbb{H}^2$ is called centrally symmetric if there exists a point $c$ such that $s_c(A) = A$. A Borel $r$-coloring of $\mathbb{H}^2$ is a partition $\mathbb{H}^2 = C_1 \sqcup C_2 \sqcup \dots \sqcup C_r$ into $r$ Borel pieces. A subset $A \subseteq \mathbb{H}^2$ is unbounded if its hyperbolic diameter is infinite (equivalently, its asymptotic dimension satisfies $\operatorname{asdim}(A) \geq 0$ in the convention that the empty set and bounded sets have asymptotic dimension $-\infty$, while unbounded sets have $\operatorname{asdim} \geq 0$).

Question: For every integer $r \geq 2$, does every Borel $r$-coloring of $\mathbb{H}^2$ contain a monochromatic centrally symmetric subset that is unbounded?

status_assertions.value: open_status:solved

A published result ("Symmetric monochromatic subsets in colorings of the Lobachevsky plane", DMTCS) establishes that for each partition of the Lobachevsky (hyperbolic) plane into finitely many Borel pieces, one of the cells contains an unbounded centrally symmetric subset. This affirmatively answers the question for all r ≥ 2.

Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain with smooth boundary, and let $\omega \subset \Omega$ be a nonempty open subset. For $T \in (0,\infty]$, consider the linear heat equation
$$\varphi_t - \Delta \varphi = 0 \text{ in } \Omega \times (0,T), \qquad \varphi = 0 \text{ on } \partial\Omega \times (0,T), \qquad \varphi(\cdot,0)=\varphi_0 \in L^2(\Omega).$$
It is known that there exist constants $\gamma > 0$ and $C = C(\gamma) > 0$ such that
$$\int_0^T \!\!\int_\Omega e^{-\gamma/t}\,\varphi(x,t)^2\,dx\,dt \;\le\; C \int_0^T\!\!\int_\omega \varphi(x,t)^2\,dx\,dt$$
for every solution $\varphi$, and (using exponential decay of the $L^2$-norm) the same form of inequality makes sense for $T = \infty$:
$$\int_0^\infty \!\!\int_\Omega e^{-\gamma/t}\,\varphi(x,t)^2\,dx\,dt \;\le\; C \int_0^\infty\!\!\int_\omega \varphi(x,t)^2\,dx\,dt. \qquad (\star)$$
Define
$$\gamma_*(\Omega,\omega) := \inf\{\gamma > 0 : (\star) \text{ holds for some } C > 0\}.$$
A simple test using radial Gaussian-like solutions concentrated in a ball $B(x_0,\rho) \subset \Omega \setminus \overline{\omega}$ yields the lower bound
$$\gamma_*(\Omega,\omega) \;\ge\; \sup\bigl\{\rho^2/4 : B(x_0,\rho) \subset \Omega\setminus\overline{\omega}\bigr\}.$$
Determine $\gamma_*(\Omega,\omega)$ explicitly (the best possible $\gamma$ in the observability inequalities, especially in the infinite-time version), and decide whether the above lower bound is sharp, in particular for radially symmetric geometries (e.g., $\Omega$ a ball and $\omega$ an annular neighborhood of $\partial\Omega$).

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Ervedoza and Zuazua (Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal., 2011, "Sharp observability estimates for heat equations") obtained sharp upper bounds on the best constant γ via a transmutation method from observability of the wave equation. Their estimates are proved sharp in one space dimension (for an interval of length L controlled at the boundary, the threshold is γ = L²/2) and in radially symmetric multi-dimensional configurations, matching the geometric lower bound sup ρ²/4. The general (non-radial) multi-dimensional case of identifying the exact best constant remains open.
