Consider an excited (cookie) random walk on $\mathbb{Z}$ defined as follows. Fix an integer $M\ge 1$ and a sequence of "cookie strengths" $p_1,\dots,p_M\in[1/2,1]$ with at least one $p_i>1/2$ (so cookies bias the walk to the right). At each site $x\in\mathbb{Z}$ place a stack of $M$ cookies with strengths $p_1,\dots,p_M$ (the $j$-th cookie at site $x$ has strength $p_j$). Let $(X_n)_{n\ge0}$ be the nearest-neighbor process on $\mathbb{Z}$ with $X_0=0$ defined by the following rule: when the walker is at site $x$ at time $n$, if the walker has visited $x$ exactly $j$ times before (so $j<M$), it eats the $j+1$-st cookie at $x$ and moves to $x+1$ with probability $p_{j+1}$ and to $x-1$ with probability $1-p_{j+1}$; if it has visited $x$ at least $M$ times, it moves to $x\pm 1$ each with probability $1/2$. Each step is independent given the past. Assume parameters such that the walk is transient (e.g.\ $\sum_{i=1}^M(2p_i-1)>1$).

Compute, as an explicit function of $M$ and $(p_1,\dots,p_M)$, the probability
$$P_0\!\left[\,X_n\ne 0\ \text{for all } n\ge 1\,\right]$$
that the walk never returns to its starting point.

Consider the class N of synchronous finite-state neuronal networks defined as follows. A network in N consists of n nodes (neurons), each in one of finitely many states (for instance, an "activity" level in {0,1,...,M} together with possibly a refractory counter). At each discrete time step, every neuron updates its state simultaneously according to a fixed local rule that depends on its current state and on the weighted sum of inputs received from neurons that are connected to it via a directed edge. The connectivity of the network is given by a random digraph on n vertices.

Previous analysis has characterized, for large n, the typical dynamics of such networks (asymptotic attractor behavior, transient behavior, and phase transitions in suitable order parameters) when the underlying random digraph is a single-type Erdős–Rényi digraph G(n,p) (each directed edge included independently with probability p).

Problem: Determine the typical large-n dynamics of networks in N — including the structure and statistics of attractors, the duration and shape of transients, and the existence and location of phase transitions — when the underlying random connectivity is replaced by each of the following ensembles:

(a) a multitype Erdős–Rényi random digraph, in which vertices are partitioned into k types and the probability of a directed edge from a vertex of type i to a vertex of type j is a prescribed value p_{ij};

(b) a generic scale-free random digraph, in which the in- and out-degree distributions follow power laws P(deg = d) ∝ d^{-γ} for some exponent γ > 1;

(c) a small-world random digraph constructed, for example, by the Watts–Strogatz mechanism: start from a regular ring lattice on n vertices in which each vertex is connected to its k nearest neighbors and rewire each edge independently with probability β to a uniformly chosen target.

In each case, identify the analogues (if any) of the attractor-size laws, transient-length scaling, and phase transitions known in the Erdős–Rényi case.

Setup. Fix an integer $d\ge 2$ and let $E=\{\pm e_1,\dots,\pm e_d\}$ be the set of unit vectors in $\mathbb Z^d$. A cookie environment is a family $\omega=(\omega(z,\cdot,\cdot))_{z\in\mathbb Z^d}$, where for each site $z\in\mathbb Z^d$ and each $i\in\mathbb N$, $\omega(z,\cdot,i)$ is a probability vector on $E$ (the "$i$-th cookie at $z$"). Let $\mathbb P$ be a probability measure on the space of cookie environments. Given $\omega$, the excited random walk (ERW) starting at $0$ is the process $(X_n)_{n\ge 0}$ with $X_0=0$ that, conditionally on $\omega$ and on its past, jumps from its current position $z$ to $z+e$ with probability $\omega(z,e,i)$, where $i$ is the number of previous visits of the walk to $z$ (including the current one). Denote the resulting annealed law by $P_0$. A cookie at $(z,i)$ is called a "placebo" if $\omega(z,\cdot,i)$ equals the simple-random-walk vector $(1/(2d),\dots,1/(2d))$, and let $M(z)=\sup\{i:\omega(z,\cdot,i)\text{ is not a placebo at }z\}$.

Consider the following assumptions on $\mathbb P$:

(IID) The cookie stacks $(\omega(z,\cdot,\cdot))_{z\in\mathbb Z^d}$ are i.i.d. under $\mathbb P$.

(BD) There is a deterministic $M\in\mathbb N$ such that $M(z)\le M$ for all $z\in\mathbb Z^d$, $\mathbb P$-a.s.

(UEL) There is $\kappa>0$ such that $\omega(z,e,i)\ge \kappa$ for all $z\in\mathbb Z^d$, $e\in E$, $i\in\mathbb N$, $\mathbb P$-a.s.

For a nonzero direction $\ell\in\mathbb R^d$, define
$$A_\ell:=\{X_n\cdot\ell\to\infty\text{ as }n\to\infty\}.$$

Question. Under assumptions (IID), (BD), and (UEL), is it true that for every nonzero $\ell\in\mathbb R^d$ one has $P_0[A_\ell]\in\{0,1\}$? More generally, identify conditions on $\mathbb P$ that imply this zero–one law for directional transience.

A zero–one law for directional transience for one-dimensional excited random walks (in the stationary ergodic elliptic setting) was established by Amir, Berger and Orenshtein (2013/2016). The analogous multidimensional zero–one law for ERW on $\mathbb Z^d$, $d\ge 2$, under i.i.d. cookie stacks, bounded number of non-placebo cookies, and uniform ellipticity, parallels the well-known Kalikow zero–one conjecture for RWRE, which remains open in dimensions $d\ge 3$ (only $d=2$ is settled, by Zerner–Merkl). No reference verifying the multidimensional ERW zero–one law in full generality was found, so the question appears to remain open.

Consider a network of neurons partitioned into a set E of excitatory cells and a set I of inhibitory cells. Each cell is modeled by a system of ordinary differential equations (a Hodgkin–Huxley-type conductance-based model) in which both the excitatory and the inhibitory cells carry, in addition to standard sodium, potassium, and leak currents, calcium ionic currents (for instance a high-threshold Ca current and a calcium-dependent potassium AHP current), and where the cells interact via synaptic couplings that may include both fast and slow excitatory and inhibitory synapses, as well as more complex (e.g., voltage- or calcium-gated) interaction terms. Let M denote the resulting continuous-time ODE system describing the full network.

Suppose that, by exploiting the fast/slow structure of M and the singular limit in which active and silent phases are separated by rapid jumps, one can associate to M a discrete-time dynamical system N on a finite-dimensional state space encoding, for each cell, its current phase (active/silent) and the relevant slow variables at the beginning of an episode. Assume the reduction is set up so that, unlike in the simpler reductions where each cell fires exactly once before being replaced by another, the dynamics of N permit a single cell to fire during several consecutive episodes before other cells take over, and numerical simulations of M exhibit dynamic clustering consistent with trajectories of N.

Problem. Formulate and prove a rigorous theorem establishing a precise form of consistency between M and N, in direct analogy with the following prototype:

Prototype (the type of statement to be generalized). For a simpler class of networks (excitatory–inhibitory, with the simpler updating rule under which each cell fires exactly once per episode), there is a theorem of the form: for every initial condition in a suitable open set of phase space, and for all sufficiently small values of the singular-perturbation parameter, the trajectory of M tracks, episode by episode, the orbit of the discrete map N in the sense that the sequence of firing patterns and the slow-variable values at the start of each episode produced by M converge, as the perturbation parameter tends to 0, to those produced by N, with explicit error estimates and a description of attractors and transients of N reflected in M.

Establish the analogous theorem in the enriched setting described above (additional calcium currents, more complex interactions, and updating rule allowing repeated firings of a cell across consecutive episodes), specifying the precise hypotheses on parameters, time scales, and synaptic structure under which the consistency holds.

Prototype (the type of statement to be generalized). Let $d \geq 2$ and let $E = \{\pm e_1, \dots, \pm e_d\}$ denote the set of unit vectors in $\mathbb{Z}^d$. A cookie environment is a family $\omega = (\omega(z, \cdot, i))_{z \in \mathbb{Z}^d,\, i \in \mathbb{N}}$ of probability vectors on $E$, where $\omega(z, e, i)$ is the probability of stepping in direction $e$ from site $z$ on the $i$-th visit to $z$. Given a realization of $\omega$, the excited random walk (ERW) $X = (X_n)_{n \geq 0}$ started at $0$ is the Markov chain on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ with $X_0 = 0$ such that, conditionally on the past up to time $n$, if $X_n = z$ has been visited exactly $i$ times (counting the present visit), then $X_{n+1} = z + e$ with probability $\omega(z, e, i)$.

Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item (IID) The cookie stacks $(\omega(z, \cdot, i))_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$, indexed by $z \in \mathbb{Z}^d$, are i.i.d. under the environment law $\mathbb{P}$.
\item (UEL, uniform ellipticity) There exists $\kappa > 0$ such that $\omega(z, e, i) \geq \kappa$ for all $z \in \mathbb{Z}^d$, $e \in E$, $i \in \mathbb{N}$, $\mathbb{P}$-a.s.
\end{itemize}

Call the ERW recurrent if $P_0$-a.s. every site $z \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ is visited infinitely often, and transient if $P_0$-a.s. no site is visited infinitely often (equivalently $|X_n| \to \infty$), where $P_0$ is the annealed law of $X$ started at $0$.

Question: Under (IID) and (UEL), must the ERW always be either recurrent or transient (i.e., does the recurrence-vs-transience dichotomy hold)?

Consider the following cascade model on a random directed graph. Let $n \geq 1$ and let $D(n, \pi)$ be the Erdős–Rényi random digraph on vertex set $\{1, 2, \dots, n\}$ in which, for every ordered pair $(i, j)$ with $i \neq j$, the directed edge $i \to j$ is present independently with probability $\pi \in [0, 1]$.

Assign to each vertex $i$ a "payload" $p_i \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ and a "threshold" $\mathit{th}_i \in \mathbb{R}_{> 0}$. Vertices may be in one of two states, "inactive" or "active." The dynamics proceed in discrete rounds: starting from a single initially active vertex (chosen, say, uniformly at random) with all others inactive, in each round any inactive vertex $j$ becomes active as soon as the sum of payloads $p_i$ over currently active in-neighbors $i$ of $j$ reaches or exceeds $\mathit{th}_j$. Once a vertex is active, it stays active. Let $A_n$ denote the (random) total number of vertices that are active when this process terminates.

Specialize to the homogeneous case $p_i = \mathit{th}_i = 1$ for every $i$ (so an inactive vertex activates as soon as it has at least one active in-neighbor), and take edge probability $\pi = \pi(n) = c/n$ for a fixed constant $c > 0$. It is known that there exists a critical constant $c_{\mathrm{crit}} \in [1, 2]$ such that:
- if $c < c_{\mathrm{crit}}$, then $A_n / n \to 0$ in probability as $n \to \infty$ (subcritical regime, the cascade dies out);
- if $c > c_{\mathrm{crit}}$, then $\liminf_{n \to \infty} \mathbb{E}[A_n / n] > 0$ (supercritical regime, a positive fraction is activated).

Prove (or disprove) that $c_{\mathrm{crit}} = 1$.

Let d ≥ 2 and let E = {±e_1, …, ±e_d} be the set of unit vectors in Z^d. A cookie environment is a family ω = (ω(z, e, i))_{z ∈ Z^d, e ∈ E, i ∈ N} of nonnegative numbers such that for every z ∈ Z^d and i ∈ N, ∑_{e ∈ E} ω(z, e, i) = 1. Let P be a probability measure on the space of cookie environments. Assume:

(a) (Balance) P-almost surely, ω(z, e, i) = ω(z, −e, i) for all z ∈ Z^d, e ∈ E, i ∈ N.

(b) (Uniform ellipticity) There exists κ > 0 such that P-almost surely, ω(z, e, i) ≥ κ for all z ∈ Z^d, e ∈ E, i ∈ N.

(c) Either (IID) the stacks (ω(z, ·, ·))_{z ∈ Z^d} are i.i.d. under P, or (SE) (ω(z, ·, ·))_{z ∈ Z^d} is stationary and ergodic under P with respect to the shifts of Z^d.

Given a realization of ω, the balanced excited random walk (X_n)_{n ≥ 0} starting at 0 is the Markov chain whose transition probability from its current position z, when z has been visited i times so far (including the present visit), to z + e is ω(z, e, i).

Question: Under the above hypotheses, is it true that for d = 2 the walk X_n is almost surely recurrent, and for every d ≥ 3 the walk X_n is almost surely transient?

Consider the following discrete-time stochastic neuronal network model on n nodes. Fix a function π : ℕ → [0,1]. Build a random directed graph G(n, π(n)) on the vertex set {1, 2, …, n} by independently including each ordered edge (i, j) with probability π(n). Each vertex i has a state x_i(t) ∈ {0, 1} (quiescent or firing). The dynamics are synchronous: at each integer time t ≥ 0, vertex i fires at time t+1 (i.e. x_i(t+1) = 1) iff the number of in-neighbors j with x_j(t) = 1 is at least 1 (a fixed integer firing threshold), and otherwise x_i(t+1) = 0; equivalently, take any standard fixed-threshold majority/integrate-and-fire update rule on the random directed graph. Starting from a prescribed initial configuration (e.g. a single firing vertex, or all vertices firing), since the state space {0,1}^n is finite the trajectory eventually enters a periodic orbit. Define the transient length τ(n) as the (random) first time at which the trajectory reaches a state already on its periodic attractor; we are interested in the typical asymptotic behaviour of τ(n) as n → ∞ under the law induced by G(n, π(n)).

Question: Does there exist a choice of edge-probability function π(n) such that τ(n) grows faster than every polynomial in n (with high probability as n → ∞)? Failing that, does there exist π(n) for which τ(n) is at least Ω(n)?

Setup. Let $N$ be a Boolean system on $n$ variables: a discrete-time dynamical system on $\{0,1\}^n$ given by a synchronous update map $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}^n$, so that the Boolean trajectory from a state $x_0\in\{0,1\}^n$ is $x_{k+1}=f(x_k)$.

Let $M$ be an ODE conversion of $N$ in the class $D_2$, namely a system of ordinary differential equations
$$\dot y_i = F_i(y),\qquad y\in[0,1]^n,\ i=1,\dots,n,$$
in which each component is built (in the standard way associated with this class) from sigmoidal/Hill-type switching functions whose Boolean limit recovers $f$, so that the unit hypercube is partitioned into orthants indexed by $\{0,1\}^n$, and the focal/target point assigned to the orthant containing state $x$ is determined by $f(x)$.

Consider a nearest-neighbor self-interacting random walk on $\mathbb{Z}$ defined by a cookie environment, as follows. Attach to each site $z\in\mathbb{Z}$ a stack of cookies $(\omega(z,e,i))_{e\in\{-1,+1\},\,i\in\mathbb{N}}$, where $\omega(z,+1,i)+\omega(z,-1,i)=1$ specifies the probabilities of jumping right and left on the $i$-th visit to $z$. After all "non-placebo" cookies (those whose distribution differs from the uniform $1/2,1/2$) are consumed, subsequent transitions at $z$ are simple-random-walk steps. Assume:

(IID) The cookie stacks $(\omega(z,\cdot,\cdot))_{z\in\mathbb{Z}}$ are i.i.d.

(WEL) Weak ellipticity: there exists $\varepsilon>0$ such that, $P$-a.s., $\omega(0,e,i)\ge\varepsilon$ whenever the $i$-th cookie at $0$ is non-placebo.

Define the average drift parameter
$$\delta := E\!\left[\sum_{i=1}^{\infty}\bigl(2\omega(0,+1,i)-1\bigr)\right].$$

Under (IID), (WEL), and the additional bounded-cookies hypothesis

(BD) there is a deterministic $M\in\mathbb{N}$ such that $P$-a.s.\ the number $M(z)$ of non-placebo cookies at any site $z$ satisfies $M(z)\le M$,

it is known that the asymptotic speed $v=\lim_{n\to\infty}X_n/n$ exists $P$-a.s., and satisfies $v<0$ if $\delta<-2$, $v=0$ if $\delta\in[-2,2]$, and $v>0$ if $\delta>2$.

Question: Does this trichotomy continue to hold when (BD) is replaced by the weaker positivity assumption

(POS$_1$) $P$-a.s., $\omega(0,+1,i)\ge 1/2$ for every $i\in\mathbb{N}$ (i.e., every cookie has nonnegative drift in the $+1$ direction)?

Subsequent work has extended the one-dimensional ballisticity trichotomy beyond bounded cookie stacks. In particular, the CUNY thesis of O. Setup. Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and let a Boolean network on $n$ nodes be a map $N:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}^n$, written componentwise as $N=(N_1,\dots,N_n)$. Given an initial state $\vec x(0)\in\{0,1\}^n$, the synchronous (parallel-update) trajectory is defined by $\vec x(k+1)=N(\vec x(k))$ for $k\in\mathbb{N}$. The associated one-stepping (asynchronous, single-coordinate-update) dynamics produces, for each choice of an update sequence, a trajectory $\vec y(k)\in\{0,1\}^n$ in which at each step exactly one coordinate $i$ is replaced by $N_i(\vec y(k))$ while the others are kept fixed.

For an initial state $\vec x(0)$, define the switching-time set
$$SW(\vec x(0))=\{k\in\mathbb{N}:\vec x(k+1)\neq \vec x(k)\},$$
the set of times at which the synchronous trajectory actually changes. A sampling rule is a way of choosing, for each initial state $\vec x(0)$, a strictly increasing sequence $(T_t(\vec x(0)))_{t\in\mathbb{N}}\subseteq\mathbb{N}$.

Say that a one-stepping dynamics is strongly consistent with the synchronous dynamics under the sampling rule $(T_t)$ if there exists an update sequence such that the resulting one-stepping trajectory $\vec y$ satisfies $\vec y(T_t(\vec x(0)))=\vec x(T_t(\vec x(0)))$ for every $t\in\mathbb{N}$ and every $\vec x(0)\in\{0,1\}^n$.

Known result. There is a class $\mathcal{C}$ of Boolean networks for which strong consistency between the one-stepping dynamics and the synchronous dynamics holds when the sampling sequence $(T_t(\vec x(0)))_{t\in\mathbb{N}}$ is chosen as an enumeration of $SW(\vec x(0))$.

Problem. Determine whether this strong-consistency result extends to a strictly larger class of Boolean networks $\mathcal{C}'\supsetneq\mathcal{C}$ if the sampling sequences $(T_t(\vec x(0)))_{t\in\mathbb{N}}$ are chosen by some method other than enumerating $SW(\vec x(0))$. Equivalently, exhibit such a sampling rule together with a class of Boolean networks properly containing $\mathcal{C}$ for which strong consistency holds, or prove that no such extension exists.

representations.normalized:
Setting. Consider a finite directed interaction network on n nodes. A Boolean system on this network is a discrete-time dynamical system on {0,1}^n given by an updating rule F : {0,1}^n → {0,1}^n that respects the network's interaction structure (each coordinate F_i depends only on the states of nodes that have an edge into node i, and the dependence is monotone in the sign of each interaction). Trajectories may be generated by synchronous update or by any deterministic asynchronous update schedule.

An ODE realization of the same network is a system of ordinary differential equations
   dx_i/dt = f_i(x_1, …, x_n; ε),  i = 1,…,n,
on a compact phase space P ⊂ R^n containing [0,1]^n, where ε > 0 is a vector of time-scale and steepness parameters, the right-hand side is Lipschitz, and each f_i depends on x_j only through "signature variables" σ_j(x_j) that, in the singular limit ε → 0, become switch-like (e.g. sigmoidal) functions interpolating between two saturation values. Given thresholds θ_i ∈ (0,1), each ODE trajectory x(t) projects to a Boolean trajectory b(t) ∈ {0,1}^n by b_i(t) = 1 iff x_i(t) > θ_i.

Two notions of consistency. Fix an initial Boolean state s ∈ {0,1}^n with corresponding ODE initial state x(0) ∈ P having b(0) = s.
 (C) Consistency: for every sufficiently small ε, the projected Boolean trajectory of the ODE solution coincides on a prescribed finite time window with some valid asynchronous Boolean trajectory of F starting at s.
 (SC) Strong consistency: for every sufficiently small ε, the projected Boolean trajectory of the ODE coincides with the synchronous Boolean trajectory of F starting at s.

Task. Identify the broadest abstract hypotheses on the family {f_i(·;ε)} (conditions on the bifurcation structure of the singular limit ε → 0, on the time-scale separation between fast signature variables and slow node states, on monotonicity of dependence on signature variables, and on the geometry of nullclines and equilibria within each Boolean orthant) under which the following hold:

 (T1) Whenever F has the property that, from state s, every asynchronous update sequence is realizable, every ODE realization in the abstract class satisfies (C) for all sufficiently small ε.

 (T2) Whenever F has the additional "one-step" / unanimity property at s (every coordinate scheduled to change actually changes in one synchronous step regardless of order), every ODE realization in the abstract class satisfies (SC) for all sufficiently small ε.

Formulate the most general such abstract hypotheses, state the corresponding versions of (T1) and (T2), and prove them.

Setup. Fix a dimension d ≥ 1 and a positive integer M (the cookie-stack height; one may also take M = ∞). A cookie environment on Z^d is a family ω = (ω(x,j))_{x∈Z^d, j≥1} where, for each site x and each j, ω(x,j) = (ω_e(x,j))_e is a probability vector indexed by the 2d unit vectors e ∈ Z^d with |e| = 1 (so ∑_e ω_e(x,j) = 1 and ω_e(x,j) ≥ 0). Given ω, the excited (cookie) random walk started at 0 is the process (X_n)_{n≥0} on Z^d with X_0 = 0 whose quenched law P_{0,ω} is defined by

  P_{0,ω}(X_{n+1} = X_n + e | X_0,…,X_n) = ω_e(X_n, j),

where j = #{0 ≤ k ≤ n : X_k = X_n} is the number of previous visits of the walk to its current site (so on the j-th visit to x the walker uses the j-th "cookie" at x). The hitting times are T_n = inf{k ≥ 0 : X_k · e_1 = n} (for d = 1, T_n = inf{k : X_k = n}).

A probability measure P on the space of cookie environments is said to "model RWRE" if it is supported on environments for which ω(x,j) does not depend on j (i.e. each site has identical cookies, so the walk is a classical random walk in random environment).

Problem. Exhibit a probability measure P on cookie environments which does not model RWRE in the above sense, and such that for P-almost every environment ω there exist deterministic centering sequences a_n ∈ R (or R^d) and normalization sequences b_n > 0 for which, under the quenched law P_{0,ω}, either

  (T_n − a_n)/b_n  ⟹  μ   or   (X_n − a_n)/b_n  ⟹  μ,   as n → ∞,

where ⟹ denotes weak convergence and μ is a nondegenerate probability distribution that does not depend on ω.

Consider a class of ordinary differential equation (ODE) models on a directed network of n nodes, where each node i carries a fast state variable x_i(t) ∈ ℝ and one or more slow signaling variables s_i(t) ∈ ℝ^k. The dynamics take the general form

  dx_i/dt = f_i(x_i, s_i, {x_j : j ∈ N(i)}),
  ds_i/dt = ε · g_i(x_i, s_i, {s_j : j ∈ M(i)}),

with 0 < ε ≪ 1, where N(i) and M(i) are the in-neighborhoods of node i in the fast and slow interaction networks respectively, and where the system exhibits robustness of its qualitative long-term behavior owing to feedback loops among the slow signaling variables s_i. Assume there is also a discrete-time finite-state model D on the same node set, intended to approximate the ODE system, and a notion of "consistency" between the ODE trajectories and the discrete model's predictions: roughly, that for every (or generic) initial condition the long-term qualitative behavior predicted by the discrete model matches the actual long-term qualitative behavior of the ODE.

Now suppose the feedback architecture among the slow signaling variables — i.e. the directed graph M and the functional form of the couplings g_i restricted to those slow-slow interactions — is not fixed but is drawn at random from some specified probability distribution 𝒫 over admissible feedback architectures, while the remaining ingredients (the fast dynamics, the network N, and the slow update functions away from the random feedback couplings) are fixed.

Tasks:
(a) Formulate a rigorous notion of consistency between the ODE system and an associated discrete-time finite-state approximation that is appropriate for the setting of randomized slow-variable feedback loops.
(b) Identify natural distributions 𝒫 on feedback architectures (for example, Erdős–Rényi-type random directed graphs together with random sign or weight assignments on the slow-slow couplings) under which consistency, in the sense of (a), holds with probability tending to 1 as n → ∞, i.e. becomes a generic property.
(c) Determine whether such genericity of consistency can be established, and characterize the structural conditions on the distribution 𝒫 that are necessary and/or sufficient for it.

Let $R = k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ be a polynomial ring in $n$ variables over a field $k$. A monomial order ideal $X$ is a finite collection of monic monomials of $R$ that is closed under divisibility: if $M \in X$ and $N \mid M$, then $N \in X$. The order ideal $X$ is called pure if all its maximal monomials (with respect to divisibility) have the same degree $e$, called the socle degree of $X$. The h-vector of $X$ is the sequence $h = (h_0, h_1, \dots, h_e)$, where $h_i$ is the number of monomials of degree $i$ in $X$; such a sequence is called a pure O-sequence. The type of a pure O-sequence is the number of maximal monomials of $X$. A finite sequence $(h_0, h_1, \dots, h_e)$ of nonnegative integers is called unimodal if there exists an index $j$ with $h_0 \le h_1 \le \dots \le h_j \ge h_{j+1} \ge \dots \ge h_e$.

Determine the largest integer $t$ such that every pure O-sequence of type $t$ is unimodal, with no restriction placed on the codimension $n$ or the socle degree $e$. In particular, decide whether every pure O-sequence of type $2$ is unimodal in every codimension.

The unimodality of pure O-sequences of type 2 has been confirmed in low codimension: codimension 3 (a corollary of the Weak Lefschetz Property results of Boij–Migliore–Miró-Roig–Nagel–Zanello) and codimension 4 (Rocky Mountain J. Let $\mathbb{H}$ denote the skew field of quaternions, i.e. $\mathbb{H}=\{a_0+a_1 i+a_2 j+a_3 k:a_\ell\in\mathbb{R}\}$ with $i^2=j^2=k^2=ijk=-1$. A quaternion-valued function $x:[a,b]	o\mathbb{H}^n$ is written componentwise as $x(t)=x_0(t)+x_1(t)i+x_2(t)j+x_3(t)k$.

Develop a systematic theory of fractional-order quaternion-valued differential equations. Concretely:

1. Define an appropriate notion of fractional derivative $D^{\alpha}_t$ (e.g. Riemann–Liouville, Caputo, or Grünwald–Letnikov type) of order $\alpha\in(0,1)$ acting on quaternion-valued functions $x:[a,b]	o\mathbb{H}^n$, taking into account the noncommutativity of $\mathbb{H}$.

2. Formulate the linear nonhomogeneous fractional quaternion-valued differential equation
$$D^{\alpha}_t x(t) = A(t)\, x(t) + f(t),\qquad x(a)=x_0\in\mathbb{H}^n,$$
where $A:[a,b]	o\mathbb{H}^{n	imes n}$ and $f:[a,b]	o\mathbb{H}^n$ are continuous, and quaternion multiplication is taken in a fixed (say left) order.

3. Establish existence and uniqueness of solutions, characterize the structure of the solution set of the homogeneous equation as a right $\mathbb{H}$-module, and produce an analogue of the Mittag–Leffler matrix function and a variation-of-constants formula expressing solutions of the nonhomogeneous problem.

4. Provide a stability theory (including Mittag–Leffler / asymptotic stability) and an algorithmic method to compute fundamental solutions of the linear fractional QDE explicitly.

Let $\mathbb{H}$ denote the skew field of quaternions, with basis $\{1,i,j,k\}$ satisfying $i^2=j^2=k^2=ijk=-1$. A quaternion-valued function $u:\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{H}$ may be written as $u=u_0+u_1 i+u_2 j+u_3 k$ with $u_\ell:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$. Consider partial quaternion-valued differential equations, that is, PDEs in which the unknown $u$ takes values in $\mathbb{H}$ and whose coefficients and operations respect the noncommutative quaternion algebra (so that left/right multiplication must be distinguished). A soliton solution is a localized travelling-wave solution that preserves its shape under propagation and under interactions with other such solutions.

For real- and complex-valued PDEs, the so-called dynamical-systems method (also called the bifurcation method of dynamical systems) reduces the search for travelling-wave solutions $u(x,t)=\varphi(x-ct)$ to the analysis of an associated planar (or higher-dimensional) ordinary differential system, whose homoclinic, heteroclinic, and periodic orbits correspond respectively to solitary-wave, kink-type, and periodic-wave solutions of the original PDE.

Develop a theory of soliton solutions for partial quaternion-valued differential equations. In particular, determine whether the dynamical-systems method can be extended to the quaternion-valued setting so as to produce soliton solutions: identify the appropriate quaternion analogue of the travelling-wave reduction, formulate the resulting (quaternion) ODE system, and characterize orbits of this system corresponding to soliton solutions of the original quaternion PDE. Provide either such an extension together with concrete classes of partial quaternion-valued differential equations admitting soliton solutions obtained by this method, or a proof that no such extension is possible.

A finite sequence $(h_0, h_1, \dots, h_e)$ of positive integers is called unimodal if there is an index $j$ with $h_0 \le h_1 \le \cdots \le h_j \ge h_{j+1} \ge \cdots \ge h_e$, and nonunimodal otherwise.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The literature on pure $O$-sequences confirms that socle degree 4 is the smallest socle degree at which a nonunimodal pure $O$-sequence can exist (since by Hibi's flawlessness result every pure $O$-sequence of socle degree at most 3 is unimodal). However, the minimal codimension $r$ achieving nonunimodality at socle degree 4 does not appear to have been determined; it is listed as an open problem in the survey on pure $O$-sequences and remains unresolved in subsequent work.

where $F : \mathbb{H}^n \to \mathbb{H}^n$ is a (typically linear or polynomial) quaternion-valued map; in the linear case $\dot{u} = A u$ with $A \in \mathbb{H}^{n\times n}$ acting (say) by left multiplication.

Augment such a system with spatial variation and diffusion: consider $u : \Omega \times [0,\infty) \to \mathbb{H}^n$ on a spatial domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$, satisfying the quaternion-valued reaction-diffusion system
$$\partial_t u(x,t) = D \,\Delta u(x,t) + F(u(x,t)), \qquad x \in \Omega,\ t > 0,$$
together with appropriate boundary conditions (e.g. homogeneous Neumann), where $D$ is a diffusion operator (a quaternion or real matrix coefficient acting componentwise) and $\Delta$ is the Laplacian acting on each real component of $u$.

Develop a theory of the dynamical behaviour of such quaternion-valued reaction-diffusion systems. In particular:

(a) Identify conditions on $F$ and $D$ under which a spatially homogeneous equilibrium $u^* \in \mathbb{H}^n$ of $\dot{u} = F(u)$, stable as an equilibrium of the ODE, becomes unstable when diffusion is introduced (a quaternionic analogue of Turing instability).

(b) Classify the spatiotemporal patterns (stationary patterns, traveling waves, spiral waves, oscillatory patterns, etc.) that can bifurcate from such instabilities, and determine which phenomena are genuinely new compared to real- or complex-valued reaction-diffusion systems due to the noncommutativity of $\mathbb{H}$.

(c) Provide concrete worked examples (for instance, quaternion analogues of activator–inhibitor or population models) exhibiting these dynamics.

A pure order ideal in n variables is a finite, nonempty set X of monomials in the polynomial ring k[x_1,...,x_n] (over a field k) that is closed under taking divisors (if m ∈ X and m' divides m, then m' ∈ X) and whose maximal monomials (with respect to divisibility) all have the same total degree. The pure O-sequence associated with X is the vector h = (h_0, h_1, ..., h_e) where h_i is the number of monomials in X of degree i; here h_0 = 1, e is the common degree of the maximal monomials (the socle degree), and the number t = h_e of maximal monomials of X is called the type.

For fixed positive integers e and t, let P(*, e, t) denote the set of all pure O-sequences (in any number of variables) having socle degree e and type t, and let #P(*, e, t) denote its cardinality. (This set is finite, since a pure O-sequence of socle degree e and type t is determined by t monomials of degree e, and only finitely many monomials divide a given finite collection of monomials of bounded degree.)

Problem. For each fixed positive integer e, determine the asymptotic behavior of #P(*, e, t) as t → ∞. In particular, identify the correct order of magnitude of #P(*, e, t) as a function of t.

Let $\mathbb{H}=\{q=q_0+q_1 i+q_2 j+q_3 k : q_0,q_1,q_2,q_3\in\mathbb{R}\}$ denote the skew field of real quaternions, with the Hamilton multiplication rules $i^2=j^2=k^2=ijk=-1$. A quaternion-valued differential equation (QDE) is a system of the form
$$\dot{x}(t)=F(t,x(t),\mu),\qquad x(t)\in\mathbb{H}^n,$$
where $\mu\in\mathbb{R}^p$ (or $\mathbb{H}^p$) is a parameter and $F:\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{H}^n\times\mathbb{R}^p\to\mathbb{H}^n$ is a sufficiently smooth function in the appropriate quaternionic sense.

Develop a rigorous bifurcation theory for such QDEs subject to parametric perturbations. Specifically:

1. Provide an intrinsic definition of a Poincaré (return) map for a periodic orbit of a quaternion-valued differential equation that respects the noncommutative quaternionic structure (rather than relying solely on a real $4n$-dimensional realification), including a suitable notion of transverse cross-section in $\mathbb{H}^n$ and a quaternionic linearization (monodromy operator) whose spectral properties characterize stability.

2. Using this Poincaré map, formulate and prove quaternionic analogues of the classical local bifurcation theorems (saddle-node, period-doubling, Neimark–Sacker / Hopf-type) for periodic orbits of QDEs under perturbations, identifying the genericity and transversality conditions on the quaternionic eigenvalues of the monodromy operator under which each bifurcation phenomenon occurs.

Equivalently: can a bifurcation theory for QDEs subjected to perturbations be developed, and how should the Poincaré map be defined in the quaternion-valued setting so that bifurcation phenomena can be studied rigorously?

A general bifurcation theory for quaternion-valued differential equations with an intrinsic quaternionic Poincaré map does not appear in the literature. Existing bifurcation results in quaternion settings (e.g., Hopf bifurcation for fractional-order quaternion-valued neural networks) proceed by decomposing the quaternion system into an equivalent real-valued system via Hamilton's rules and applying classical real bifurcation theory, rather than constructing a genuine quaternionic Poincaré map. The problem of defining such a map intrinsically and developing the corresponding bifurcation theory remains open.

A finite simplicial complex Δ on vertex set {x_1,…,x_n} is a collection of subsets (faces) of {x_1,…,x_n} closed under taking subsets. A face of cardinality i+1 is called an i-face. The f-vector of Δ is f(Δ)=(f_0,f_1,…,f_d), where f_i is the number of i-faces of Δ and d is the maximum dimension of a face. The complex Δ is called pure if all its inclusion-maximal faces (facets) have the same dimension d. A pure f-vector is the f-vector of some pure simplicial complex; equivalently, it is the rank vector of a pure order ideal of squarefree monomials in n variables (the variables corresponding to the vertices). A finite sequence (a_0,a_1,…,a_d) of positive integers is called unimodal if there exists an index j with a_0 ≤ a_1 ≤ … ≤ a_j ≥ a_{j+1} ≥ … ≥ a_d, and nonunimodal otherwise.

Determine the smallest integer n for which there exists a pure simplicial complex on n vertices whose f-vector is nonunimodal.

Consider quaternion-valued differential equations (QDEs), i.e., systems of the form
   x'(t) = F(t, x(t), x(t - τ_1), …, x(t - τ_m)),
where x(t) ∈ ℍ^n (with ℍ the skew field of quaternions), F is a quaternion-valued (possibly linear or nonlinear) map, and τ_1, …, τ_m ≥ 0 are constant time delays. For real-valued delay differential equations it is well known that introducing delays may cause stability switches, Hopf bifurcations, and even chaotic dynamics.

Investigate the analogous phenomena in the quaternion-valued setting. Specifically:
(a) Develop a general qualitative theory describing how the introduction of a delay τ > 0 affects the stability of equilibria and periodic solutions of QDEs.
(b) Determine conditions under which a delay can induce a stability switch in a QDE that is asymptotically stable when τ = 0.
(c) Establish criteria (analogous to Hopf-bifurcation theorems) under which varying a delay parameter generates bifurcation of periodic orbits in QDEs, taking into account the noncommutativity of quaternion multiplication.
(d) Determine whether delayed QDEs can exhibit chaotic behavior, and if so, provide concrete classes of QDEs realizing such dynamics.

A finite matroid can be identified with a pure simplicial complex Δ on vertex set V = {1, 2, …, r} (the independence complex) with the property that, for every subset W ⊆ V, the restriction Δ|_W = {F ∈ Δ : F ⊆ W} is again a pure simplicial complex. Let f(Δ) = (f_{-1}, f_0, f_1, …, f_{d-1}) denote the f-vector of Δ, where f_i is the number of i-dimensional faces and d-1 is the dimension of Δ. Define the h-vector h(Δ) = (h_0, h_1, …, h_d) by the polynomial identity
   ∑_{i=0}^{d} f_{i-1} (x-1)^{d-i} = ∑_{i=0}^{d} h_i x^{d-i}.

A finite sequence (a_0, a_1, …, a_n) of nonnegative real numbers is called unimodal if there exists an index k with a_0 ≤ a_1 ≤ ⋯ ≤ a_k ≥ a_{k+1} ≥ ⋯ ≥ a_n, and log-concave if a_i^2 ≥ a_{i-1} a_{i+1} for every 1 ≤ i ≤ n-1.

Questions:
(a) Is the f-vector of every matroid (independence) complex unimodal? Is it log-concave?
(b) Is the h-vector of every matroid complex unimodal? Is it log-concave?

status_assertions.value: open_status:solved

The log-concavity of the f-vector of the independence complex of an arbitrary matroid (Mason–Welsh conjecture) was established by Adiprasito–Huh–Katz (Hodge theory for combinatorial geometries) and, in its ultra-log-concave form (Mason's conjecture), by Anari–Liu–Oveis Gharan–Vinzant and independently by Brändén–Huh. Log-concavity of the h-vector of a matroid complex (Dawson's conjecture) was first proved for matroids representable in characteristic 0 by Huh, and has since been established in further generality. Log-concavity implies unimodality for sequences of positive entries, so all of the listed questions are answered affirmatively.

$$\dot{x}(t)=A(t)\,x(t)+f(t),\qquad x(t)\in\mathbb{H}^n,\ A(t)\in\mathbb{H}^{n\times n},\ f(t)\in\mathbb{H}^n.$$
In real-variable analysis, a fuzzy number is a function $u:\mathbb{R}\to[0,1]$ that is normal, fuzzy convex, upper semicontinuous, and has compact support; the space $E^1$ of fuzzy numbers carries a metric $D$ and a notion of generalized Hukuhara differentiability under which fuzzy differential equations
$$\dot{x}(t)=F(t,x(t)),\qquad x(t)\in E^1,$$
are used to model dynamical systems with uncertainty.

Develop an analogous theory of fuzzy quaternion differential equations. Concretely:

(a) Propose a rigorous definition of a "fuzzy quaternion number," i.e., a class of mappings $u:\mathbb{H}\to[0,1]$ (or an equivalent level-set description via subsets of $\mathbb{H}$) extending the real fuzzy-number axioms, and equip the resulting space $E^{\mathbb{H}}$ with a suitable metric and arithmetic operations compatible with the noncommutative structure of $\mathbb{H}$.

(b) Define a notion of differentiability (for example a quaternionic generalized Hukuhara derivative) for mappings $x:[a,b]\to E^{\mathbb{H}}$ and formulate the corresponding initial-value problem
$$\dot{x}(t)=F(t,x(t)),\qquad x(t_0)=x_0\in E^{\mathbb{H}}.$$

(c) Establish existence, uniqueness, and stability theorems for such fuzzy quaternion differential equations, and in particular develop solution methods for the linear nonhomogeneous case in which $F(t,x)=A(t)x+f(t)$ with $A$ and $f$ having fuzzy quaternion-valued entries, thereby providing a mathematical framework for quaternion-valued dynamical systems subject to uncertainty or ambiguity.

Let $\mathbb{H}$ denote the skew field of real quaternions, i.e., $\mathbb{H}=\{a_0+a_1 i+a_2 j+a_3 k : a_0,a_1,a_2,a_3\in\mathbb{R}\}$ with $i^2=j^2=k^2=ijk=-1$. A quaternion-valued differential equation has the general linear nonhomogeneous form
$$\dot{x}(t)=A(t)\,x(t)+f(t),\qquad x(t)\in\mathbb{H}^n,\ A(t)\in\mathbb{H}^{n\times n},\ f(t)\in\mathbb{H}^n.$$
In real-variable analysis, a fuzzy number is a function $u:\mathbb{R}\to[0,1]$ that is normal, fuzzy convex, upper semicontinuous, and has compact support; the space $E^1$ of fuzzy numbers carries a metric $D$ and a notion of generalized Hukuhara differentiability under which fuzzy differential equations
$$\dot{x}(t)=F(t,x(t)),\qquad x(t)\in E^1,$$
are used to model dynamical systems with uncertainty.

Develop an analogous theory of fuzzy quaternion differential equations. Concretely:

(a) Propose a rigorous definition of a "fuzzy quaternion number," i.e., a class of mappings $u:\mathbb{H}\to[0,1]$ (or an equivalent level-set description via subsets of $\mathbb{H}$) extending the real fuzzy-number axioms, and equip the resulting space $E^{\mathbb{H}}$ with a suitable metric and arithmetic operations compatible with the noncommutative structure of $\mathbb{H}$.

(b) Define a notion of differentiability (for example a quaternionic generalized Hukuhara derivative) for mappings $x:[a,b]\to E^{\mathbb{H}}$ and formulate the corresponding initial-value problem
$$\dot{x}(t)=F(t,x(t)),\qquad x(t_0)=x_0\in E^{\mathbb{H}}.$$

(c) Establish existence, uniqueness, and stability theorems for such fuzzy quaternion differential equations, and in particular develop solution methods for the linear nonhomogeneous case in which $F(t,x)=A(t)x+f(t)$ with $A$ and $f$ having fuzzy quaternion-valued entries, thereby providing a mathematical framework for quaternion-valued dynamical systems subject to uncertainty or ambiguity.

Some progress has been made on this program. Yang, Xu, and Qi (2015) studied the Cauchy problem for quaternion fuzzy fractional differential equations, and subsequent work has addressed Hyers–Ulam–Rassias stability of high-dimensional quaternion impulsive fuzzy dynamic equations on time scales. However, a comprehensive theory of fuzzy quaternion differential equations parallel to the classical fuzzy ODE theory is not yet fully developed, so the broad program remains only partially solved.

Let $\Delta$ be a simplicial complex on vertex set $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ that is the independence complex of a matroid (i.e., $\Delta$ is nonempty, every subset of a face is a face, and for any two faces $F,G\in\Delta$ with $|F|<|G|$ there exists $x\in G\setminus F$ with $F\cup\{x\}\in\Delta$). Let $k$ be a field, $S=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, and let $I_\Delta\subset S$ be the Stanley–Reisner ideal generated by the squarefree monomials $\prod_{i\in F}x_i$ for $F\notin\Delta$. The Stanley–Reisner ring $S/I_\Delta$ is Cohen–Macaulay; let $h(\Delta)=(h_0,h_1,\ldots,h_d)$ denote its $h$-vector.

A finite, nonempty set $X$ of monomials in some polynomial ring $k[y_1,\ldots,y_r]$ is called an order ideal if it is closed under taking divisors. Such an order ideal $X$ is pure if all its maximal monomials (under divisibility) have the same total degree. The $O$-sequence of $X$ is the vector $(f_0,f_1,\ldots,f_e)$ where $f_i$ is the number of monomials of degree $i$ in $X$; a sequence of nonnegative integers is called a pure $O$-sequence if it arises in this way from some pure order ideal.

Prove or disprove: For every matroid complex $\Delta$, the $h$-vector $h(\Delta)$ is a pure $O$-sequence.

Let $\mathbb{H}$ denote the skew field of real quaternions $q = q_0 + q_1 i + q_2 j + q_3 k$, where $i^2 = j^2 = k^2 = ijk = -1$. A quaternion-valued differential equation (QDE) is a system of the form
$$\dot{x}(t) = A(t)\, x(t) + f(t), \qquad x(t) \in \mathbb{H}^n,$$
where $A: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{H}^{n\times n}$ and $f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{H}^n$, with multiplication interpreted in $\mathbb{H}$ (and so being noncommutative).

Develop a theory of quaternion-valued optimization and applied modeling based on QDEs by addressing the following:

(a) Identify and rigorously formulate concrete classes of real-world phenomena — in particular in engineering control, color recognition, color image compression, and robotic systems control — for which a quaternion-valued model
$$\dot{x}(t) = F(t, x(t)), \qquad x(t) \in \mathbb{H}^n,$$
captures structural information (e.g. coupled spatial/chromatic components, three-dimensional rotations) that cannot be captured by an equivalent real-valued model of the same dimension. Provide precise criteria distinguishing QDE models from their real componentwise reductions.

(b) Formulate a notion of quaternion-valued optimization problem
$$\min_{x \in \Omega \subseteq \mathbb{H}^n} J(x), \qquad J: \mathbb{H}^n \to \mathbb{R},$$
including suitable definitions of quaternion gradient, quaternion Hessian, convexity and KKT-type optimality conditions adapted to the noncommutative structure of $\mathbb{H}$, and prove existence, uniqueness, and characterization theorems analogous to those in real or complex optimization.

(c) Derive algorithms (e.g. quaternion gradient descent, Newton-type, or Pontryagin-type optimal control schemes for QDEs) with provable convergence guarantees, and apply them to the modeling problems identified in (a).

Let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero, and let $R = K[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ be the standard graded polynomial ring. Let $I \subset R$ be a homogeneous ideal generated by a regular sequence $f_1, \dots, f_n$ of forms of positive degree, so that $A = R/I$ is an artinian graded complete intersection $K$-algebra, with graded decomposition $A = \bigoplus_{i \geq 0} A_i$.

One says that $A$ has the Weak Lefschetz Property (WLP) if there exists a linear form $\ell \in A_1$ such that, for every $i \geq 0$, the multiplication map
$$\times \ell : A_i \longrightarrow A_{i+1}$$
has maximal rank (that is, is either injective or surjective).

Question: Does every artinian graded complete intersection $A = K[x_1, \dots, x_n]/(f_1, \dots, f_n)$ (over a field of characteristic zero) have the Weak Lefschetz Property?

The problem is known to be true in codimension at most 3 (over a field of characteristic zero) and for monomial complete intersections in any codimension, but remains open in general for codimension at least 4. Recent work (e.g., results on height-four equigenerated complete intersections, 2022–2025) establishes WLP in special cases such as forms of equal degree d=3,4,5 and in various degree ranges, but the full conjecture is unresolved.

A pure order ideal is a finite, nonempty collection X of monomials in some polynomial ring k[x_1,...,x_n] that is closed under taking divisors (if M ∈ X and N divides M then N ∈ X) and in which all maximal monomials (with respect to divisibility) have the same total degree. The h-vector (or pure O-sequence) associated with X is the integer sequence h = (h_0, h_1, ..., h_e), where h_i is the number of monomials of degree i in X and e is the common degree of the maximal monomials. A sequence of nonnegative integers is called a pure O-sequence (in n variables) if it arises in this way for some pure order ideal in k[x_1,...,x_n].

Interval Conjecture for Pure O-sequences (ICP). Suppose that
  h = (h_0, h_1, ..., h_{i-1}, h_i, h_{i+1}, ..., h_e)
and
  h' = (h_0, h_1, ..., h_{i-1}, h_i + α, h_{i+1}, ..., h_e),
for some index i and some positive integer α, are both pure O-sequences. Then for every integer β with 1 ≤ β ≤ α − 1, the sequence
  (h_0, h_1, ..., h_{i-1}, h_i + β, h_{i+1}, ..., h_e)
is also a pure O-sequence.

Question. Does the ICP hold for pure O-sequences in three variables (n = 3)?

Background and definitions. For a smooth manifold $M$, let $\mathcal{P}(M)$ denote the set of all smooth positive probability densities on $M$, that is, the set of smooth volume forms (or, after fixing a reference volume, smooth positive functions) $p$ on $M$ with $\int_M p = 1$. A smooth diffeomorphism $\varphi : M \to M$ is called equiaffine (volume-preserving in the sense of preserving a fixed smooth volume form $\mu_0$) if $\varphi^* \mu_0 = \mu_0$; more generally, we consider the manifold of smooth transformations of $M$ that preserve a fixed equiaffine structure. Denote this manifold by $\mathrm{EqAff}(M)$.

Known fact (to be assumed). When $M = S^1$, the space $\mathcal{P}(S^1)$ is diffeomorphic, as an infinite-dimensional manifold, to $\mathrm{EqAff}(S^1)$.

Problem. Determine whether the analogous statements hold in the following two cases:

(a) $M = S^n$ (the $n$-dimensional sphere) for $n \geq 2$: is $\mathcal{P}(S^n)$ diffeomorphic to $\mathrm{EqAff}(S^n)$?

(b) $M = \mathbb{R}^n$: is $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ diffeomorphic to $\mathrm{EqAff}(\mathbb{R}^n)$?

In each case, either construct an explicit diffeomorphism between the space of smooth positive probability densities and the manifold of smooth equiaffine transformations, or prove that no such diffeomorphism exists.

The classification of finite projective planes, and even the determination of the possible orders, is a long-standing open problem. It is known that every prime power is an order (Desarguesian planes), the Bruck–Ryser–Chowla theorem rules out infinitely many non-prime-power orders, and computer-assisted work (Lam, Thiel, Swiercz, 1989) ruled out order 10. The smallest order whose existence is unresolved is 12; no projective plane of non-prime-power order is known.

Let $(M,g)$ be a (smooth, connected) Riemannian manifold. A statistical structure on $(M,g)$ is a triple $(g,
abla,
abla^*)$, where $
abla$ and $
abla^*$ are torsion-free affine connections on $M$ that are dual with respect to $g$, meaning that for all vector fields $X,Y,Z$ on $M$,
$$X\,g(Y,Z) \;=\; g(
abla_X Y, Z) \;+\; g(Y, 
abla^*_X Z).$$
Given any symmetric $(0,3)$-tensor field $T$ on $M$, one obtains such a dual pair by setting
$$g(
abla_X Y, Z) \;=\; g(
abla^{LC}_X Y, Z) - 	frac{1}{2} T(X,Y,Z), \qquad g(
abla^*_X Y, Z) \;=\; g(
abla^{LC}_X Y, Z) + 	frac{1}{2} T(X,Y,Z),$$
where $
abla^{LC}$ is the Levi-Civita connection of $g$. The quadruple $\{M,g,
abla,
abla^*\}$ is called a dually flat space when both $
abla$ and $
abla^*$ are flat (zero curvature and zero torsion).

Address the following:

(a) Does every Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$ admit a symmetric $(0,3)$-tensor field $T$ for which the resulting quadruple $\{M,g,
abla,
abla^*\}$ is a dually flat space? If not, characterize those Riemannian manifolds for which such a $T$ exists.

(b) When such a tensor $T$ exists but is not unique, describe and classify the family of dually flat structures on $(M,g)$ obtainable in this way (for example, in terms of the space of admissible cubic forms $T$, or the moduli of compatible Hessian/affine-flat coordinate systems on $M$).

The literature establishes that dually flat structures correspond locally to Hessian structures and to pairs of affine-flat coordinates, and existence imposes strong topological/affine constraints (e.g., the underlying manifold must admit a flat torsion-free connection, hence vanishing rational Pontryagin classes). Recent work (e.g., on moduli of left-invariant statistical structures on Lie groups, dually flat structures for singular models, and Hessian geometry) treats classification in special settings, but a complete general answer characterizing all Riemannian manifolds admitting a dually flat enhancement and classifying the moduli of such structures does not appear to have been given. Status appears unresolved in full generality.

A Steiner system S(t, k, v) is a v-element set V together with a collection B of k-element subsets of V (called blocks) such that every t-element subset of V is contained in exactly one block of B.

A finite sequence (h_0, h_1, …, h_d) of positive integers is called a pure O-sequence if there exists a finite, nonempty set M of monomials in some polynomial ring k[x_1, …, x_n] such that:
(i) all monomials in M have the same degree d, and
(ii) for each i = 0, 1, …, d, h_i equals the number of distinct monomials of degree i that divide at least one monomial of M.

Question: Does there exist a Steiner system S(4, 5, 21)? Equivalently, is the sequence (1, 21, 210, 1330, 5985, 1197) a pure O-sequence?

Let $\mathcal{S} = \{p_	heta : 	heta \in \Theta\}$ be a smooth statistical manifold of probability distributions on a measurable space $(\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{B})$, equipped with the Fisher information metric $g$ and a dual pair $(
abla, 
abla^*)$ of torsion-free affine connections satisfying
$$X\, g(Y,Z) = g(
abla_X Y, Z) + g(Y, 
abla^*_X Z),$$
for all vector fields $X,Y,Z$ on $\mathcal{S}$. Recall that the $\alpha$-connections of Amari, $
abla^{(\alpha)}$ and $
abla^{(-\alpha)}$, form such a dual pair, and that $(\mathcal{S}, g, 
abla^{(1)}, 
abla^{(-1)})$ is dually flat with canonical divergence given by the Kullback–Leibler relative entropy
$$D(p\,\|\,q) = \int_{\mathcal{X}} p \log rac{p}{q}\, d\mu.$$

Recall also that a sequence $(\mu_n)_{n \geq 1}$ of probability measures on a Polish space $\mathcal{Y}$ is said to satisfy a large deviation principle (LDP) with rate function $I : \mathcal{Y} 	o [0,\infty]$ if $I$ is lower semicontinuous and
$$-\inf_{y\in A^\circ} I(y) \le \liminf_{n	o\infty} rac{1}{n}\log\mu_n(A) \le \limsup_{n	o\infty} rac{1}{n}\log\mu_n(A) \le -\inf_{y\in \overline{A}} I(y)$$
for every Borel set $A \subseteq \mathcal{Y}$. By Sanov's theorem, the empirical measures of i.i.d.\ samples drawn from $p \in \mathcal{S}$ satisfy an LDP on the space of probability measures with rate function $I(q) = D(q\,\|\,p)$.

Problem. Formulate and establish a precise mathematical correspondence between large deviation principles whose rate functions arise as relative entropies (or, more generally, $f$-divergences) and the dual affine connection structure $(
abla, 
abla^*)$ on $\mathcal{S}$. In particular, characterize how the geometric quantities associated with $(g, 
abla, 
abla^*)$ — geodesics, dually flat coordinates, the canonical divergence, and the generalized Pythagorean theorem — control the asymptotics, contraction principles, and conditional limit theorems associated with such LDPs, and conversely how the LDP rate function determines the dual connection pair via its Legendre–Fenchel structure.

Let $\mathbb{F}_2 = \{0,1\}$ denote the field with two elements, and for a positive integer $n$ regard $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ as the Boolean cube equipped with the uniform probability measure. For functions $f, g : \mathbb{F}_2^n \to \mathbb{F}_2$, define their correlation by
$$\mathrm{Corr}(f,g) \;=\; \Big|\,\mathbb{E}_{x \in \mathbb{F}_2^n}\!\left[(-1)^{f(x)+g(x)}\right]\Big|.$$
Call a family of functions $\{f_n : \mathbb{F}_2^n \to \mathbb{F}_2\}_{n \ge 1}$ "explicit" if the language $\{(n,x) : f_n(x) = 1\}$ lies in the complexity class $\mathrm{NP}$.

Question: Does there exist an explicit family of functions $\{f_n : \mathbb{F}_2^n \to \mathbb{F}_2\}_{n \ge 1}$ such that, for every sufficiently large $n$ and every multivariate polynomial $p \in \mathbb{F}_2[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ of total degree at most $\log_2 n$, one has
$$\Big|\,\mathbb{E}_{x \in \mathbb{F}_2^n}\!\left[(-1)^{f_n(x)+p(x)}\right]\Big| \;\le\; \frac{1}{n}\,?$$

Setup. Let $M$ be a smooth manifold. A statistical manifold structure on $M$ is a triple $(g,
abla,
abla^*)$, where $g$ is a (pseudo-)Riemannian metric and $
abla,
abla^*$ are torsion-free affine connections on $M$ that are dual with respect to $g$, i.e. for all vector fields $X,Y,Z$ on $M$,
$$X\,g(Y,Z)=g(
abla_X Y,Z)+g(Y,
abla^*_X Z).$$
Equivalently, the Amari–Chentsov tensor $C(X,Y,Z):=g(
abla_X Y-
abla^{(g)}_X Y,Z)$ is totally symmetric in $X,Y,Z$, where $
abla^{(g)}$ is the Levi–Civita connection of $g$.

A parametric family $\{p(x,\xi):\xi\in M\}$ of probability density functions on a measurable space $(\mathcal X,\mu)$, with $\xi$ ranging over the manifold $M$, is said to induce a statistical manifold structure $(g_F,
abla^{(\alpha)},
abla^{(-\alpha)})$ via the Fisher information metric
$$g_F(\partial_i,\partial_j)(\xi)=\int_{\mathcal X}\partial_i\log p(x,\xi)\,\partial_j\log p(x,\xi)\,p(x,\xi)\,d\mu(x),$$
together with the Amari $\pm\alpha$-connections, whose Amari–Chentsov tensor is
$$C(\partial_i,\partial_j,\partial_k)(\xi)=\int_{\mathcal X}\partial_i\log p\,\partial_j\log p\,\partial_k\log p\,\,p(x,\xi)\,d\mu(x).$$
Say that an abstract statistical manifold $(M,g,
abla,
abla^*)$ is realizable by probability distributions if there exists such a family $\{p(x,\xi)\}$ on some $(\mathcal X,\mu)$ whose induced metric and dual connections coincide with $(g,
abla,
abla^*)$.

The dually flat case: $(M,g,
abla,
abla^*)$ is called dually flat if both $
abla$ and $
abla^*$ are flat (zero curvature and torsion).

Problem.
(a) Find necessary and sufficient conditions on an abstract statistical manifold $(M,g,
abla,
abla^*)$ for it to be realizable by a family of probability distributions in the sense above.
(b) Specialize: give necessary and sufficient conditions, in the dually flat case, for $(M,g,
abla,
abla^*)$ to be realizable as the statistical manifold associated to such a family of probability distributions (e.g. an exponential family with Fisher metric and $\pm 1$-connections).

Partial results exist. In the dually flat setting, there is a well-known correspondence with Bregman divergences and exponential families: any regular dually flat statistical manifold induces, via Legendre duality of a convex potential, an exponential-family-type representation, and conversely exponential families produce dually flat structures (Amari, Nagaoka, and subsequent work). Realization criteria via affine immersions (e.g., centroaffine immersions of codimension two by Kurose and others) provide geometric, but not full distribution-level, characterizations. This is Tomaszewski's 1986 conjecture on randomly signed sums. It was proved by Nathan Keller and Ohad Klein in 2020 (arXiv:2006.16834), with the proof later published in Advances in Mathematics (2022). Their proof combines a refined Berry–Esseen inequality for Rademacher sums, local concentration inequalities, and case analysis on the sizes of the coefficients.

A compact affine flat manifold is a compact smooth manifold $M$ equipped with a flat torsion-free affine connection on its tangent bundle; equivalently, $M$ admits an atlas whose transition maps are restrictions of affine transformations of $\mathbb{R}^n$. Such a manifold is called complete if its universal cover is affinely diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^n$, in which case $M = \mathbb{R}^n / \Gamma$ for a discrete subgroup $\Gamma$ of the affine group $\mathrm{Aff}(\mathbb{R}^n) = \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{R}) \ltimes \mathbb{R}^n$ acting freely and properly discontinuously, and $\Gamma \cong \pi_1(M)$.

Characterize the class of groups that arise as the fundamental group $\pi_1(M)$ of some compact affine flat manifold $M$. In particular, determine whether every such fundamental group must be virtually solvable (the Auslander conjecture in the complete case), and more generally describe all groups that can occur.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The problem is closely tied to the Auslander conjecture, which asserts that fundamental groups of compact complete affine flat manifolds are virtually solvable. The conjecture is known in dimensions ≤ 6 (Abels–Margulis–Soifer) and in low-dimensional or Lorentzian holonomy cases (Fried–Goldman), but remains open in general. The broader characterization of all possible fundamental groups of compact affine flat manifolds is also unresolved.

Let $n\ge 1$ and consider the discrete cube $\{-1,1\}^n$ equipped with the uniform probability measure. For a parameter $0<\rho<1$, define the noise (Bonami–Beckner) operator $T_\rho$ acting on functions $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ by
$$(T_\rho f)(x) \;=\; \mathbb{E}\bigl[f(y)\bigm| x\bigr],$$
where $y\in\{-1,1\}^n$ is the random vector whose $i$-th coordinate equals $x_i$ with probability $\tfrac{1+\rho}{2}$ and $-x_i$ with probability $\tfrac{1-\rho}{2}$, independently across coordinates.

Prove or disprove: for every fixed $0<\rho<1$, every $n\ge 1$, and every nonnegative function $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ with $\mathbb{E}[f]=1$, the upper tail of $T_\rho f$ satisfies
$$\Pr\bigl[T_\rho f \ge t\bigr] \;=\; o\!\left(\frac{1}{t}\right) \qquad \text{as } t\to\infty,$$
where the $o(1/t)$ rate is allowed to depend on $\rho$ but not on $n$ or $f$.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Talagrand's convolution conjecture was established on Gaussian space by Eldan and Lee (2014), giving a dimension-free improvement over Markov's inequality. On the Boolean hypercube the conjecture remained open for decades; in 2025 Yuansi Chen proved a near-resolution, obtaining a tail bound of order $(\log\log t)/(t\sqrt{\log t})$ via a perturbed reverse-heat-flow argument, which falls short of the conjectured $o(1/t)$ only by a $\log\log t$ factor. Thus the precise statement remains open, but the conjecture is essentially resolved up to a doubly-logarithmic factor.

Let $n \geq 1$ and let $f : \{-1,1\}^n \to \{-1,1\}$ be a Boolean function. The (real) degree $\deg(f)$ of $f$ is the degree of the unique multilinear polynomial $p \in \mathbb{R}[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ such that $p(x) = f(x)$ for all $x \in \{-1,1\}^n$. For $x \in \{-1,1\}^n$ and $i \in [n]$, let $x^i$ denote the input obtained from $x$ by flipping the $i$-th coordinate. The sensitivity of $f$ at $x$ is $s(f,x) = |\{ i \in [n] : f(x) \neq f(x^i)\}|$, and the (maximum) sensitivity of $f$ is $\mathrm{sens}[f] = \max_{x \in \{-1,1\}^n} s(f,x)$.

Question: Does there exist a polynomial $P$ such that for every $n \geq 1$ and every Boolean function $f : \{-1,1\}^n \to \{-1,1\}$,
$$\deg(f) \leq P(\mathrm{sens}[f]) ?$$

status_assertions.value: open_status:solved

This is the Sensitivity Conjecture of Nisan and Szegedy. It was resolved positively by Hao Huang in 2019, who proved that the block sensitivity (and hence the degree, via known polynomial relations) is at most a polynomial in the sensitivity; specifically, $\deg(f) \leq \mathrm{sens}[f]^4$ via the chain $\deg(f) \leq \mathrm{bs}(f)^2$ combined with Huang's $\mathrm{bs}(f) \leq \mathrm{sens}(f)^2$ (in fact $\mathrm{sens}(f) \geq \sqrt{\deg(f)}$ up to constants).

Background. In classical surface theory, a minimal surface in Euclidean 3-space always admits isothermal coordinates: local coordinates (u,v) in which the induced first fundamental form takes the conformal shape E(du^2+dv^2) for some positive function E.

In affine differential geometry of nondegenerate surfaces in the unimodular affine 3-space R^3, every immersed surface M^2 ⊂ R^3 with nondegenerate second fundamental form carries a canonically defined symmetric bilinear form h, called the affine (Berwald–Blaschke) fundamental form (or affine metric), defined invariantly under equiaffine transformations by
   h_{ij} = L_{ij} / |det(L_{kl})|^{1/4},
where L_{ij} is the classical second fundamental form expressed in any local parameterization. The mean curvature of h with respect to the affine normal is the affine mean curvature, and M is called an affine minimal surface when this affine mean curvature vanishes identically.

Problem. Let M be an affine minimal surface in R^3 (so that h is a Riemannian or Lorentzian nondegenerate metric on M). Do there always exist, locally around every point of M, isothermal coordinates with respect to the affine fundamental form h, i.e. local coordinates (u,v) in which
   h = λ(u,v) (du^2 ± dv^2)
for some smooth positive function λ (with the sign depending on whether h is definite or indefinite)?

A targeted web search did not return any source establishing or refuting the existence of isothermal coordinates with respect to the affine fundamental form on affine minimal surfaces. For real-analytic or smooth nondegenerate metrics in dimension two, the classical Korn–Lichtenstein theorem provides isothermal coordinates whenever h is positive definite and sufficiently regular, but no specific reference confirming this is asserted in the affine-minimal context, and the indefinite case is more subtle. Status appears unresolved from accessible search evidence.

Let n and k be positive integers with k ≤ n. A function f : {−1,1}^n → {−1,1} is called a degree-k polynomial threshold function (PTF) if there exists a real multivariate polynomial P(x_1,…,x_n) of degree at most k such that f(x) = sgn(P(x)) for all x ∈ {−1,1}^n. The (total) influence of f is

  I(f) = ∑_{i=1}^n Pr_{x ∼ {−1,1}^n}[ f(x) ≠ f(x^{(i)}) ],

where x^{(i)} denotes x with its i-th coordinate flipped, and the probability is with respect to the uniform distribution on {−1,1}^n.

For each n and k, define the "symmetric candidate" g_{n,k} : {−1,1}^n → {−1,1} by

  g_{n,k}(x) = sgn( p(x_1 + x_2 + ⋯ + x_n) ),

where p is a univariate polynomial of degree k chosen so that p alternates sign on the k+1 values of the sum s = x_1 + ⋯ + x_n that lie closest to 0 (with the convention that when n−k is even these are the k+1 values −k, −k+2, …, k, and otherwise the k+1 values −k, −k+2, …, k−1, k+1 closest to 0; equivalently, p has its k real roots placed between the k+1 layers of the Boolean cube whose Hamming weight is closest to n/2).

Question: Is it true that for every n ≥ k ≥ 1,

  max{ I(f) : f is a degree-k PTF on {−1,1}^n } = I(g_{n,k}),

i.e., the maximum total influence over all degree-k PTFs is always attained by this symmetric "alternating layers" threshold function?

This is the Gotsman–Linial conjecture (1991) on the maximal average sensitivity (total influence) of degree-k polynomial threshold functions. A 2021 preprint by Daniel Kane titled "The Gotsman–Linial Conjecture is False" disproves the conjecture for almost all degrees d and almost all n, while confirming it in some remaining cases. Hence, as stated, the answer to the question is no.

Let $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ denote the $n$-dimensional vector space over the field with two elements, and for subsets $A,B \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ write $A+B = \{a+b : a \in A,\, b \in B\}$. An affine subspace of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ is a coset $v + V$ of a linear subspace $V \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$.

Prove or disprove the following statement: there exists a polynomial $p$ such that, for every positive integer $n$, every real number $C \geq 1$, and every nonempty finite set $A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ satisfying
$$|A+A| \leq C\,|A|,$$
the set $A$ can be covered by at most $p(C)$ affine subspaces of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$, each of cardinality at most $|A|$.

The Polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa conjecture over F_2 (Marton's conjecture) was proved in 2023 by Gowers, Green, Manners, and Tao (arXiv:2311.05762, "On a conjecture of Marton"). They establish that if |A+A| ≤ C|A| in F_2^n, then A is covered by poly(C) translates of a subspace of size at most |A|, in fact equivalent to the formulation in the problem. The proof has been fully formalized in Lean 4.

Let $(M,h)$ be a smooth Riemannian manifold. Using $h$ to identify $TM$ with $T^*M$, pull back the canonical symplectic form on $T^*M$ to obtain a canonical symplectic form $\omega$ on $TM$. Let $
abla$ be any torsion-free affine connection on $M$. The horizontal-vertical splitting $T(TM) = H^
abla \oplus V$ induced by $
abla$, together with the canonical isomorphism $V_v \cong T_{\pi(v)}M \cong H^
abla_v$ (where $\pi:TM	o M$ is the projection), determines an almost complex structure $J$ on $TM$ by
$$J(X^H) = X^V, \qquad J(X^V) = -X^H,$$
for every tangent vector $X$ on $M$ (lifted horizontally and vertically). It is known that the pair $(\omega, J)$ is compatible (i.e., $\omega(\cdot, J\cdot)$ is a symmetric positive-definite form and $\omega(J\cdot,J\cdot)=\omega(\cdot,\cdot)$) if and only if $
abla$ is compatible with $h$ (equivalently, $
abla$ is the Levi-Civita connection of $h$).

Problem: Give an intrinsic characterization of those symplectic manifolds $(N,\Omega)$ equipped with a compatible almost complex structure $\mathcal{J}$ which arise locally in the above way. That is, determine necessary and sufficient local conditions on $(N,\Omega,\mathcal{J})$ guaranteeing that, near every point of $N$, there exist a Riemannian manifold $(M,h)$ and a torsion-free affine connection $
abla$ on $M$ compatible with $h$, together with a local diffeomorphism from an open subset of $N$ onto an open subset of $TM$ pulling back $(\omega, J)$ to $(\Omega, \mathcal{J})$.

representations.normalized:
For a Boolean function $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, let its Fourier expansion be $f(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]} \hat f(S)\,\chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S} x_i$, and recall Parseval's identity $\sum_S \hat f(S)^2 = 1$. For $\varepsilon>0$, say that the Fourier spectrum of $f$ is $\varepsilon$-concentrated on a collection $\mathcal F\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ if $\sum_{S\notin\mathcal F} \hat f(S)^2 \le \varepsilon$.

A DNF formula of size $s$ is a disjunction of at most $s$ terms, where each term is a conjunction of literals from $x_1,\dots,x_n$ (and their negations). A function $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ is computable by a DNF of size $s$ if it equals such a formula under the standard $\{-1,1\}$ encoding of Boolean values.

Question: Is it true that there exists an absolute constant $C>0$ such that for every integer $s>1$, every $\varepsilon\in(0,1/2]$, and every $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ computable by a DNF of size $s$, the Fourier spectrum of $f$ is $\varepsilon$-concentrated on some collection $\mathcal F\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ with $|\mathcal F| \le s^{C\log(1/\varepsilon)}$?

Setup. Let $(M,
abla,h)$ be an $n$-dimensional statistical manifold; that is, $M$ is a smooth manifold, $h$ is a (pseudo-)Riemannian metric on $M$, and $
abla$ is a torsion-free affine connection on $M$ such that the $(0,3)$-tensor $
abla h$ is totally symmetric. Let $ ar
abla$ denote the dual (conjugate) connection of $
abla$ with respect to $h$, defined by
$$X\,h(Y,Z)=h(
abla_X Y,Z)+h(Y, ar
abla_X Z)$$
for all vector fields $X,Y,Z$ on $M$. Then $(M, ar
abla,h)$ is again a statistical manifold.

Recall that a statistical manifold $(M,
abla,h)$ is called $1$-conformally flat if, locally around each point, there exists a positive smooth function $\phi$ such that the conformally related statistical structure $(	ilde
abla,	ilde h)$ defined by
$$	ilde h = \phi\, h, \qquad h(	ilde
abla_X Y, Z)=h(
abla_X Y, Z)-(d\log\phi)(Z)\,h(X,Y)$$
is flat (i.e.\ $	ilde
abla$ is a flat affine connection and $	ilde h$ is a Hessian metric for $	ilde
abla$).

Construction of the distribution. Fix $p\in M$ and let $U\subset M$ be a $
abla$-convex neighborhood of $p$, meaning that for every $q\in U$ there is a unique $
abla$-geodesic in $U$ from $p$ to $q$. For each $q\in U\setminus\{p\}$, let $v_q\in T_qM$ denote the velocity at $q$ of the $
abla$-geodesic from $p$ to $q$, and define the rank-$(n-1)$ distribution
$$D_q := \{w\in T_qM : h(w,v_q)=0\}.$$

Question. Suppose that for every choice of base point $p\in M$ and every $
abla$-convex neighborhood $U$ of $p$, the distribution $D$ on $U\setminus\{p\}$ constructed as above is integrable (in the sense of Frobenius). Must the dual statistical manifold $(M, ar
abla,h)$ then be $1$-conformally flat?

For a finite set $T \subset \mathbb{R}^n$, define
$$b(T) = \mathbb{E}_{\varepsilon}\Big[\max_{t \in T} \langle t, \varepsilon\rangle\Big],$$
where $\varepsilon = (\varepsilon_1,\dots,\varepsilon_n)$ has independent components uniform on $\{-1,+1\}$, and define
$$g(T) = \mathbb{E}_{X}\Big[\max_{t \in T} \langle t, X\rangle\Big],$$
where $X = (X_1,\dots,X_n)$ has independent standard Gaussian components.

Prove or disprove: there exists an absolute constant $C > 0$ such that for every finite set $T \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ (and every $n$), one can find a finite set $T' \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ with
$$g(T') \le C\, b(T),$$
and such that for every $t \in T$ there exists $t' \in T'$ with
$$\|t - t'\|_1 \le C\, b(T).$$

For a Boolean function $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, write its Fourier–Walsh expansion as
$$f(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}\widehat{f}(S)\,\chi_S(x),\qquad \chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}x_i,$$
where $\widehat{f}(S)=2^{-n}\sum_{x\in\{-1,1\}^n}f(x)\chi_S(x)$. Parseval's identity gives $\sum_S \widehat{f}(S)^2=1$, so $\{\widehat{f}(S)^2\}_{S\subseteq[n]}$ is a probability distribution on the subsets of $[n]$. Define the spectral entropy
$$H[\widehat{f}^{\,2}]=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]} \widehat{f}(S)^2 \log_2\!\left(\frac{1}{\widehat{f}(S)^2}\right),$$
with the convention $0\log(1/0)=0$. The total influence is
$$I[f]=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]} |S|\,\widehat{f}(S)^2,$$
equivalently $I[f]=\sum_{i=1}^n \Pr_x[f(x)\neq f(x^{\oplus i})]$, where $x^{\oplus i}$ flips the $i$-th coordinate of $x$.

Question: Does there exist a universal constant $C>0$, independent of $n$, such that for every $n\geq 1$ and every Boolean function $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$,
$$H[\widehat{f}^{\,2}]\;\leq\; C\cdot I[f]\;?$$

Let $\Sigma$ be a Riemann surface equipped with a projectively flat connection $\nabla$ (that is, a torsion-free affine connection whose unparametrized geodesics define a flat projective structure on $\Sigma$). Let $\gamma:S^1\to\Sigma$ be an immersed closed curve.

A point $p=\gamma(t)$ is called an inflection point of $\gamma$ if the velocity vector $\dot\gamma(t)$ and the acceleration $\nabla_{\dot\gamma}\dot\gamma(t)$ are linearly dependent (equivalently, if $\gamma$ has higher-order contact with a $\nabla$-geodesic at $p$). At a non-inflection point one may, using the projectively flat structure, define a notion of osculating conic; an affine vertex of $\gamma$ is a point at which the osculating conic has contact of order at least five with $\gamma$ (equivalently, a critical point of the projective/affine curvature function defined off the inflection locus).

Assume that the set of inflection points of $\gamma$ is isolated, and let $V(\gamma)$ denote the number of affine vertices of $\gamma$ and $I(\gamma)$ the number of inflection points.

Establish a sharp lower bound for $V(\gamma)$ in terms of topological and geometric invariants of $(\Sigma,\nabla,\gamma)$, and determine the precise relationship (for instance, an inequality of the form $V(\gamma)\ge f(I(\gamma))$ or a parity/congruence relation) between $V(\gamma)$ and $I(\gamma)$ that holds for every such curve.

Let n be an odd positive integer. For a Boolean function f : {-1,1}^n → {-1,1} and a parameter ρ ∈ [0,1], the noise stability of f at ρ is defined as
   Stab_ρ[f] = E[f(x) f(y)],
where x is uniformly distributed on {-1,1}^n and y ∈ {-1,1}^n is the ρ-correlated copy of x (each coordinate y_i independently equals x_i with probability (1+ρ)/2 and -x_i with probability (1-ρ)/2).

A linear threshold function (LTF) on {-1,1}^n is a function of the form f(x) = sign(a_0 + a_1 x_1 + ⋯ + a_n x_n) for some real coefficients a_0, a_1, …, a_n (with the convention that sign(0) is fixed to be either +1 or -1). The majority function on n (odd) variables is Maj_n(x) = sign(x_1 + x_2 + ⋯ + x_n).

Question: Is it true that for every odd n and every linear threshold function f : {-1,1}^n → {-1,1}, one has
   Stab_ρ[f] ≥ Stab_ρ[Maj_n]   for all ρ ∈ [0,1]?

Let $r \in \mathbb{N}$, let $n$ be an odd positive integer, and fix $\epsilon \in (0, 1/2)$. For $x \in \{-1,1\}^n$, an $\epsilon$-noisy copy $y$ of $x$ is the random vector obtained by independently, for each coordinate $i \in \{1,\dots,n\}$, setting $y_i = x_i$ with probability $1-\epsilon$ and $y_i = -x_i$ with probability $\epsilon$. For a function $f : \{-1,1\}^n \to \{-1,1\}$, define
$$P(f) \;=\; \Pr\!\left[f(y^{(1)}) = f(y^{(2)}) = \cdots = f(y^{(r)})\right],$$
where $x \in \{-1,1\}^n$ is chosen uniformly at random and, conditional on $x$, the vectors $y^{(1)},\dots,y^{(r)}$ are independent $\epsilon$-noisy copies of $x$. A function $f$ is called odd if $f(-x) = -f(x)$ for every $x$. For each odd $k \le n$, let $\mathrm{Maj}_k : \{-1,1\}^n \to \{-1,1\}$ be the function that depends only on the first $k$ coordinates and outputs the sign of their sum.

Question: Is it true that, for every choice of $r$, odd $n$, and $\epsilon \in (0,1/2)$, the maximum of $P(f)$ over all odd functions $f : \{-1,1\}^n \to \{-1,1\}$ is attained by $\mathrm{Maj}_k$ for some odd $k \le n$?

Background and definitions. A Hessian manifold is a smooth manifold $M$ equipped with a flat affine connection $
abla$ and a Riemannian metric $g$ such that, locally around every point, there exist affine coordinates $x^1,\dots,x^n$ (i.e. coordinates in which the Christoffel symbols of $
abla$ vanish) and a smooth real-valued function $\varphi$ with
$$g_{ij} \;=\;  rac{\partial^2 \varphi}{\partial x^i \partial x^j}.$$
Given such a Hessian structure, the tangent bundle $TM$ carries a canonical complex structure: in any affine local chart $(x^1,\dots,x^n)$ on $M$ with fiber coordinates $(y^1,\dots,y^n)$ (so that a tangent vector at $x$ is $\sum_i y^i\,\partial/\partial x^i$), the functions
$$z^j \;=\; x^j + \sqrt{-1}\,y^j, \qquad j=1,\dots,n,$$
serve as holomorphic coordinates on $TM$, and the resulting complex structure is independent of the choice of affine chart. With respect to this complex structure, the metric on $TM$ obtained from $g$ via the local Kähler potential $\varphi(x^1,\dots,x^n)$ (extended to $TM$ in the obvious way) is Kähler.

A complex manifold $X$ is called a Stein manifold if it is holomorphically convex and holomorphic functions separate points of $X$.

Problem. 
(a) Let $(M,g)$ be a Hessian manifold and assume that the Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$ is complete. Endow $TM$ with the canonical complex structure described above. Is $TM$ necessarily a Stein manifold?

(b) Specifically, let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a convex domain that contains no complete affine line, and let $\Gamma$ be a discrete subgroup of the affine automorphism group of $\Omega$ acting freely and properly discontinuously on $\Omega$, so that the quotient $M=\Omega/\Gamma$ inherits a Hessian structure. Is the tangent bundle $T(\Omega/\Gamma)$, with its canonical complex structure, a Stein manifold?

Let $n,k\ge 1$. For a Boolean function $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ and a noise rate $\delta\in[0,1/2]$, define the noise sensitivity
$$\mathrm{NS}_\delta[f] \;=\; \Pr_{x,y}[f(x)\ne f(y)],$$
where $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$ is uniformly random and $y\in\{-1,1\}^n$ is obtained from $x$ by independently flipping each coordinate with probability $\delta$.

A linear threshold function on $\{-1,1\}^n$ is a function of the form $\mathrm{sgn}(w_0+\sum_{i=1}^n w_i x_i)$ for some real numbers $w_0,w_1,\dots,w_n$. Say that $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ is the intersection of $k$ linear threshold functions if there exist linear threshold functions $g_1,\dots,g_k$ such that $f(x)=1$ iff $g_i(x)=1$ for all $i$, and $f(x)=-1$ otherwise.

Prove or disprove: there is an absolute constant $C>0$ such that for every $n,k\ge 1$, every $\delta\in[0,1/2]$, and every $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ that is the intersection of $k$ linear threshold functions,
$$\mathrm{NS}_\delta[f] \;\le\; C\sqrt{\log k}\cdot\sqrt{\delta}.$$
